| 1257 | **[mu-link/sync] The external-MIDI slave is frequency-locked only (phase error and tempo-change offsets never correct) and stamps pulses by arrival time.** Audit finding. In ExternalMidi mode [ServerEngine.h:214](mu-link/Source/Server/ServerEngine.h#L214) only copies the smoothed tempo into the clock and [TransportClock.h:41](mu-link/Source/Clock/TransportClock.h#L41) integrates beats from it, so mu-link's beat grid is never compared with the pulses. Consequences: the grid sits an arbitrary distance (up to one audio block) from the master's downbeat after every Start and keeps that offset; a tempo ramp or push-pull on the master lags through the smoothing and the accumulated offset is permanent; estimate noise random-walks the phase; and the two clocks differ by tens of ppm so it creeps. Pulses are stamped with their arrival time on the MIDI callback thread ([MidiClockInput.h:24](mu-link/Source/Clock/MidiClockInput.h#L24), `getMillisecondCounterHiRes`) rather than the driver timestamp the message carries, adding OS scheduling jitter (the unit test only holds 1.5 BPM at 0.8 ms of jitter). Fix: reuse the continuous PLL from the MidiClockSync fix: count pulses (24 per beat) for the master's position and slew the frame-clock beat toward it; use the message timestamp (verify that the Windows MIDI backend supplies a capture time); show a Locked / Drifting indicator. Re-run manual test MS1 afterwards. Not built or run. **Progress (commit 8533caa, build 1184):** mu-link's external-clock slave now counts the master's song position (MidiClockEstimator::songPulse, tick-0) and ServerEngine slews the frame-clock beat toward it each block (0.5 s time constant, step capped at 10 % of the block's beat so it stays monotone, jump if >1 beat off); simulated 0.1 % tempo-estimate bias: 0.003 beat after two minutes vs 0.24 unservoed (ServerTests). **Remaining:** stamp pulses with the driver/capture timestamp instead of arrival time (verify the Windows MIDI backend supplies one; hardware), the Locked / Drifting indicator (new UI, ux ruling), and the MS1 re-run (#1294). The commit message wrongly says "Closes #1257"; the row stays Open. **Owner (2026-10-11):** still needs a hardware MIDI-clock master and a ux-controller ruling (Locked / Drifting indicator). **UI half split out (ux ruling, [docs/mu-link/design-ui.md](docs/mu-link/design-ui.md) section 4):** the Locked / Drifting lamp, the phase-error atomic and the tolerance constant are #1504; this row keeps the driver-timestamp and hardware parts. | 🔴 Open | — |

Held up: RelaxedInt copy semantics; param apply (relaxed stores, no dirty flags, audio reads the Rhythm at the hit); a staged hot-swap carrying a different outputMode (the whole Rhythm is swapped including outputMode, and the MidiOutputEngine note-off uses its own activeNote / activeChannel stored at note-on); slot swap carries the pending off; transport stop flushes within 20 ms; one trigger per rhythm per block; velocity clamped >= 1.5/127. (b) The one real issue: a pending note-off was dropped when a slot was torn down within 20 ms of a hit (`RhythmManager::remove`, the `PresetIO.cpp` shrink in `commitStagedFullPreset`, the `PresetIO_HostState.cpp` shrink in `restoreStateFromTree`), leaving the downstream synth with a hung note. **Fixed in ec68f8c (focused build, number 1400, local/unpushed):** `MidiOutputEngine::takePending(note, channel)`; processor `orphanOffs[16]`, `numOrphanOffs` and `parkPendingMidiOff(slot)` (drops the new entry when full: worst case one stuck note after more than 16 teardowns without a processed block); callers run before each teardown; the audio thread drains right after `numRhythms` is read under the existing `ScopedTryLock`, adding a note-off at offset 0 per parked entry and then clearing, before `advanceSequencer`; a try-lock miss keeps entries parked. Test `teardownSendsNoteOff` (remove path and `setStateInformation` shrink path: each note-on matched by exactly one off, same note and channel, offset 0; not yet confirmed to fail without the fix). mu-clid-tests 153, mu-clid Debug listening all OK; `docs/mu-clid/design-ui.md` has a 'Shared note' sentence. A dsp-controller review of ec68f8c is running. (c) Minor notes, no failure constructed: note-offs stall during bypass / suspend or a try-lock miss until the next normal block (negligible); two rhythms on the same note and channel share one downstream voice, so one's 20 ms off cuts the other's note (by design, documented); MIDI notes sit at offset 0 of the block, so up to one block of jitter (same as voice triggers; sample-accurate placement is later); `addEvent` can allocate if the host's buffer is full (worst case 8 rhythms x 2 events, about 150 bytes per block vs about 2 KB reserved by wrappers; stress render with dense MIDI in); a MIDI-mode rhythm's silent voice and mixer strip still run each block (skipping needs profiling); input MIDI such as Note-mode triggers stays in `midiMessages` mixed with generated notes (pre-existing). (d) mu-Clid MIDI build check after the mapping move passed: focused Debug build 1400; mu-clid-midi-tests 78 with 0 failures; `ParameterLayoutTests` asserts 37 host-visible parameters and passes; no 'outMode' in mu-clid-midi sources; no listening pipeline for it. | 1504 | **[mu-link/sync] UI half of #1257: Locked and Drifting Clock lamp states, phase-error atomic and tolerance constant.** Per [docs/mu-link/design-ui.md](docs/mu-link/design-ui.md) section 4 (decided by Claude overnight 2026-10-11): `mu-link/Source/Clock/ClockLock.h` holds `kDriftThresholdBeats` = 1/48, `kRelockThresholdBeats` = 1/96 and `nextDriftingState(drifting, absErr)` (hysteresis). `ServerEngine.h` publishes the error and the verdict from the external-clock phase servo; `AudioServer` exposes `externalPhaseErrorBeats()` and `externalDrifting()`; `LinkShellBackend::getMidiClockState` returns Drifting (Off, Waiting, Locked unchanged; Lost takes precedence over Drifting). `TransportBar` already draws Drifting (amber, lampOn, "Drifting, re-aligning"), so no UI change. DEVIATION: the published error is a one-pole average (the servo's own gain, 0.5 s time constant, resets to the raw error on a jump) because the clock count arrives in whole pulses, so the raw error saws through about +-1/48 beat even on a perfect lock; a jump of a quarter beat or more reaches Drifting within about 10 pulses. Tests: hysteresis (exact thresholds, hold between, 12-step sequence crossing both and wobbling near each), engine test (Locked, Drifting after a six-pulse jump, Locked again, 0 and not drifting once stopped), adapter test (Locked, Drifting, Locked; Lost beats Drifting). Not checked on screen with a live clock. **Notes (mu-link clock review fixes, commit 08182e0, build 1399):** (a) after a jump `errorAverage` resets to 0 (the lamp publishes first, flashes at most once); (b) the first servoed block after Start applies a non-zero offset with one `locate(target)`, and the lamp error excludes the intended offset; (c) the 1-beat jump threshold uses the error minus the not-yet-closed offset slew (a single-block delta was not enough: a first version failed a 240 BPM +250 ms test); (d) new `clearServoState()` in the not-servoed and internal branches clears servo state, `phaseErrorBeats` and `clockDrifting`; (e) tests: steady clock Locked at 64/512/2048/4096 frames, 2-beat source jump Locked within a few blocks, +250 ms leads the beat by 0.5 two beats after Start, mid-play +250 ms at 240 BPM slews (no block advances more than 1.15x its length) ending 1.0 beat ahead. mu-link-tests 75 pass, verify-bus 3/3. Known, pre-existing: a negative offset at Start clamps to beat 0 (`TransportClock::locate`), so the lamp may briefly show Drifting. dsp-controller review pending on: new plain members `bool servoActive`, `double lastOffsetBeats`, `double offsetPendingBeats`; `clearServoState()` storing relaxed to the existing atomics; the changed jump/locate decision, nudge bookkeeping and internal-clock branch. **dsp-controller notes (PASS WITH NOTES, no Blocker or Major; on 08182e0):** offsetBeats is recomputed each block from the live tempo estimate so pending also picks up tempo jitter (small, decays); a Song Position locate while running does not clear servoActive / pending (re-closed by the 10% slew; set servoActive=false on a consumed locate for parity); the jump's locate skips pulses for BlockStats / MIDI clock out (documented deliberate); test gaps: tempo change plus offset change in the same block, Song Position locate with a non-zero offset while running. | ✅ Closed | 1389 |

| 1287 | **[mu-tant/timing] Under MIDI clock a gate edge near a pulse may close and reopen at a block edge (possible click).** The clock beat is pulse-quantised, so every block between two pulses gets the same start beat, while mu-Tant evaluates gates per sample from `blkBeatStart + i * bps`; at the next block edge its position can step back by up to a pulse, so a gate edge just before a pulse can be crossed twice. Test: a mu-Tant render under MIDI clock with 64-sample blocks that checks every gate edge for a double transition (needs the `--midi-clock` render option from #1250). The continuous beat in #1259 would remove the cause. Not built or run. **Closed (build 1184, commit 8533caa):** block-edge tests at 32/64/480 samples under a +-40-sample-jittered clock assert the beat never runs backwards and consecutive blocks are exactly contiguous (overlap <= 1e-12); plus 64-sample MIDI-clock listening tests for all four products (*_midi_clock_64). Listening suite 31/31. Not an audio-level gate-edge inspection of a mu-Tant render. | ✅ Closed | 1184 |

| 1262 | **[mu-clid/naming] Move mu-Clid into its own `mu_clid` namespace.** Found in the naming survey (2026-10-09, see [docs/design-naming.md](docs/design-naming.md)); owner asked for it to be logged. mu-Tant, mu-Toni and mu-On put every type in `mu_tant` / `mu_toni` / `mu_on`; mu-Clid has almost all of its 46 types at global scope (SequencerEngine, Rhythm, PluginProcessor, PluginEditor, PresetIO, RhythmManager, SampleLibrary, HotSwapStager, EuclideanPanel, RhythmPanel, RhythmSidebar, SettingsOverlay, VoiceSection and the rest; only LinRange is in `mu_clid`). This breaks the family rule that product code lives in the product's namespace, and it blocks combining engines in one binary: a global `PluginProcessor` / `SettingsOverlay` sits beside the other products' namespaced ones. Scope: wrap the mu-Clid sources in `mu_clid` (the JUCE `createPluginFilter` stays global), move product code out of `mu_pp` into `mu_clid`, fold `md` / `ModDest` in, and update `mu-clid-tests` (about 140 tests name these types unqualified) and `StandaloneApp`. Saved data is untouched: state identifiers, parameter ids and extensions do not change. Do on the build PC, one file group at a time with a Debug build and the unit tests between steps, and after the MIDI-sync fixes that edit the same files (SequencerEngine.cpp, PluginProcessor.cpp, MidiClockSync) so the two do not collide. **Closed (build 1190, commit "Stage C: mu-Clid moves into the mu_clid namespace"):** all mu-Clid types are in `mu_clid`; `createPluginFilter` and the StandaloneApp glue stay global; product code is out of `mu_pp` (adapters, preset/param tables and the PluginProcessor_Internal helpers now in `mu_clid`), `mu_pp_migrate` became `mu_clid::migrate`, `md` / `ModDest` are nested in `mu_clid`; tests use `using namespace mu_clid` where needed. | 1261 | **[family/transport] MIDI sync "Clock only" cannot start the sequencers, and "Transport only" never advances the beat.** Found in the MIDI / sync audit (2026-10-09) by reading the code and the diff of the family-transport change. Standalone Settings offers three Messages modes ([StandardSettingsOverlay.cpp:69](mu-core/UI/StandardSettingsOverlay.cpp#L69)). (1) **Clock only:** [MidiClockSync.h:62](mu-core/Plugin/MidiClockSync.h#L62) sets `isPlaying_` only when transport messages are on, but [TransportResolver.h:71](mu-core/Plugin/TransportResolver.h#L71) takes `playing` from `clock.isPlaying()` whenever sync is enabled, so playing stays false forever: no product plays, and the Play button stays enabled ([TransportBar.cpp:141](mu-core/UI/TransportBar.cpp#L141)) but each click is overwritten back to stopped on the next block by the resolver's mirror. This is a regression: before the resolver, mu-Clid used `clock.isPlaying() or internalPlaying` and Clock only worked. (2) **Transport only:** no pulses are counted so the clock beat stays at 0 and the sequencers never advance, and `getBpm()` returns its 120 default so the enabled BPM field has no effect (the old mu-Clid code had the same frozen beat). Fix: choose play, tempo and beat sources independently in the resolver. Play comes from the clock only if transport messages are on (else the own Play button); tempo and beat come from the clock only if clock ticks are on (else the own BPM, with the own beat advanced from the Start edge). Make the TransportBar enable states follow the same rule. Add resolver unit tests for all three modes (see the sync-coverage issue). **Done (commit 965321d; site notes in 72591b3):** the resolver picks play and tempo / beat independently; 9 resolver unit tests cover host, host with no position, all three Messages modes, own transport, Start from bar 1, a mode switch mid-play and the no-clock tempo fallback. Unverified: not run live against a MIDI clock source (no hardware here). | ✅ Closed | 1160 |
| 1260 | **[mu-clid/timing] Under MIDI clock about 60 % of 16th-note steps fire one pulse late (about 21 ms at 120 BPM).** `MidiClockSync` builds the beat by adding 1.0 / 24.0 per pulse ([MidiClockSync.h:79](mu-core/Plugin/MidiClockSync.h#L79)). 1/24 is not exact in binary, so after 6 pulses the beat is a hair below 0.25, and [SequencerEngine.cpp:205](mu-clid/Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp#L205) computes `(int)(beatPosition / StepLengthBeats)`, which floors that to the previous step; the step then waits for the next pulse to push the beat over. Measured with the same IEEE double arithmetic in PowerShell: 62 % of sixteenths floor low in the first bar after a Start, 60 % over 64 bars, worst accumulated error 3.5e-10 beats over 1000 beats. The extra lateness is one pulse interval: 27.8 ms at 90 BPM, 20.8 ms at 120, 14.4 ms at 174. mu-Toni already guards its step maths with a 1e-9 tolerance and mu-On compares against the step time, so neither is affected. Fix: add a small epsilon (1e-9) to the beat before the floor in SequencerEngine::processBlock and any other beat-to-step floor in mu-core / mu-Clid; better, count pulses as an integer and derive the beat as pulses / 24.0 so nothing accumulates. Add a unit test that feeds 4 bars of clock and checks every 16th boundary gives the right step index. **Done (commit 965321d):** MidiClockSync counts pulses as an integer and derives the beat from it; a 1e-9 epsilon guards the step floor in mu-Clid's SequencerEngine; a unit test over 4 bars of clock checks every 16th boundary and passes. Unverified: not run against a live MIDI clock source. | ✅ Closed | 1160 |
| 1259 | **[family/transport] The MIDI-clock slave beat is a pulse-count staircase, a block behind, and one pulse off at Start.** Audit finding. [MidiClockSync.h:52](mu-core/Plugin/MidiClockSync.h#L52) returns the pulse count at the START of the block, so (a) a pulse that arrives inside block N only moves the beat for block N+1 and steps fire up to a block late, jittering with the pulse phase; (b) blocks with no pulse all report the same start beat (a 256-frame block at 120 BPM sees one value for about 4 blocks), so the position moves in 1/24-beat jumps: mu-Tant gates and mu-Toni modulators sample a staircase, and mu-On / mu-Toni fire on the block after the pulse rather than on its sample; (c) on Start, `0xFA` sets the beat to 0 and playing, but the beat returned for that same block is the stale pre-Start value, so the Start block plays from the old position; and by MIDI convention the first `0xF8` after Start IS tick 0 (the slave starts on the next clock), whereas the code counts it as 1/24, which puts the whole grid one pulse (about 21 ms at 120 BPM) ahead of a hardware master. Check (c) against a real hardware master. Fix: give MidiClockSync a continuous, monotonic beat: record the sample position and beat of the last pulse, extrapolate to each block start (and any sample) at the estimated tempo, and slew a phase correction toward the pulse-count beat when a pulse lands (a PLL with a phase term, not just a frequency estimate); treat the first clock after Start as tick 0; return the corrected Start-block beat; expose the pulse sample offsets so sequencers can fire a step on the pulse's own sample. The BPM clamp mismatch (estimator 20 to 400, MidiClockSync 20 to 300, internal 20 to 300) can be unified in the same change. Not built or run. **Status (2026-10-10):** not started unattended: it rewrites the clock timing that only a hardware master can confirm. The per-block ground-truth MidiClockSync test from #1250 is in place to guard it. **Tick-0 part (merged in from #1286, owner 2026-10-10):** by the MIDI spec the first `0xF8` after Start is song position 0, but [MidiClockSync.h](mu-core/Plugin/MidiClockSync.h) gives pulse n the beat n / 24, so step k fires one pulse (about 21 ms at 120 BPM) before the master plays it. Pre-existing. Measure against a hardware master or a MIDI loopback first (the round-trip test #1292 is expected to show it); if confirmed, start the pulse count at -1 on Start and clamp the beat at 0. **Closed (build 1184, commit 8533caa):** MidiClockSync beat is continuous (integer song index + PLL; each phase error slewed in over the next pulse period so the beat never steps or runs backwards; block start read forward from earlier clocks; blockEnd beat exported and the resolver hands sequencers the exact span so consecutive blocks are contiguous; Start-block reports the Start position; first clock after Start/Continue/SPP is that position = tick 0, matching mu-link's FA F8 output; tempo fed in every Messages mode; extra clamp removed; tempo reset on enable; a jump is capped at 2x the nominal span; members lose trailing underscores; mu-On's sequencer takes the exact span via processSpan). Simulated-master results: steady 0.00001 beat, +-40-sample jitter 0.001. Not done from the row: exposing pulse sample offsets (not needed: the continuous beat places steps within the block). Tick-0 is spec/loopback-consistent but NOT confirmed against a hardware master; that stays with #1294 (MS1). | ✅ Closed | 1184 |
| 1258 | **[family/midi] No Song Position Pointer in, and no Start / Stop / Continue / Song Position out.** Audit finding (whole tree searched). Input: [MidiClockSync.h:58](mu-core/Plugin/MidiClockSync.h#L58) skips every message that is not one byte, so `0xF2` is ignored, and [MidiClockInput.h:21](mu-link/Source/Clock/MidiClockInput.h#L21) never looks for it. A DAW or drum machine that is relocated and then sent Continue leaves the apps resuming from wherever they stopped: permanently out of phase by whole bars, with no way back except Stop and Start from the top. Output: mu-link sends only `0xF8` ([MidiClockOut.h:30](mu-link/Source/Clock/MidiClockOut.h#L30)), never `0xFA` / `0xFB` / `0xFC`, so outboard gear that waits for Start never starts from mu-link's Play button, and when mu-link stops the pulses just cease with no Stop message. Fix: handle SPP (one unit = 6 clocks = a sixteenth; set the beat, then Continue) in MidiClockSync and the mu-link estimator; in mu-link emit Start on rewind-and-play, Continue on resume, Stop on stop, and SPP before Continue after a locate, with the first `0xF8` following Start. Not built or run. **Done (commit 6cdeabc, build 1169; site notes 9e6c1b5):** Song Position Pointer in: mu-core MidiClockSync handles it while stopped in Transport and Both modes (the resolver moves the own beat in Transport mode), and the mu-link estimator through `consumeLocate` / `TransportClock::locate`. Out from mu-link: Start plus the beat-0 pulse from the top or on a rewind while playing; Stop; resuming elsewhere snaps the clock to the sixteenth and sends SPP + Continue + that pulse, so clients and slaves restart together; a new MIDI-out port or device mid-play gets SPP + Continue; the later of locate and Start wins. Unverified with outboard gear. | ✅ Closed | 1169 |
| 1255 | **[mu-link/midi] An app attached to mu-link receives no MIDI and sends none.** Audit finding. While attached, [MuLinkBridge.h:131](mu-core/Link/MuLinkBridge.h#L131) detaches the app from the local AudioProcessorPlayer and the producer thread processes a freshly cleared `scratchMidi` ([MuLinkBridge.h:58](mu-core/Link/MuLinkBridge.h#L58)) holding only an injected program change; the processor's MIDI output is discarded ([MuLinkBridge.h:163](mu-core/Link/MuLinkBridge.h#L163)). So with mu-link running, a MIDI keyboard no longer plays mu-Toni or mu-Tant, mu-Clid's note mode and MIDI-out mode (which drives outboard synths) do nothing, and the app ignores its own MIDI clock input (by design, mu-link owns the clock). The incoming events sit unread in the player's MidiMessageCollector. Fix: drain that collector into the producer's MIDI buffer, and route the processor's MIDI output to a chosen output port (mu-link's or the app's own). Heard-latency caveat: until the latency issue is fixed, MIDI played through the bus is heard about a ring later. Not built or run. **Progress (commit 6cdeabc, build 1169):** MIDI in done: while attached, the bridge registers its own MidiMessageCollector on the app's device manager and feeds the bus render. MIDI-in latency is about 170 ms while attached (depends on #1256, or a smaller ring target for MIDI clients). **Still open, MIDI out (deferred):** the bus renders about one ring (about 170 ms at 48 kHz) ahead, so sending at render time would lead the audio. Needs a timed sender in mu-core (lift MidiClockOut's timestamped FIFO and sender into a shared TimedMidiOut; placement is an architecture-steward decision) and the render lead passed from MuLinkClient; also skip the echo when `!producesMidi()`, strip realtime bytes, and open the port by identifier so it works when the app has no audio device open. **Owner approval (2026-10-10):** build the shared timed MIDI sender in mu-core (lift MidiClockOut's timestamped FIFO and sender thread); placement is ruled by architecture-steward. **Closed (build 1177, commit a064fe3):** MIDI out while attached via the new header-only `mu_core::TimedMidiOut` (architecture-steward ruling, [docs/design-plugin-family.md](docs/design-plugin-family.md) "Device MIDI output"; mu-link's MidiClockOut now wraps it). The bridge owns the MIDI-out port while attached (frees the device manager's handle, opens its own, follows Settings, hands it back on detach with all-notes-off); events are due at now + render lead + sample position; only apps whose `producesMidi()` is true; no system bytes; the scene program change is filtered. Limits: an output of "none" is not honoured while attached; MIDI-in latency is about one ring until #1256. Manuals updated (mu-Clid, mu-link, mu-Tant). | ✅ Closed | 1177 |
| 1254 | **[mu-link/clock-out] MIDI clock out is bunched at the top of each audio block, sent from the audio thread, through a raw pointer swapped by the UI.** Audit finding. [AudioServer.h:121](mu-link/Source/Server/AudioServer.h#L121) calls `emit()` once per callback, which sends every pulse of the block back to back with `sendMessageNow` ([MidiClockOut.h:30](mu-link/Source/Clock/MidiClockOut.h#L30); the header notes sample placement is a later refinement). Pulses are only as steady as the audio block: at 120 BPM a 480-frame WASAPI block jitters each pulse by up to 10 ms (half a pulse), and a 2048-frame block sends two pulses in a burst then 40 ms of nothing, which a slave that measures pulse spacing reads as a swinging tempo. `sendMessageNow` can also block or allocate on some Windows MIDI backends. And [MuLinkComponent.cpp:453](mu-link/Source/UI/MuLinkComponent.cpp#L453) writes the plain `MidiOutput*` from a UI timer while the audio thread reads it: if the user changes the output in Options, AudioDeviceManager deletes the old port and the next callback can call into freed memory (a crash mid-set). Fix: queue pulses with sample-accurate timestamps (their position inside the block) and send them with `MidiOutput::startBackgroundThread` and `sendBlockOfMessages` so JUCE schedules them; hand the port over through an atomic and clear it before the manager closes it. Not built or run. **Done (commit 6cdeabc, build 1169; site notes 9e6c1b5):** clock out is now sample-accurate. ServerEngine reports per-pulse frame offsets; the audio thread queues timestamped bytes in a lock-free FIFO (no allocation, no MIDI syscall); a sender thread (realtime priority, falling back to highest priority, for example on Linux without rtprio) sends each one when due (1 ms wake); the queue is skipped while there is no port; the block is stamped at callback entry. The port is handed over in `audioDeviceStopped` / `audioDeviceAboutToStart` (JUCE swaps the default MIDI out only with callbacks stopped), so the UI no longer re-sets a raw pointer every tick; a re-prepare keeps tempo and position. UI play / tempo / rewind are now atomics applied once per block, which also fixed a UI / audio data race on TransportClock. Tests in mu-link ServerTests. Unverified: real jitter on a hardware slave (needs a MIDI loopback). | ✅ Closed | 1169 |
| 1253 | **[family/sync] No sync offset, nudge or tap tempo, and tempo is whole-number only.** Audit finding. | 1252 | **[family/transport] A lost MIDI clock leaves the app-side slave "playing" on a frozen beat.** Audit finding. mu-link has a stall watchdog ([ServerEngine.h:206](mu-link/Source/Server/ServerEngine.h#L206)) but the shared [MidiClockSync.h](mu-core/Plugin/MidiClockSync.h) the standalones use has none: if the cable is pulled or the master stops sending `0xF8` without a `0xFC`, `isPlaying_` stays true and the beat and tempo freeze. Re-encoding the embedded sample as FLAC (already built into JUCE 8, lossless) would typically cut it 40-60 % with no quality change. Opus was considered (JUCE 9.0.3) and rejected: it is lossy and a drum sampler should return the user's sample intact. Needs: write FLAC on embed, read either on load so existing presets still work, and a listening-test round trip proving the decoded sample is bit-identical. **Closed (commit 057c7d4, build 1170):** integer PCM WAV / AIFF embedded samples (up to 24-bit, up to 8 channels) are re-encoded as FLAC, with properties `sampleDataCodec` / `sampleDataBits` beside `sampleData`, and decoded back into their original file type and name on load. Float, 32-bit or compressed sources, and files FLAC would not shrink, stay raw; older presets load unchanged; an unknown codec is refused. Code in [mu-clid/Source/Persistence/EmbeddedSample.h](mu-clid/Source/Persistence/EmbeddedSample.h); EmbeddedSampleTests prove 16-bit and 24-bit round trips sample-identical. Measured 58.9 % / 39.3 % smaller on a synthetic drum sample, not measured on real user samples. Cue / loop chunks are not kept on the FLAC path (mu-Clid reads audio only). A FLAC-embedded preset will not play its sample in a build older than 1170 (covered by the #1237 note that new-format files won't open in earlier builds). | ✅ Closed | 1170 |

| 1232 | **[Audit]** MED — MidiClockSync's tempo average reads the wrong ring slots for the first 24 clock ticks after every Start. All four processBlocks (and mu-Clid Lite) use it; their own copies are gone. mu-Tant's gates and mu-Toni's arp now follow a host position; mu-Clid no longer runs on its own Play button while a DAW is stopped; with MIDI clock on, the clock's Stop stops every product. mu-Toni's arp steps now sit on the beat grid (step k at beat k × step length, fired on its exact sample, numbered by the beat so a loop / locate replays the same notes; gate note-offs sample-accurate too); MIDI-trigger mode still restarts per key press. New render `--host-start-beat` (a simulated playing host) + TONI_host_lock listening test; new mu-toni-tests ArpRunnerTests (grid-exact onsets, jump re-sync, trigger restart). All 23 listening tests + unit suites pass. Not yet tried in a real DAW. | ✅ Closed | 1145 |

| 1170 | **[mu-toni/arp] Per-step velocity / accent.** Split from #1073 item (4). Needs a design decision first — the arp has no step grid (it scans a note pool), so "per-step" could mean: a repeating accent pattern (accent every N steps, or a short on/off pattern) with an Accent amount; velocity from the held MIDI note driving level (and / or filter); or a per-step velocity lane like a modulator.  **Owner decision 2026-10-08: an accent pattern.** Per layer, a repeating on/off accent pattern (1–16 steps) that advances with the arp's own steps, plus an Accent amount: an accented step plays louder and opens the filter a little (303-style). No played-velocity input and no separate velocity lane (Amp Level is already a modulation target). Pattern + amount persist with the layer (layer preset / full preset / session). **Done:** per-layer params `v{N}_acc` (Accent 0–100 %), `accLen` (1–16 steps), `accPat` (bit i = step i+1; default step 1 of 4, Accent 0 so existing sounds are unchanged); ArpAccent picks each step's accent from the pattern (Loop mode: position from the beat, so accents lock to the bar; MIDI trigger: from the key press); ToniVoice::setAccent lifts the note up to +6 dB and its filter up to one octave, smoothed over 5 ms for tied notes. Accent amount is a modulation target (`arp.accent`, appended row). UI: Accent + Acc Steps knobs and the accent row (the shared StepEditor as two-level cells, layer colour, playhead) in the Appergater box. Persists through the composed slot state with no extra code. New mu-toni-tests cases (pattern maths; accented step louder; Accent 0 changes nothing). Toggling a cell and the playhead checked on screen. | ✅ Closed | 1148 |
| 1169 | **[mu-clid/modulation] Pan (and the sends) missing from the destination dropdown.** Owner report (2026-10-07): Pan doesn't show as a mod destination. Cause: mu-Clid's dropdown lists targets in a hand-written display order (makeModDestProvider kOrder) that #1167 / #1168 didn't extend, so the four new rows (amp.pan, send.effect / .delay / .reverb) never appear. **Done:** The display order moved into ModulationDestinations.h as ModDest::kDropdownOrder (the provider builds from it) with Pan (45) under Amp and the three sends (46–48) under a new Effects heading after the insert slots. New ApvtsLayout test: every live kTable row must appear in kDropdownOrder, so a target can't be added without showing up. | ✅ Closed | 1067 |

| 1168 | **[mu-clid/modulation] FX sends as modulation targets.** Owner request (2026-10-07): make the voice's Effect / Delay / Reverb send knobs (in the Effects box) modulation targets — one row each in mu-Clid's ModTarget table, depth = % of the knob's range, applied per rhythm by the audio engine via the ModulationMatrix. **Done:** Rows send.effect / send.delay / send.reverb (section Effects, params sendEff / sendDly / sendRev — the mixer channel's ch{N}_ params) appended to ModDest::kTable. mu-core MixerEngine::ChannelState gained per-block modulation overrides (panMod, sendEffectMod, sendDelayMod, sendReverbMod; NaN = unmodulated, ChannelState::effective picks), used by the mixer's pan and send stages; reset / copy / channel swap carry them. mu-Clid's applyRhythmModulation seeds the sends (and pan) from the mixer channel as knob proportions, writes the modulated values to the overrides each block, clears them when the rhythm has no modulation, and snapshots them (kSnapSendEff / Dly / Rev) for the knobs' live arcs. ModTarget.h documents mixer-strip targets; the ApvtsLayout target test accepts them (ModDest::isMixerStripParam). Also pre-seeded the missing "filter.lowCut" key in modParamValues (it was inserted on first use on the audio thread). | ✅ Closed | 1066 |

| 1167 | **[mu-clid/ui] Pan knob in the Amp box, modulatable.** Owner request (2026-10-07, screenshot of the Amp box — asked as "mu-tant", but the Amp box with Level + Accent is mu-Clid's; mu-Tant has no Amp section): add a Pan knob in the empty top-right of the Amp box, replicating the mixer strip's pan (same parameter, so the two stay in step), and make it a modulation target. **Done:** AmpSubsection gained a Pan knob (KnobWithLabel "Pan", knobPan colour, −1..+1, no value text — as on the mixer strip) in the Amp box's top-right cell, bound to the same ch{N}_pan parameter (writes it, loads it, follows mixer changes via RhythmPanel's ch-param listener), status bar shows C / L n / R n. Modulation target amp.pan (section Amp) with the same mixer override path as the sends (#1168) and a live arc (kSnapPan). design-voice.md documents pan + sends. Screenshot-checked. | ✅ Closed | 1066 |

| 1165 | **[family/ui] Status bar info in every app.** Owner report (2026-10-07): mu-Tant doesn't show the status bar info (control name + value) at the bottom; all apps should. **Cause found:** the shared EditorShellBase owns the StatusBar in every app, but each product must forward its controls' onStatusUpdate to getStatusBar().showParam. mu-Clid forwards the master loop + RhythmPanel (and Lite its panels); mu-Tant forwards only the master loop — VoicePanel's knobs / dropdowns / X-Mod / filter / insert / mixer, the GatingDesigner and the modulators never reach it; mu-Toni forwards only its EnginePanel; mu-On forwards nothing (GroovePanel engine grid, Swing / Accent, modulators). Fix: wire every panel's status callback to the status bar in each editor, matching mu-Clid (ideally once in the shared shell / panels so a new app gets it for free), then check hovering / turning each control updates the bar in all four apps. **Done:** New shared EditorShellBase::forwardKnobStatus(panel): walks the panel and routes every KnobWithLabel, InsertSubsection and ParamKnobGrid that has no status handler of its own to the status bar (name + value on hover and while turned). ParamKnobGrid gained onStatusUpdate (its plain sliders / combos report label + value text on hover or change). mu-Tant (VoicePanel), mu-Toni (EnginePanel) and mu-On (GroovePanel, incl. the engine grid and Swing / Accent) call it once in their editors; mu-Clid already routed its own. Checked live: mu-Tant Cutoff and mu-On Pitch show on the status bar. | ✅ Closed | 1063 |

Check panel sizing and display objects so nothing clashes with or overlaps a screw or a neighbour. **Done:** Screws on in every app (setScrews(true) after setMetalStyle). New MuLookAndFeel::drawSections (raised boxes: shadows, faces, corner screws, name plate centred in the kSectionPlateH band above) and kSectionPlateH. mu-Tant VoicePanel: mu-Clid structure — preset strip (header inset kScrewedPanelInset, strip screws), one voice panel (Root / Scale + OSC 1 / OSC 2 / NOISE / X-MOD / FILTER / EFFECTS / MIXER boxes, titles moved from inside the panels to plates above), gate panel, modulator panel; content clear of box screws (kSubPanelScrewClear), filter knobs no longer run to the box edge. mu-Toni EnginePanel: preset strip, source panel (OSCILLATOR 1 / 2 / MIX boxes), voice panel (PITCH / FILTER / AMP / EFFECTS boxes — at full mu-Clid widths the band overran the screw insets, so Amp closes its sends up to 4 columns (its row-1 gap column) and Effects takes the rest), a compact APPERGATER panel (was mostly empty), modulators take the spare height; voice-band dropdowns kept kDropdownEdgeGap off the box edges. mu-On GroovePanel: preset strip, engine panel (one box holding the lane's controls in one row — was a mostly empty panel), steps panel (GROOVE box with Swing / Accent, now the shared KnobWithLabel, + the lane's STEPS box; Rumble's envelope in a box the same size), modulators; EnginePanel / GrooveGrid plates now drawn by the host as section plates. Shared: ParamKnobGrid selectors take two cells (Bass "Wave" read "Si…" in LCD lettering), kLabelH / kCellH exposed; ModulatorEditor (metal) gives a tall panel's spare height to the display — the one-row assignment box stops at kMetalAssignMaxH (mu-Clid unchanged); isMetal takes a const component. design-ui-family §11 documents the sections helper and the panel structure. Screenshot-checked every app (mu-On Kick / Bass / Rumble lanes) with zoomed corners: no content over a screw or a neighbour. | ✅ Closed | 1056 |

| 1162 | **[mu-core/ui] Store the new metal / screw UI design centrally.** Owner request (2026-10-07): the screwed metal UI built up on mu-Clid (app paint colours, per-voice colours, raised sub-panels, panel / sub-panel / strip screws and their clearances, LCD sample bar, lamp-style modulation display, logic symbols, add buttons, evenly spread sidebar) is the new family UI design. Make sure every style choice (colours, sizes, strengths, clearances) lives in MuLookAndFeel / MuTheme::Lighting rather than in product code, and that the design is documented so the other apps can adopt it. **Done:** Audit of every file touched in the UI round: the remaining hard-coded style values moved into mu-core — MuLookAndFeel kScrewedPanelInset / kScrewedChannelGap (content clear of panel screws; replaces the `2 + kPanelScrewClear [- kChannelInset]` sums in mu-Clid's RhythmPanel / EuclideanPanel / VoiceSection), kSidebarFlatEdge / kSidebarMetalEdge / kSidebarMetalTop / kSidebarScrewedEdgeX / kSidebarScrewedItemX, lamp display kLampCellGap / kLampCellCorner / kLampCurveGlowW / kLampCurveW, LCD text kLcdTextH / kLcdNameTextH / kLcdTextPadX / kLcdBrowseW; MuTheme::Lighting lcdOwnLift / lcdAccentLift / lampHotSpotReach. | 1157 | **[mu-clid/samples] New rhythms show "Missing: 01 Kick.wav — click to find".** Owner report (2026-10-07): every rhythm added with + Rhythm shows the missing-sample warning. Find out why. **Done:** Cause found — content data, not code: the user's Rhythms/_default.muRhythm (saved 2026-05-24) references r0_sample="01 Kick.wav", which is not in the Samples folder (it holds "Kick 01.wav" … from 2024). + Rhythm loads _default.muRhythm into the new slot, so every new rhythm carries that dangling reference and the sample bar correctly reports it missing. No code writes "01 Kick.wav". A scan of the user content found 9 other presets with sample references that no longer resolve (absolute paths to old sample libraries / temp embed files, DT_kick_06.wav, …). Fix is a content edit (re-point _default.muRhythm at an existing sample, or re-save the default rhythm) — left to the owner. | ✅ Closed | 1046 |

| 1156 | **[mu-clid/rhythm] New rhythms are named "_default".** Seen in the owner's #1154 screenshot: + Rhythm creates the slot as "<unnamed>", then applyDefaultRhythm loads _default.muRhythm through the preset path, which takes the file's presetName ("_default") as the rhythm's name. Loading the default rhythm is a settings reset, not an identity change — it already keeps the slot's colour (stopped path only). Fix: name new rhythms "Rhythm N"; the default-rhythm load keeps the slot's name and colour on both the stopped and the playing (staged) path. **Done:** PluginEditor names new rhythms "Rhythm N" (startup slot "Rhythm 1"); applyDefaultRhythm loads with keepIdentity, which stageRhythmPreset and applyRhythmPreset honour by leaving the slot's name + colour alone — on the playing (staged) path too, where the colour previously wasn't restored. Screenshot-checked: Rhythm 2 … Rhythm 8. | ✅ Closed | 1043 |

| 1155 | **[family/ui] Add buttons look like buttons; + Target centred, not full width.** Owner feedback (2026-10-07): the sidebar's "+ Rhythm" (dashed outline) should look like a button, and so should the modulator's "+ Target", which also shouldn't span the full width — a normal-width button, centred. **Done:** AddButton is now a juce::TextButton: metal style draws it with the family button look (like New / Save, hover + press), flat style keeps the dashed border; disabled dims (alpha). Callers unchanged (onClick). Metal: + Target (ModulatorEditor) and + Assignment (ModMatrixPanel, same pattern) are kAddButtonW 110 px wide, centred; flat keeps the full-width strip. Sidebar + Rhythm keeps the sidebar width. | ✅ Closed | 1043 |

One itemBounds(i) helper feeds the layout, the add animation, the drag drop-line and the drop index. Screenshot-checked with 8 rhythms (all apps share the sidebar). | ✅ Closed | 1043 |

Right end unchanged (1065 px). | ✅ Closed | 1039 |

| 1150 | **[mu-clid/ui] Screw clearance, round 2.** Owner feedback on #1149 (2026-10-07): (1) the voice panel's bottom-right screw overlaps the Effects sub-panel's corner — shrink the sub-panel a bit; (2) the modulator A–H / Matrix tab buttons slightly smaller so they don't sit so close to the screws; (3) the left sidebar's content (rhythm boxes, + Rhythm) smaller, clear of the screws; (4) the Euclid logic (OR), Filter type and Insert effect dropdowns slightly smaller, leaving a space between them and the edge of their panel. **Done:** (1) Effects sub-panel 9 px narrower (kEffectsW 315): the three send knobs sit in 51 px columns (kSendColW) so the box ends short of the voice panel's bottom-right screw. Screenshot-checked each area. | ✅ Closed | 1036 |

| 1149 | **[mu-clid/ui] Screws: content clear of sub-panel screws; panel screws further in.** Owner feedback on #1148 (2026-10-07): in the modulator's control strip the content covers the sub-panel screws (Stepped dropdown on the left, the expand button on the right) — the content can be slightly smaller to clear them. | 1148 | **[mu-clid/ui] Cross-head screws on panels; voice band in sub-panels.** Owner spec (2026-10-07), mu-Clid first (the other apps follow later): small cross-head (Phillips) screw graphics in the corners of every panel; the Pitch / Filter / Amp / Effects areas of the voice band become raised sub-panels; smaller screws in the corners of the sub-panels. | 1147 | **[family/ui] App colours: painted metal + per-voice highlights.** Owner spec (2026-10-07): each app has one primary colour — mu-Clid purple, mu-Tant green, mu-Toni blue, mu-On yellow. The main graphics are metal with the primary colour looking painted on: dull, dark, washed out (not the current bright neon outlines and wash). Each voice (rhythm / voice / layer / track) has its own colour, which highlights its icon in the left sidebar plus the voice's patch selector and name display in the header bar at the top. Plan: (1) mu-core derives a painted tone from the app accent (desaturated + darkened) and drawAccentPanel / drawRaisedSubPanel / the sidebar frame draw with it; (2) every app passes its primary to setMetalStyle (closes #1144); (3) the voice palette leaves out the four app hues' near-duplicates where they would clash, and ChannelHeaderBar lights the preset LCD + name display in the voice colour; (4) screenshot all four apps before / after. **Done:** Built and screenshot-checked on all four apps. mu-core: app primaries as tokens (appPurple / appGreen / appBlue / appYellow, MuTheme::AppPrimaries); paintColour() + Lighting paintSaturation / paintBrightness / paintCoat / paintEdgeLift drive drawAccentPanel (coat, glow, painted edge) and the raised sub-panel outline (panelTint retired); setAppAccent also points the theme's active-segment colours, the button on-colour and the global accent at the app colour, so tabs / segments / toggles / the mixer follow it. New 8-colour voice palette without the four app hues (Red, Cyan, Orange, Magenta, Lime, Rose, Silver, Copper); mu-On lanes remapped (Kick red, Bass orange, Hat cyan, Snare magenta, Rumble lime). ChannelHeaderBar: name shown on an LCD backlit in the voice colour and the preset selector lit in it (DropdownSelect::setLcdColour, "muLcd" label property); every header-bar panel now in the app paint. Sidebar icons in the voice colour (mu-Clid mini ring single-colour mode, mu-Tant glyph stronger). mu-Tant filter-routing button + upgrade banner off the family purple. Knob function colours unchanged. docs/design-ui-family.md §8 + §11 updated. | ✅ Closed | 1029 |

| 1146 | **[mu-clid/presets] Rhythm preset save mangled some names.** RhythmPanel cleaned the file name with replaceCharacters(9 unsafe chars, "_") — JUCE requires both strings to be the same length, so every rhythm save tripped an assertion in Debug and, in Release, a name containing one of : \| * ? < > " was cut short or read past the end of the string. It also used withFileExtension, which cut a dotted name ("Kick 1.5" → "Kick 1.muRhythm"). **Done:** RhythmPanel now uses mu_pp::safePresetFileName (fallback "Rhythm") and appends .muRhythm; the save dialog's default name uses the same helper. No other mismatched replaceCharacters calls remain in the family. New unit test covers the helper (unsafe chars, dotted names, empty → fallback). | ✅ Closed | 1025 |

| 1145 | **[mu-clid/modulation] Pad / Insert Length depth against the knob's current maximum?** Pre / Post Pad and Insert Length modulation depth is measured against the full 0–63 range, but what plays is limited to the knob's current maximum (clampLayout), so with few steps most of the depth range does nothing. Proposal: measure against the current maximum, with a preset re-upgrade. **Owner decision (2026-10-07): measure against the current maximum.** Plan: Pre / Post Pad and Insert Length become proportions of the knob's current range, like Hits / Rotate / Insert Start already are — the range the knob shows (Pre max = min(63, Steps−1 − Post − InsLen), Post likewise, InsLen max = min(8, Steps−1 − Pre − Post), from the unmodulated layout); one HitGenerator helper gives those maxima to the UI ranges, the processor seed / write-back / arc snapshot and the preset upgrade. Preset upgrade: mu-Clid modulator data gains a padDepthUnits="knobMax" marker; unmarked data has its pad / insert-length depths rescaled by fullRange / currentMax (clamped to ±100%) using the rhythm's loaded layout, so an old preset still moves the same number of steps. **Done:** Built as planned. HitGenerator::padKnobMaxima() is the one formula for the knob ranges (EuclideanPanel::updateRanges), the processor's seed / write-back / arc snapshot, and the preset upgrade; the fixed-range kPad / kInsertLength scaling is gone from the modulation path. Preset upgrade: mu-Clid's serialiseModulators writes padDepthUnits="knobMax"; on load, unmarked data (after the existing 12/63 pre-standard step) has pad / insert-length depths rescaled by fullRange / currentMax from the rhythm's loaded layout, clamped to ±100% (all four load paths set the Euclid values before reading modulators). Known approximation: an old depth that overshot the knob now reaches the end of the knob slightly later in the source's swing. Tests: padKnobMaxima cases (normal, over-budget, no budget); upgrade from pre-standard, full-range and current data. | ✅ Closed | 1026 |

| 1144 | **[mu-toni, mu-on/ui] App accent colours.** mu-Toni and mu-On use mu-Clid's purple as their metal-style accent (setMetalStyle(true) with no colour). Waiting on the owner to choose each app's colour; then one line per app. **Done:** Resolved by #1147: mu-Toni blue, mu-On yellow (owner's choice). | ✅ Closed | 1029 |

| 1143 | **[family/hot-swap] Unify hot-swap staging and give it to mu-Toni / mu-On.** mu-Clid (HotSwapStager) and mu-Tant (VoiceHotSwapStager) each have their own; mu-Toni and mu-On apply preset / program-change loads immediately, not at the loop end. Needs a design pass first: the loop-boundary rules differ (rhythm loops vs gate patterns vs arp / step grid). **Design pass (2026-10-07):** both stagers share one core — per-slot pending payloads plus one full-preset slot, the same isReady / boundaryReached store-release / load-acquire handshake, and "a full preset supersedes per-slot swaps". They differ only in the payload (mu-Clid pre-builds Rhythm + VoiceEngine + sample path off the audio thread; mu-Tant stores a ValueTree and pre-loads wavetables) and the boundary rule (mu-Clid: master-loop wrap / per-rhythm wrap mask; mu-Tant: each voice's gate-pattern length via the shared hotswap::swapBoundaryReached). Proposal: a mu-core template `mu_hotswap::Stager<Payload, N>` that owns the slots + flags (stage / cancel / flagIfReady / take); the boundary test and the apply stay product-side, so no product's rules change. **Owner to decide before building:** the swap point for mu-On (proposed: the 16-step pattern wrap = every bar) and mu-Toni (proposed: every bar, or the master loop when one is set — the arp has no natural loop), and whether stopping should still apply immediately (both current stagers do). **Owner go-ahead (2026-10-07):** proposals accepted. **Done:** new mu-core Plugin/HotSwap.h — mu_hotswap::Stager<SlotPayload, FullPayload, N> (per-slot payloads + one full preset, stage / stageFull / cancel on the message thread, flagIfReady / flagFullIfReady on the audio thread, isFlagged / consume / consumeFull to commit; a full preset drops pending per-slot swaps) plus the shared loopWrapped / boundaryReached predicates and kBarBeats. mu-Clid HotSwapStager and mu-Tant VoiceHotSwapStager now sit on it with their APIs and boundary rules unchanged (mu-Clid still commits every flagged rhythm under one suspendProcessing via consume). mu-Toni and mu-On gain hot-swap: a full / layer / track preset (UI or MIDI program change) loaded while the transport runs (host, MIDI clock or internal — the audio thread's play state) is staged and applied at the next bar line (mu-On: the 16-step pattern wrap; mu-Toni: every bar — it has no master loop), or at once when playback stops; loaded while stopped it applies at once. Commits run in commitDeferredWork, refresh the editor via onLayerPresetLoaded / onTrackPresetLoaded / onPresetSwapCommitted, and show the transport bar's SWP badge (full) and the header's SWP pill (layer / track); reset cancels a staged swap. design-plugin-family.md hot-swap section rewritten for the shared stager. All tests pass (mu-Tant's stager tests now exercise the template); mu-On launch-and-play checked — staged loads in mu-Toni / mu-On not yet exercised live. | ✅ Closed | 1059 |

| 1142 | **[family/ui] Shared voice band sections (Pitch / Filter / Amp).** mu-Clid has them as components (VoiceSection), mu-Toni rebuilds the layout by hand in EnginePanel, mu-Tant has its own. Share them like InsertSubsection, with a per-product parameter-name mapping (the three products name their params differently). Larger job. **Findings (2026-10-07):** only mu-Clid and mu-Toni share the Pitch / Filter / Amp band; mu-Tant's voice panel is a different structure (two oscillators + X-Mod, the mu-Tant-only dual filter, PEnv / FEnv depth knobs) and should stay product-side. mu-Clid and mu-Toni also lay the band out differently: mu-Clid uses its own widths (Pitch 4 columns with Depth above R; Amp Level / Accent over A/D/S/R; sends beside a narrowed insert dropdown), while mu-Toni uses the shared kVoice* widths (A/D/S/R/Depth in one row, sends in the Amp row). **Owner to decide:** should mu-Toni adopt mu-Clid's band layout (then a shared mu-core VoiceBand with a per-product param-suffix map is a straight lift of mu-Clid's three subsections), or should each keep its layout (then little is gained by sharing beyond what KnobWithLabel already gives)? **Owner go-ahead (2026-10-07):** mu-Toni adopts mu-Clid's band (per the earlier instruction that the voice band = mu-Clid's VoiceSection). **Done:** new mu-core UI/Voice/VoiceBand — mu-Clid's band geometry (kPitchW / kFilterW / kAmpW / kEffectsW / kSendsX / kLeftGap …), layout of four product-supplied sections + the three FX sends right-aligned in the Effects box, and the drawing (metal: drawSections boxes + plates; flat: dividers + plates); VoiceBandSection builds a section from controls a product already owns (two Size-2 rows, place(control, row, col, span, dropdown)). mu-Clid VoiceSection now subclasses VoiceBand (its subsections and their rhythm binding unchanged; screenshot identical). mu-Toni EnginePanel uses VoiceBand: Pitch = target dropdown + Depth above R over A/D/S/R; Filter unchanged; Amp = Level over A/D/S/R; Eff / Dly / Rev sends now in the Effects box beside a narrowed insert dropdown — the same layout as mu-Clid; its hand-built band code removed. mu-Tant stays product-side (different structure). Docs updated. | ✅ Closed | 1059 |

| 1141 | **[family/editor] Lift repeated editor set-up into EditorShellBase.** Each editor repeats: mixer overlay status forwarding to the StatusBar, the shared credits list (JUCE / Signalsmith / clap-juce-extensions …) for the About panel, and similar boilerplate. Move the common parts into the shell; apps supply only what differs. **Done:** EditorShellBase::setProductIdentity(name, extraCredits) sets the About panel (shared family credits + product extras), the transport logo and, for licensed products, the activation panel name; setMixerOverlay forwards a MixerOverlay's status messages to the StatusBar. All four editors use it (mu-Clid keeps its Björklund credit as an extra). Side fix: mu-Tant's About panel now credits Monocypher, which its licence check uses. | ✅ Closed | 1024 |

| 1140 | **[mu-on/link] Connect mu-On to mu-link.** mu-On's StandaloneApp passes an empty mu-link name `{}`; the other three pass their names, so mu-On can't follow mu-link's clock or show on its mixer. | 1134 | **[family/processor] Program-change plumbing into ProcessorBase.** All four processors repeat the same code: inherit juce::AsyncUpdater, call scanMidiProgramChanges in processBlock → triggerAsyncUpdate, drain in handleAsyncUpdate, cancelPendingUpdate in the destructor. Move it into ProcessorBase (one call from processBlock, or done in processCoreBlock), keeping mu-Clid's and mu-Tant's handleAsyncUpdate hot-swap commits working. **Done:** ProcessorBase now inherits juce::AsyncUpdater (protected) with a final handleAsyncUpdate that runs the new commitDeferredWork() hook (mu-Clid / mu-Tant hot-swap commits) and then drains program changes; products call queueMidiProgramChanges(midi) once per block. | 1133 | **[mu-on/presets] Full presets, per-track presets and MIDI program change.** mu-On's preset Save / New / browser did nothing (no savePreset/loadPreset), the per-lane preset bar had only Reset wired, and its program-change handlers were empty. Add: full `.muOn` presets (APVTS state + step grid + lane modulators + Rumble envelope, wrapped with name / description / category, via the shared mu-core preset-file helpers); per-track `.muTrack` presets (the lane's engine params, its step row, its modulators, and the Rumble envelope for Rumble) — a track preset belongs to one instrument, so each lane's list shows only presets for that lane; the header bar's preset list + Save wired, the delete button hidden (fixed lanes); MIDI program change (Ch 1-5 → track presets, Ch 9 → full presets) via the shared queue + the Program Change settings section; editor refresh after a load. Also: per-track helpers on StepPattern (serialiseTrack / deserialiseTrack); a track preset of another instrument is refused with a message; the lane preset menu keeps showing the loaded preset. Verified: track preset saved from Kick (params + step row + modulators) and loaded back on screen (an added step cleared); new PresetTests in mu-on-tests (helpers + track-row round-trip) pass. | ✅ Closed | 1022 |

| 1132 | **[mu-toni/presets] Full presets, per-layer presets and MIDI program change.** mu-Toni's preset Save / New / browser did nothing, it had no per-layer preset bar, and its program-change handlers were empty. Add: full `.muToni` presets (APVTS state + per-layer modulators, wrapped with name / description / category, via the shared helpers); the shared ChannelHeaderBar at the top of the engine panel (layer name, reset, preset list, Save; delete hidden — fixed layers) with per-layer `.muArp` presets (the layer's `v{N}_` params + its modulators, loadable into any layer); a per-layer reset; MIDI program change (Ch 1-4 → layer presets, Ch 9 → full presets) + the Program Change settings section; editor refresh after a load. | 1131 | **[family/presets] Shared preset-file helpers + Program Change settings section.** Preset file handling was written per product. StandardSettingsOverlay gains addProgramChangeSection(layer-table name, full-table name) + onMidiPresetsClicked / onFullPresetsClicked, replacing mu-Clid's and mu-Tant's own copies. Verified: all four apps build; mu-Tant settings page unchanged; all tests pass (mu-Clid 147, mu-Tant 134, mu-Toni 10, mu-On 19). | ✅ Closed | 1022 |
| 1130 | **[family/modulation] Shared destination-dropdown builder.** New mu-core UI/ModTargetDropdown.h: mu_mod::populateDropdown fills a destination dropdown from a ModTarget table (id = row + 1, heading whenever the section changes, reserved rows skipped) with options: active insert effect (insert.p1..p4 shown only when an effect is active, labelled with its slot names under its name, unused slots hidden — shared family behaviour), an extra filter, and a display order. mu-Toni and mu-On use it plain; mu-Tant adds its stepped-only filter; mu-Clid passes its display order (Euclid A/B/C, Pitch, Filter, Amp, Insert) and its stepped-only octave. Each product's hand-written loop removed. Verified: all tests pass; mu-Clid's list order checked on screen. | ✅ Closed | 1019 |
| 1129 | **[family/license] Licensing and activation in ProcessorBase.** ProcessorBase now owns the licence state (licensingEnabled, offlineLicensed), isLicensed() (unlicensed products always licensed; Release licensed = offline .lic OR online activation; Debug unlocked), LicensingConfig + initLicensing and an onActivated() hook (called off the message thread after a successful online activation). initLicensing is defined in the new mu-core License/ProductLicensing.h, included only by licensed products, since only they compile the verifier. mu-Clid and mu-Tant call initLicensing({ product id, .lic, public key, activation file }) and drop their copies (licenseInfo, isLicensed, activation lambda, kActivationFilename); mu-Clid keeps a Lite-only isLicensed() = true and uses onActivated to lift its 16-step cap. Debug-verified; the Release-only branch of isLicensed is not compiled until a Release build. | ✅ Closed | 1018 |
| 1128 | **[family/persistence] One shared save/restore of per-voice modulators in the host state.** mu-core ModulatorSerialise.h gains writeChannelData (state <VoiceData><Voice idx> per channel with its <Modulators>, plus an optional per-channel extras callback), findChannelNode and readChannelModulators (clears, restores, optional per-channel target check). mu-Tant uses it with its extras (wavetable paths, gate patterns); mu-On and mu-Toni use it plain. Older sessions still load: mu-On converts its old <Lane> nodes and mu-Toni its old <MuToniMods> container to the standard shape before reading (the product-specific names stay out of mu-core). | ✅ Closed | 1017 |
| 1127 | **[family/audio] One shared scale table.** New mu-core Audio/MusicalScales.h (mu_audio: Scale, kScales, clampScaleIndex, scaleSemitone, toneToMidi, snapToScale, midiToFreq). mu-Tant's and mu-Toni's Audio/Scales.h are now thin using-declaration headers over it (mu-Tant keeps its own kBaseOctave), so none of their includers changed. | ✅ Closed | 1017 |
| 1126 | **[family/ui] Shared standard settings page.** New mu-core UI/StandardSettingsOverlay (on SettingsOverlayBase): General (Audio master volume, Display UI size + the reopen-for-fonts hint, Transport BPM optional) and MIDI (standalone MIDI Clock); products add sections at named places (Where::General / MidiBeforeClock / MidiAfterClock / Group) and the page stacks them with the standard headings and gaps. mu-On uses it as-is (its SettingsOverlay.cpp deleted, header is an alias); mu-Toni adds Tony's line; mu-Tant adds Hot-swap, Note Mode, Program Change; mu-Clid (no Transport) adds Output, Hot-swap, MIDI Mode, Program Change and the Locations group. Side effects: mu-Tant, mu-Toni and mu-On now also show the UI-size font hint; the MIDI Clock rows use mu-Clid's row gap. Verified by screenshot (mu-Clid, mu-Toni). | ✅ Closed | 1017 |
| 1125 | **[family/plugin] App settings, preferences and FX listeners in ProcessorBase.** ProcessorBase now owns the settings file (initAppSettings(appName): <OS app data>/TDP/<app>.xml, restores UI size + MIDI-clock prefs), the MidiClockSync and its getters / saving setters, setUiScale saving, getContentDir (Documents/TDP/<app> or the user's "contentDir"), and isFxParamId / registerFxListeners / unregisterFxListeners / syncAllFxParams. All four products call initAppSettings("muX") and drop their copies (settings block, restore lines, setUiScale / setMidiSync* / getContentDir overrides, appSettings + midiClockSync members; mu-Tant / mu-Toni / mu-On also their FX listener code). mu-Clid keeps its own parameter-listener routing. ~350 lines removed. | ✅ Closed | 1017 |
| 1124 | **[family/modulation] Standard enforced: check script, docs, CLAUDE.md rule.** Step 3. New tests/scripts/check-mod-targets.py fails if any code reintroduces per-target depth scales, a product defines its own target-row struct, or a product has no mu_mod::ModTarget table (PASS on all four). "Modulation targets — family standard" section in docs/design-plugin-family.md (rule, per-product tables, how it works, the depthUnits preset marker, enforcement); CLAUDE.md critical rule added. | ✅ Closed | 1015 |

ModDest::kTable rows are now mu_mod::ModTarget (section + per-rhythm param columns; reserved slots param nullptr); registerDepthScales removed. Every target is seeded / written back as a proportion of its knob range (sustain, resonance, filter-env depth, pitch-env depth, amp level, accent, pads, insert length newly so; pitch octave / semitones as range-proportional offsets), with the linear ranges in mod_skew (ModulationSkew.h) and the APVTS layout now built from the same constants (static_asserts pin pads / insLen to HitGenerator). Tests: table rows name real per-rhythm params; old-preset pad modulation moves the same steps; marked data untouched. | ✅ Closed | 1015 |
| 1122 | **[mu-core/modulation] Standard modulation targets: depth = % of the knob's range.** Step 1. New mu-core Modulation/ModTarget.h (mu_mod::ModTarget {id, label, section, param}, findTarget / isValidTarget) and ModTargetChecks.h (missingParams, depthNotProportional). ModulationMatrix: depth-scale registry, registerDepthScale, the 100 fallback and the unused log-Hz path removed — amount = source% x depth% / 10000 for every target. mu-Tant (parameter mapping merged into kModDestTable, registration removed), mu-Toni (param column replaces the kModDestVpSlot array) and mu-On (ModDestEntry = ModTarget via makeTarget) moved onto the shared row with no change in sound. Checks wired into mu-Tant (params + depth) and mu-On (depth) tests; mu-Toni's test target does not compile the modulation engine, so its guard is the jassert in vpSlotFor. Stepped rounding stays with each product (smooth pitch glide needs unrounded values). | ✅ Closed | 1015 |
| 1121 | **[mu-tant/modulation] X-Mod Index modulated far more than its depth suggests.** Owner: depth 3.2% on X-Mod Index swung the parameter hard. Cause: mu-Tant seeds every destination into the matrix as a 0-1 proportion, so each needs depth scale 1.0, but registerDepthScales listed only the osc / level ids; xmod.index, xmod.depth and xmod.ssb fell back to mu-core's 0-100 default of 100, making them 100x too strong (3.2% acted as 320% of the range and slammed the rails). Fix: registerDepthScales now registers scale 1.0 for every non-".prop" id in kModDestTable (shared filter.* keep mu-core's scales), so a new destination cannot be missed. New mu-Tant test: depth 3.2% on each X-Mod destination moves it exactly 3.2% of its range. mu-Toni (registers from its table) and mu-On (".prop") were unaffected. Note: existing presets with X-Mod modulation will now sound much gentler. | ✅ Closed | 1013 |

| 1108 | **[mu-link/tests] mu-link-tests can fail when a mu-family standalone is running.** Seen 2026-10-05 at v1.1.0.991: one run failed 24 of 35 while a mu-Clid standalone had just started; an immediate rerun (mu-Clid still running) passed 35 / 35. The tests use the same named shared-memory registry as the real bus, and a running product's MuLinkBridge polls to attach every 500 ms, so the two can collide. Fix: give the test process its own registry name (e.g. a test-only name suffix / injected name) so it can never meet a live app's bus. **Fixed:** `MuLinkProtocol` builds every map name through `transportMapName()` / `registryMapName()` / `ringMapName()`, which append `mapNameSuffix()` — empty in the products and mu-link, so their names are unchanged. The test runner sets a random private suffix at start-up and exports it in `MU_LINK_TEST_MAP_SUFFIX`, which the `--shm-child` re-launch inherits and reads, so parent and child share one private bus that no live app can see. Verified: mu-link-tests pass 35 / 35 three runs in a row with a mu-Clid standalone running; products unchanged (empty suffix). | ✅ Closed | 994 |

| 1095 | **[mu-clid] Pre Pad / Post Pad still capped at 12.** Owner: they appear limited to a maximum of 12. Since #1093 the shared Steps − 1 budget is the real limit, but the APVTS ranges (and four other hard-coded 12s) still capped each pad at 12. Raise `HitGenerator::kMaxPrePad` / `kMaxPostPad` to 63 (the largest budget, 64 steps − 1) and use the constants everywhere the 12 was restated: RhythmParamTable's load/automation clamp, the modulation-override clamp in PluginProcessor, and the mod-indicator snapshot. The snapshot normalised pads/insLen against a fixed 0–12 / 0–8, which has been wrong since #1093 made the knob ranges dynamic — it now stores the actual modulated value and the knobs bind in actual mode, so the ring maps onto each knob's current range. Modulation depth scale for the pads deliberately stays 12 (full depth = ±12 steps) so existing presets' pad modulation doesn't become 5× stronger. Insert Length keeps its 8 maximum. Note: host automation of these two params is stored normalised, so existing automation lanes will rescale. The RhythmParamBoundary test that asserted the old 12 cap now checks 20 passes and 99 clamps to 63. Steps' APVTS max also reads `HitGenerator::kMaxSteps`. | ✅ Closed | 977 |

| 1094 | **[mu-clid/ui] Insert Start shows the real (1-based) step the insert begins on, so its minimum is Pre Pad + 1.** Owner: with Pre Pad = x, Insert Start should be at least x + 1. After #1093 the knob still showed the stored value, which in Pad-mode pre-pad counts from the end of the gap (so 0 = first step after it) and in Mute mode counts from step 0 — neither reads as a step number. The knob now displays the absolute step, counted from 1: shown = stored + (Pre Pad in Pad mode ? Pre Pad : 0) + 1, giving a minimum of Pre Pad + 1 in both modes. Display only (slider textFromValue / valueFromText, so the centred value, status bar and typed entry all agree) — the stored value, presets and modulation are unchanged. The knob repaints when Pre Pad or its mode changes, since its number depends on them. Verified in the running app: Insert Start shows 1 with Pre Pad 0. | ✅ Closed | 976 |

| 1093 | **[mu-clid/sequencer + ui] Pad / insert controls aren't limited by the step count or by each other.** Owner: Pre Pad, Post Pad and Insert Length can all be set past the number of steps, and Insert Start can land inside the Pre Pad gap. Today the knobs run to their fixed APVTS maxima (12 / 12 / 8) whatever Steps is, and only Insert Start tracks Steps. Agreed rules (owner chose both): **(1) combined budget** — Pre Pad + Post Pad + Insert Length ≤ Steps − 1, so at least one step always stays for the Euclid pattern; **(2) the insert sits between the pads** — never inside the Pre Pad gap, never running into the Post Pad gap, in both Pad and Mute modes. Insert Start keeps its stored meaning (in Pad-mode pre-pad it already counts from the end of the gap; in Mute mode it's absolute), so the bounds are lo = (pre Mute ? pre : 0), hi = Steps − post − len − (pre Pad ? pre : 0). **Engine:** one `HitGenerator::clampLayout` applied by all three pattern paths (audio-thread getPattern, allocating getPattern — now delegating — and getStepTypes for the ring), so modulation and presets can't exceed the limits either; clamp order pre → post → insert length. **UI:** each ring's knob ranges recomputed from the generator whenever Steps, a pad knob, Insert Length or the Pre Pad mode changes, and before values are loaded (fixes a load-order clamp). APVTS maxima named as HitGenerator constants. Any stored value the layout pulls in is written back to APVTS (computed from the rhythm, not the knobs), so the parameter, the knob and the sound agree. 4 new HitGenerator tests (budget order, over-budget pattern, Mute/Pad insert bounds). | ✅ Closed | 975 |

| 1092 | **[build/versioning] Move the family to version 1.1.x — and make major.minor a single source.** Owner: the UI rework (neumorphic knobs, slide switches, re-laid-out Euclid panel) is a big change, so version 1.1.xxx. The build number keeps counting (next = 972 → 1.1.0.972; tags v1.1.0.NNN, commits v1.1.NNN) — the Release ≤ Debug guard and the in-plugin update check both rely on it being monotonic. Today "1.0" is hard-coded in ~12 places (root CMakeLists project + PLUGIN_VERSION, IncrementBuildNumber's rc regen, AboutPanel, EditorShellBase update banner, both Inno .iss, BuildInstaller(.Lite).cmake, PackageRelease.cmake, release.yml tag, mu_build_artifacts.ps1 hook, mu-link's app version). New root `version.txt` ("1.1") is read by all of them; BuildNumber.h gains `MU_VERSION_STRING` ("1.1.0.N"). The update banner now shows the release's own tag for the available version instead of rebuilding it with the local prefix. Docs/process (CLAUDE.md commit format, /build + /release skills, memory) updated to v1.1. Also found and fixed while verifying: mu-Toni, mu-On and mu-link had always shown **1.0.0** in Windows file properties — JUCE's generated .rc can't take a four-part x.y.0.N version and falls back — so they now get their own `versioninfo.rc.in` (as mu-Clid/mu-Tant already had), regenerated each build by the increment target (RC4–RC6); mu-link's app target also gets `VERSION`. Verified: every Debug exe/VST3 reports 1.1.0.974. (CLAP binaries carry no Windows version resource at all — clap-juce-extensions builds them without one; hosts read the version from the plugin, so left as is.) | ✅ Closed | 974 |

| 1091 | **[mu-core/link] Linux release build fails: non-Windows `MuLinkBridge` stub has no `setPresetName`.** release.yml run 37019629708 (v1.0.0.971): windows-latest passed, ubuntu-latest failed compiling every product's Standalone — `StandaloneShell.h:134: 'class mu_link::MuLinkBridge' has no member named 'setPresetName'` — so `publish` was skipped and no GitHub release was created. #1065 added `setPresetName` to the Windows bridge and StandaloneShell calls it unconditionally, but the `#else // _WIN32` no-op stub (same public shape, so products compile off Windows) never got it; Windows-only local builds couldn't catch it. Fix: add a no-op `setPresetName` to the stub. The change is inside the non-Windows branch, so Windows binaries are byte-identical — kept at 971 (no Debug bump) so the release stays one number; Linux verifies it in the re-run. Verified: re-run 37025047992 passed on ubuntu-latest + windows-latest and published v1.0.0.971. | ✅ Closed | 971 |

| 1082 | **[tooling/backlog] Standardised the backlog's resolved status on `✅ Closed` and added a structural checker.** An audit of `backlog.md` found four classes of drift that the prose rules in CLAUDE.md had never caught: (1) **two of the three tables had no delimiter row** — only Open carried `\|---\|---\|---\|`, so On Hold and Closed did not render as tables on GitHub at all, and an **orphan delimiter** stranded between #1044 and #1043 made GFM treat #1044's row as a spurious table header; (2) **two ordering violations** — #1063/#1064 transposed, and #1053/#1052 stranded eight rows above their descending position; (3) **five spellings of the resolved status** (`✅ Fixed` ×1022, `✅ Design resolved` ×4, `✅ Audited`, `✅ Verified`, `✅ Closed`) against a key that declared one; (4) **8 rows with an unescaped `\|`** inside the description (from shell snippets like `` `… \| tee log` ``), which split them into extra cells and pushed Status/Closed Build out of place — backticks do **not** protect pipes in GitHub tables, only `\|` does. All four fixed: delimiters repaired, rows reordered, **1029 status cells normalised to `✅ Closed`**, section heading → `## ✅ Closed`, column header → `Closed Build`, and the 8 rows escaped. Terminology propagated to [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) (grouping rule + a new "single resolved status" rule), [.github/workflows/sync-backlog.yml](.github/workflows/sync-backlog.yml) and [.claude/commands/deepaudit.md](.claude/commands/deepaudit.md). **Also fixed a real defect in the CI writer:** sync-backlog.yml instructed the workflow to *"Append a new row to the bottom of the Open table"*, contradicting the descending-order rule — every GitHub-issue import was corrupting the ordering; now inserts at the top. **New guard:** [tests/scripts/check-backlog.ps1](tests/scripts/check-backlog.ps1) (PowerShell, per owner preference) enforces all six invariants — sections present/ordered, header+delimiter per table, descending order, no duplicate numbers, status matching its section, exactly 4 cells — with `check-core-boundary.py`'s exit-code convention (0 clean / 1 violation / 2 setup error). Verified against three seeded-fault copies (duplicate+transposed number, deleted delimiter, stray `✅ Fixed`); all caught. Backlog now passes: 1032 rows, 0 violations. Not yet wired into `ci.yml` — run it manually after editing the backlog. | ✅ Closed | — |

| 1081 | **[mu-tant/audio] Owner reports mu-Tant is "very quiet".** Not reproduced by measurement (logged from a review-only machine — no build/render possible). **Leading cause: the #1042 factory-preset rework, which is a level change by construction.** Two compounding effects: (a) the generator's per-voice `level` is authored at roughly **−8 to −10 dB** across the drone/pad bank ([mu-tant/tools/gen_factory_presets.py:401-410](mu-tant/tools/gen_factory_presets.py#L401)), below the parameter's own **−6.0 dB default** ([:94](mu-tant/tools/gen_factory_presets.py#L94)); (b) #1042 removed `gate_bypass=1` from every shipped voice ("bypass is a design-time aid only") and gave each one a real gate pattern, many of them deliberately **sparse with big gaps** for call-and-response layering. Before #1042 a bypassed gate meant a continuously-open, full-level drone; now the same patch is amplitude-gated to a duty cycle well under 100%, so **RMS/perceived loudness drops even though peak level is similar**. Net: mu-Tant should be expected to sound materially quieter post-#1042 than the owner remembers, by design rather than by defect. Also verify it isn't the Note-mode gate ([PluginProcessor.cpp:1123](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L1123)) — that gates the whole mix to silence when `midiNoteMode == 1` with no notes held, but it produces silence, not quietness, so it fits the report poorly. **Owner decision needed:** raise the authored `level` band (regenerate the pack), reduce gate sparseness, or accept the new dynamics as intended. Next step: A/B render a pre-#1042 and post-#1042 factory voice through the listening-test pipeline and compare RMS. **Owner, 2026-10-06: not an issue — closed, no change.** | ✅ Closed | 1019 |

| 1080 | **[mu-link/connection] mu-Clid + mu-Tant no longer auto-connect to mu-link (owner-reported regression; both used to).** The product-side wiring is intact — verified `muLinkName` is passed correctly by every product ("mu-Clid" / "mu-Tant" / "mu-Toni"; mu-on empty by design) into `App::Config { displayName, muLinkName }` ([StandaloneShell.h:83](mu-core/Plugin/StandaloneShell.h#L83)), and the bridge is created whenever that name is non-empty ([:124](mu-core/Plugin/StandaloneShell.h#L124)). **Leading cause: a protocol-version skew between an updated product and a stale installed mu-link.** #1065 (d049bcc) bumped `kProtocolVersion` **2→3** ([MuLinkProtocol.h:23](mu-core/Link/MuLinkProtocol.h#L23)) to add `ClientSlot::presetName`. The client guard refuses any mismatch — `open()` compares the registry's version and, on a mismatch, drops the mapping and returns false ([MuLinkSharedMemory.h:115-120](mu-core/Link/MuLinkSharedMemory.h#L115)) — so a v3 mu-Clid/mu-Tant attaching to a v2 mu-link **silently** falls back to its own device: `attachToMuLink()` just returns and re-polls every 500 ms with no error, no log, and no UI indication ([MuLinkBridge.h:119](mu-core/Link/MuLinkBridge.h#L119)). Skew is easy to hit because **mu-link ships on a different track from the products**: [release.yml:57-61](.github/workflows/release.yml#L57) builds mu-clid/-lite/-tant/-on/-toni but **not mu-link**, so a GitHub release never carries it; mu-link reaches testers only via [cmake/DeployMuLink.cmake](cmake/DeployMuLink.cmake), a POST_BUILD that runs **on Release builds only**. Update the products without a matching mu-link Release build and every client stops attaching. **Second candidate:** mu-link running with no audio device — the bridge also bails when `transport().sampleRate == 0` ([MuLinkBridge.h:123](mu-core/Link/MuLinkBridge.h#L123)), and the server only publishes a transport from inside its audio callback ([ServerEngine.h:222](mu-link/Source/Server/ServerEngine.h#L222)), so if mu-link can't open its device (e.g. a product's standalone holds it exclusively) clients never attach — equally silent. **Diagnostics:** confirm the running mu-link.exe was built at/after v1.0.937, and check whether mu-link's own mixer shows any client slots. **Fix regardless of cause: make the failure visible** — surface "mu-link found but incompatible (protocol vN vs vM)" and "mu-link has no audio device" in the status bar or window title instead of silently retrying, and consider adding mu-link to the release so the versions can't drift. **Owner, 2026-10-06: not an issue — closed, no change.** | ✅ Closed | 1019 |
