| 1072 | **[mu-toni/build] Implement the mu-toni MVP — arpeggiator mono synth.** Staged build of the finalised design (#1071); plan in [docs/mu-toni/design-buildplan.md](docs/mu-toni/design-buildplan.md). **✅ MVP COMPLETE — built v1.0.943, mu-toni-tests 0/10, family Standalone+VST3+CLAP all link.** All five stages done: T1 arp engine (`Scales.h`/`Chords.h`/`Arpeggiator.h` + tests), T2 voice (`AnalogueOsc.h` PolyBLEP + `ToniVoice.h` — 2 osc + noise + `MultiModeFilter` + Amp/Filter/Pitch `juce::ADSR` + portamento + legato + osc test), T3 plugin (`PluginProcessor` 43-param/voice APVTS + `ArpVoiceRunner.h` arp-clock→voice + MIDI note-in root/trigger + `processCoreBlock` render hook + default patch), T4 UI (`EnginePanel` rebindable arp/osc/filter/env panel via shared widgets + APVTS attachments), T5 (`.muArp`/`.muToni` extensions, **freeware** = no licence wired by default, mu-link bridge one-liner in `StandaloneApp` + host/mu-link transport sync, settings easter-egg "Its an appagator, is it a powerful tool?"). **Modulation section — DONE v1.0.945 (identical layout to the other products):** added per-voice `VoiceSlot` (8 control sequences + `ModulationMatrix`), the shared mu-core `ModulatorPanel` as the engine panel's bottom band (rebinds per layer + playhead-driven), `Source/Modulation/MuToniModDest.h` (20 arp/voice/env destinations + provider + depth-scale registration), engine resolves each voice's matrix per block via `mu_mod::resolveLane` (proportion space), and modulators persist in the APVTS state (`MuToniMods` child). Runs without crash; mu-toni-tests 0/10; family Standalone+VST3+CLAP all link. **Remaining follow-ups:** analogue PolyBLEP osc instead of mu-tant wavetable (bank not cross-product-shareable yet); no X-Mod; `.muToni`/`.muArp` preset-browser chrome not wired (DAW state save works); UI is a functional grid pending a design-ui-family polish pass. See [docs/mu-toni/design-buildplan.md](docs/mu-toni/design-buildplan.md). **--- original T1 note ---** the pure, unit-tested **arp engine** — `Audio/Scales.h` (scale table + `midiToFreq`, copied from mu-tant into `mu_toni::`), `Audio/Chords.h` (the ~35-chord library, absolute intervals), `Sequencer/Arpeggiator.{h,cpp}` (pool derivation: scale·chord·bipolar-inversion·octaves-span·diatonic-snap → sorted semitone pool; **skewed-triangle scan** deterministic — +100 up-arp / −100 down / 0 up-down / interior-skip between; step→MIDI). `Tests/ArpeggiatorTests.cpp` covers the anchor cases + determinism, wired into `mu-toni-tests`. **T2:** voice engine (wavetable oscs + X-Mod + `MultiModeFilter` + Amp/Filter/Pitch `juce::ADSR` + portamento + Legato + `InsertProcessor`). **T3:** PluginProcessor APVTS + `VoiceSlot` + `processCoreBlock` render hook + MIDI note-in + default patch + `MuToniModDest.h`. **T4:** UI (arp/env/osc/filter/insert panel replacing blank `EnginePanel` + sidebar + settings easter-egg). **T5:** presets (`.muArp`/`.muToni`), **freeware** (compile out licence/activation), mu-link bridge, polish. **Also delivered post-#945:** the Insert effect (per-voice `InsertProcessor` post-VCA + shared `InsertSubsection`), Filter Low Cut + Amp FX sends + Noise type + Pitch-env osc target, and the **voice section relaid to mu-clid's `VoiceSection` geometry** (fixed `MuLookAndFeel` constants, Size-2 knobs, compact 2-row Pitch/Filter/Amp/Insert). Built v1.0.950. | ✅ Closed | 950 |

| 1071 | **[mu-toni/design] Author the mu-toni product design docs — generative arpeggiator sequencer.** mu-toni MVP reuses mu-tant's synth engine (2 wavetable oscs + 2-lane X-Mod + scale-quantised pitch + mu-core filter + insert), the mu-core modulation section, and the standard mu mixer **unchanged** — the only novel surface is the **sequencer**. New concept: a **generative arpeggiator** where each step's note is a *pure function* of the current parameter set — user picks a **Scale** + a **Chord** in that scale, and the sequencer arpeggiates the chord. Controls so far: Scale dropdown, Root note (C…B) + **Root octave (0–8)**, Chord dropdown (**APVTS, DAW-automatable**), **Chord Inversion** (rotate voicing — lowest tones up an octave, applied before octave stacking), Octaves span (1–4), Direction (−100..+100, semantics TBD), Trigger mode (Loop / MIDI-triggered), more to add. **MIDI:** PC→preset settings identical to mu-tant, **plus** played-note input — root selectable by MIDI note by **full pitch (note + octave)** (**latest note-on wins**, held-note fallback stack); free-run (Loop) vs note-triggered mode where **note-on loops until release** — mu-toni's one departure from mu-tant's PC-only/no-played-notes stance. **mu-link support required** (standalone-only, shared `MuLinkBridge.h` one-liner hook; arp Loop/Rate slaved to the mu-link master clock when attached; identity "mu-Toni"). **Chord model = absolute named chord types** (7-tier library, common→exotic, ~35 chords Major…maj7♯11) rather than scale-degrees — Scale keeps roots in key. **Output is monophonic** (arpeggio, NOT a chord player — the chord only selects the note pool). **Chord/Root sequencing MVP = Route A via the mu-core modulator** — Chord + Root note/octave are scalar mod destinations, so a step control-sequence on `arp.chord`/`arp.rootNote` *is* a progression with zero new machinery (family "everything is modulation"). The bespoke bar-aligned **chord/root timeline (Route B)** — reusing mu-tant's `GatingDesigner` grid to place bundled chord+note events shared across voices — is **deferred to phase 2** (only earns its complexity for real bar-aligned progressions). **Portamento (glide):** a per-step pitch **slew** with a **time knob** + an **On/Off toggle that is a modulation target** (`arp.portaOn`) → step-mod enables glide per note for **303-style slides**; slew on the arp's pitch-output stage; stateful smoothing on top of the pure-function target note. **Resolved this session:** (1) **Direction** = ±100 is 100% down/up, 0 = equal, linear between (`P(up)=(Dir+100)/200`), a biased random walk. (2) **Engine = note-triggered mono synth (integration B)** — each arp step is a note-on retriggering **Amp + Filter ADSR** reused from mu-core (`juce::ADSR`+`VoiceParams`, as mu-clid), + Filter Env **Depth**; so μ-Toni = mu-tant timbre + mu-clid envelopes + arp. (3) **Mono only, strum ruled out.** (4) **Chord/root sequenced via the modulator — final, no dedicated timeline.** Docs now carry a **mu-core reuse map** (UI widgets: `BipolarSliderRow` for Direction/Filter-Env-Depth, `DropdownSelect`, `SegmentControl`, `KnobWithLabel`, `VoiceSlot`/`ModulationMatrix`; DSP all reused) + a **design-standards alignment** checklist (APVTS / no-alloc / ModulationMatrix-single-reader / shared widgets / colour tokens / full-words — all ✓). Only genuinely new: the arp math, note-on/off+gate wiring, portamento slew, and **played-MIDI-note input** (first family member to consume played notes). **Rate** is a core arp control = **tempo-synced note values** (1/4…1/32 + dotted/triplet), locked to the shared/mu-link transport, and a mod destination (`arp.rate`). Remaining owner questions are minor (chord-library trim, diatonic-snap, inversion polarity, Direction-walk random-vs-ratio, voice count 1 vs 1–8). Because the note is computed per-step from the live parameters, **every arp parameter is a mu-core modulation destination** — each step re-evaluates "what note would this be under the current (possibly modulated) settings". Deliverables: `docs/mu-toni/design.md` (product overview + shared-engine inheritance map) and `docs/mu-toni/design-sequencer.md` (the arp model). Docs-only, no code. **GRILLING PASS — DESIGN FINALISED (supersedes the tentative notes above where they differ):** (a) **Direction = deterministic skewed-triangle SCAN** (NOT random) — `fUp=(Dir+100)/200`; +100 up-arp, −100 down-arp, 0 up-down; the shorter sweep **skips notes evenly** to keep uniform Rate timing; **identical every loop**; pattern length emerges from the pool traversal (so no separate repeat-length control); boundaries wrap. (b) **Articulation reworked** — **Legato is a synth-voice on/off param** (modulatable); a note **ties (no amp retrigger) only when Gate Length = 100% AND Legato on**, and **glide is heard only on those tied notes**; **Gate Length** (1–100% of step) is the modulatable control that drives per-step slides; **the separate Portamento On/Off flag is REMOVED**; glide time is **analogue ms**. (c) **Envelopes = Amp + Filter + Pitch ADSR** (Pitch depth 0 default, all mu-core `VoiceParams`). (d) **Inversion = bipolar ±n** (negative = drop voicings). (e) **All ~35 chords ship**, grouped by tier dividers. (f) **Diatonic-snap toggle**, off by default, modulatable. (g) **Rate = straight + dotted + triplet** note values. (h) **Voices = 1–8 slots, default 1**, each an independent mono arp (own timbre/arp/envelopes/chord-root). (i) **Default patch = Loop mode, sounds on play** (Cm, 2 oct, 1/16, up). (j) **Per-slot preset noun = `.muArp`**, full `.muToni`. (k) **CONFIRMED: every voice runs the standard shared mu-core `InsertProcessor`** (per-voice insert + full algo set, via shared `InsertSubsection`, post-VCA). (l) **mu-toni is FREEWARE** — no purchase/licence/activation/demo; the mu-core License subsystem (`LicenseManager`/`ActivationStore`/`OnlineActivation`/`LemonSqueezyClient`) + `ActivationPanel` UI + `Source/License/LicenseKey.h` + the `-DMU_*_DEMO` gate are all **unused**; About panel shows no licence status. First freeware family member. Mod destinations now include `arp.gateLen`/`arp.legato`/`arp.portaTime`/`arp.diatonicSnap` + Amp/Filter/Pitch ADSR (dropped `arp.portaOn`). (m) **Settings-screen easter-egg + name origin:** the name "μ-Toni" is from **Tony**; his in-joke line goes on the SettingsOverlay **verbatim** as an italic credit line — exact text `Its an appagator, is it a powerful tool?` (keep the mis-spelled "appagator" — it's the joke; do NOT correct it), styled `labelText`/`mutedText` alongside the shared Contact Support chrome. Remaining = fine-tuning only (ms/range values, MIDI-in omni-vs-channel, velocity/accent). Docs updated: design.md + design-sequencer.md. | ✅ Closed | 950 |

| 1070 | **[mu-link/audio→fixed] Audio through mu-link sounded a bit distorted.** The master safety soft-clip ([ServerEngine.h](mu-link/Source/Server/ServerEngine.h) `masterSoftClip`) ran unconditionally with its knee at **0.8 (≈ −1.9 dBFS)**, so even a single moderately-hot instrument (a mu-tant drone / mu-clid transient peaking above −1.9 dBFS) got tanh-shaped → subtle added harmonics that weren't there on the instrument's own device. Raised the knee to **0.9** so single-source / normal-level playback passes through bit-exact, while the tanh still asymptotes to ±1.0 so the summed bus can never hard-clip the device. Summing several hot clients still engages the clip by design (pull faders down; a look-ahead limiter is a possible future upgrade). Build 939, mu-link tests 35/35. **Owner: confirm the distortion is gone in a real session.** | ✅ Closed | 939 |

| 1052 | **[Audit→fixed]** — every modulation-bindable `KnobWithLabel` polls the entire assignment list each 30 Hz tick to refresh its "is-modulated" indicator. | 1020 | **[mu-tant/bug] Filter envelope (gate-editor FILT layer) barely moved the cutoff — over-aggressive slew.** Owner-reported: a drawn filter envelope "doesn't appear to be triggering". Root cause in [applyFilterEnvelope](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp): the filter cutoff is a **per-block** value, but the de-click rise limit `maxRise` was a **per-sample** rate (`1/(kMinAttackMs·sr)`, kMinAttackMs=10) applied **once per block** — so the rising edge was limited ~blockSize× too slowly (≈5 s to fully open at 512/48k). A per-bar decay envelope resets to its peak each bar and never climbed back, so the cutoff stayed near base → no audible sweep. The per-sample gate (`applyGateBlock`) was unaffected. **Fixed:** scaled `maxRise` by the block length (`numSamples`), so the rising edge completes in ~kMinAttackMs (one block, ~10 ms — the intended click guard) and the envelope tracks its drawn shape. `applyFilterEnvelope` now takes `numSamples`. Build 903, mu-tant tests 130/130. | ✅ Closed | 903 |

Each scene cell targets a client slot; trigger sends every enabled+connected client its PC. mu-link + tests build green (35/35). **Needs the owner's end-to-end play-test** (run mu-link + a rebuilt standalone, set a scene, click recall). | 1014 | **[mu-core/mu-clid/mu-link] Garbled characters in UI text — unwrapped non-ASCII string literals.** Root cause: `juce::String::String(const char*)` decodes with **`CharPointer_ASCII`** (JUCE `juce_String.cpp:308`), so a raw UTF-8 literal (e.g. em-dash `—`) is read as Latin-1 and garbles (the reported "MIDI Program Change □□ Full Presets"). `/utf-8` fixes the *bytes* but JUCE still mis-decodes — literals must be wrapped in `fromUTF8`/`CharPointer_UTF8` (the demo banner, About credits, `charToString` sidechain dash, `VoicePanel` "Load .wav…" already are, so they render fine — the font has the glyphs). **Fixed** the user-facing offenders by wrapping/`charToString`: [MidiFullPresetsPanel.cpp:169](mu-core/UI/MidiFullPresetsPanel.cpp#L169) (the reported Ch-9 header — shared, so fixes mu-clid + mu-tant), [RhythmPanel.cpp:708](mu-clid/Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp#L708) (missing-sample indicator), [PresetIO.cpp ×4](mu-clid/Source/Plugin/PresetIO.cpp) (sample-missing error messages), [MuLinkComponent.cpp:72/141](mu-link/Source/UI/MuLinkComponent.cpp#L72) (em-dash placeholders). Build 882 — mu-clid + mu-link rebuilt; **mu-tant standalone exe relink pending** (mu-Tant.exe was running; its shared lib + the mu-core panel fix compiled, VST3/CLAP get it, standalone relinks when the app closes). **Remaining (lower priority, console-only):** ~130 test `beginTest`/`expect` descriptions have the same unwrapped em-dash/arrow but only print to the test console, not the GUI; a follow-up can sweep them + add a CI grep guard so it stops recurring. | ✅ Closed | 882 |

| 1013 | **[mu-tant/audio] Seamless hot-swap — retire-ramp voices dropped by a count-reducing full-preset swap (the one tail-cut gap).** Confirmed the swap is param-only and **never resets** filter z-state / per-voice insert / global `fxChain` buffers, so comb-filter + delay/reverb tails already ring through. The remaining hard-cut: a full preset with **fewer** voices instantly stopped summing the dropped voices. **Fixed:** when a committed full-preset swap reduces the count *while playing*, [applyFullPresetTree](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L1221) now snapshots each dropped voice's OLD engine config + insert algo/params **before** `replaceState`, and `renderRetiringVoice` keeps rendering them through their intact engine + OLD insert under a falling linear gain (~25 ms) before dropping — so the comb-filter / effect tail fades instead of snapping. RT-safe via a per-voice `samplesLeft` atomic (config written before arm/release, read only when armed/acquire); `processBlock` extends the rendered channel count to cover fading voices; retire state cleared in `prepareToPlay`. No DSP reset added → all other tails preserved. Build 880. | ✅ Closed | 880 |

| 1012 | **[mu-core/family] MIDI Clock + Note-mode as STANDARD synth features — centralise to mu-core, apply to every synth product.** Owner: "these should be standard features for all mu synth products." So lift mu-clid's product-side **MIDI Clock** (Source: Internal / MIDI In; Messages: Clock only / Transport / Both — standalone only) + **MIDI Note mode** (Free / Note) into mu-core / mu-tant. **Done — end to end:** **(a) MIDI Clock** — `MidiClockSync` lifted mu-clid → **`mu-core/Plugin/MidiClockSync.h`** (verbatim, JUCE-only; mu-clid includes the shared copy, no behaviour change); mu-tant wired to it — overrides the `ProcessorBase` MIDI virtuals, `processBlock` slaves the beat/tempo to external MIDI clock (standalone; mu-link takes priority when attached), `setMidiSyncEnabled`/`setMidiSyncMessages` persist to appSettings, **MIDI Clock settings rows** (Source / Messages, standalone-only) added to mu-tant's overlay mirroring mu-clid. **(b) Note mode (gate + pitch-track)** — the drone sounds only while a MIDI note is held and the held note sets the tonal centre (play it like an instrument): (1) audio-thread held-note stack with last-note priority + de-dupe ([scanNoteMode](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp)); (2) anti-click amplitude **gate** — an ~8 ms linear ramp toward held(1)/silent(0) applied to the final mix ([applyNoteModeGate](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp)); (3) **pitch-track** via a new `VoiceConfig::pitchOffsetSemis` (added to both oscs' final MIDI in `SynthVoice::setConfig` after `toneToMidi`, so scale intervals + per-osc oct/semi/fine survive); offset = `held − (root + 12·kBaseOctave)` (kBaseOctave shared via [Scales.h](mu-tant/Source/Audio/Scales.h)); (4) **Note Mode** settings row (Free / Note), shown in **both** plugin + standalone (mu-tant's Note mode works from a keyboard too, unlike mu-clid's plugin-only). `midiNoteMode` persists to appSettings; a Free↔Note switch resets the stack + gate. Build 889 green, mu-tant tests **130/130**. **Optional residual (not blocking):** adopt the shared `MidiClockSync` in mu-on/mu-toni when they mature. | ✅ Closed | 889 |

| 995 | **[mu-core/License → CRASH] Full mu-Clid crashed on construction (standalone wouldn't launch; pluginval scan 0xC0000005) — use-after-free in `ActivationStore::load`.** Owner reported the mu-Clid Debug standalone "no longer loads — clicking the exe has no effect" (exit `0xC0000005`). Localised with a headless pluginval pass (full mu-Clid VST3 failed at *scan/instantiation*; **Lite + mu-Tant + mu-On + mu-Toni all passed**) → the fault is in `PluginProcessor` construction, full-build-only (the `#if !MUCLID_LITE_BUILD` license/activation block), before any editor. Boot-trace breadcrumbs pinned it to `OnlineActivation::hasLocalActivation` → [ActivationStore::load](mu-core/License/ActivationStore.h): `if (auto* obj = juce::JSON::parse(f.loadFileAsString()).getDynamicObject())` — the parsed `var` is a **temporary destroyed at the end of the condition's full-expression, before the `if` body**, so its refcount hits zero, the `DynamicObject` is freed, and `obj` dangles → `obj->getProperty(...)` is a **use-after-free**. Only fires when the activation file **exists and parses to an object** (so mu-Tant, with no activation file, passed; `LicenseManager::check` was safe — it already used a *named* `parsed` var). Triggered on the owner's machine by a real `muclid.activation` left in `D:\OneDrive\Documents\TDP\muClid` from earlier LS testing. **Fix:** hold the parsed `var` in a named local (`const auto parsed = juce::JSON::parse(...)`) so it outlives the `getDynamicObject()` raw pointer + property reads. Verified: pluginval full mu-Clid VST3 passes + standalone launches. One-line mu-core fix → also protects mu-Tant / any sibling that ever writes an activation file. Pre-existing since the #980 activation work; unrelated to the #993/#994 session changes (those are editor-side). | ✅ Closed | 864 |

| 994 | **[mu-core/transport] In-DAW (plugin) play button only changed colour green→red instead of swapping the ▶/■ icon like standalone.** Owner: mu-Clid Lite in a DAW shows the play button turning green→red when the host plays, but the *correct* behaviour (as in the mu-clid standalone) is for the ▶ play icon to become a ■ stop icon. Root cause: [TransportBar::refreshPlayBtn()](mu-core/UI/TransportBar.cpp) standalone branch swaps `kPlay`↔`kStop` *and* recolours, but the plugin branch hard-set `kPlay` always and only recoloured. Fix: plugin branch now sets `playBtn.setButtonText(dawPlaying ? kStop : kPlay)` so the icon tracks DAW transport, matching standalone. Shared `TransportBar` so it corrects every product's in-DAW transport button (Lite + full mu-clid + mu-tant). Button stays non-interactive in plugin mode (host owns transport) — only the icon/colour reflect state. | ✅ Closed | 854 |

| 993 | **[build/versioning] Build-number policy was wrong — Debug bumps were throttled by a 5-minute window, so the number reported didn't match the shipped binary.** Owner loaded mu-Clid Lite and it showed 852 while a prior report said 850 — because [IncrementBuildNumber.cmake](cmake/IncrementBuildNumber.cmake) only bumped a Debug build when >300 s had elapsed since the last bump (mtime of `build_number.txt`), so rebuilds within the window silently reused a number, and rebuilds outside it bumped — making the counter track wall-clock gaps instead of builds. **Correct policy (owner rules):** (1) **every Debug build increments by exactly 1**, no time throttle; (2) **Release never increments** — it reuses the last Debug number and rebuilds only the Release artefacts (Debug artefacts untouched); (3) **Release must never *exceed* the last Debug number** — a Release coming out *lower* than the current Debug counter is **normal** (the counter marches ahead during repeated debug-fix builds; the last shipped Release legitimately sits below it). The error is only Release > last Debug (can only happen if Release wrongly incremented) → STOP with a fatal error so the owner can decide. **Fix:** removed the session-window logic; Debug always `+1` and records the value to a `.last_debug_build` witness file; Release reuses `build_number.txt` and `FATAL_ERROR`s only if it is *greater* than `.last_debug_build`. Also: always report the number from `mu-core/BuildNumber.h` read *after* the final build (never quote an intermediate build). Docs (CLAUDE.md build workflow) + build-workflow memory updated to match. **Release-process rules (4 & 5) reaffirmed, no code change:** a Release always (a) deploys artefacts to the OneDrive tester share and (b) produces a zip uploaded to the GitHub "latest release" so website links resolve; Mac/Linux CI runs only on explicit owner trigger. | ✅ Closed | 854 |

| 980 | **[release/licensing] Lemon Squeezy activation — online primary + offline challenge-response fallback.** Replace the static `.lic`-file model with: **(1) Online (primary)** — user pastes their Lemon Squeezy license key; plugin calls LS `/v1/licenses/activate` (key + machine-fingerprint instance id) over HTTPS (JUCE `URL`/`WebInputStream`), stores the returned activation token, and `/v1/licenses/validate`s on later launches. **(2) Offline (fallback)** — when no network: plugin shows a **challenge** (machine fingerprint + product, as a short code/QR); user visits the site (#983) / emails it; owner's signer (extends [gen_license.ps1](tools)/a hosted endpoint) validates the LS key and returns an **Ed25519-signed response bound to that fingerprint** (reuses the existing Monocypher verify + embedded public key); plugin verifies signature **and** that the fingerprint matches this machine, then caches it. The canonical signed payload must therefore **add a machine-fingerprint field** (current payload signs email/order/expires/name only — not machine-locked, so a response code can't be shared). Needs: a machine-fingerprint helper, an HTTP activation client (graceful timeout/offline → fall back to step 2), and persistent activation storage. **Blocked on owner:** Lemon Squeezy store/product IDs + where the offline signer is hosted. **Launch scope = mu-Clid + mu-Tant only** (mu-On + mu-Toni not yet ready — no LS product until they ship; their IDs slot in later with zero #980 impact). **LS product IDs:** mu-Clid = **1134518**, mu-Tant = **1134546** (drafts); store ID + per-variant IDs TBD. **Owner decision (tester model):** testers get the **Release (licensed) build + a signed `.lic` each** — so NO deploy change, but the offline signer must work per product. **Signer state (verified v1.0.832):** [gen_license.ps1](tools/gen_license.ps1) signs `product=mu-Clid` (OpenSSL Ed25519, canonical format matches the new [LicenseManager](mu-core/License/LicenseManager.cpp) exactly); `tools/private.pem` present + **git-ignored**, and its public key **matches mu-clid's embedded key byte-for-byte** → **mu-Clid `.lic` issuance works today**. **mu-Tant gap:** placeholder all-zero key — needs (1) keypair via [keygen.ps1](tools/keygen.ps1), (2) public key pasted into [mu-tant LicenseKey.h](mu-tant/Source/License/LicenseKey.h), (3) `gen_license.ps1` parametrised with `-Product` (currently mu-Clid-hardcoded lines 40+71; [verify_license.ps1](tools/verify_license.ps1) is already product-agnostic). **OWNER DECISIONS (locked, v1.0.833):** **(1) Phase 1 = online (LS activate/validate) first**; offline challenge-response automation is Phase 2. **(2) Machine-lock EVERYTHING** — `fingerprint=` is *always* in the canonical payload (no dual-path verifier); testers have no `.lic` yet, so all licenses get issued fingerprint-bound on demand. Tester issuance therefore uses the *same* challenge→issue flow as the offline fallback. **(3) Signer = manual now** (owner runs the tool by hand), hosted endpoint later (Phase 2). **(4) Activation UX = non-blocking** — unlicensed Release opens in Demo (the #981 caps) with an Activate button/overlay; no launch wall. **(5) Keygen/signer = a JUCE GUI `.exe` (`MuLicenseTool`)**, NOT PowerShell — replaces `keygen.ps1`+`gen_license.ps1`, links Monocypher + a shared `LicenseCanonical.h` lifted from LicenseManager so signer≡verifier by construction (drops the OpenSSL + duplicated-canonical-string drift risk). Keygen mode (keypair → private file + `uint8_t[32]` for `LicenseKey.h`) + Issue mode (form → machine-locked `.lic`). **Phase 1 components (mu-core, compiled per licensed product like the verifier):** `MachineFingerprint` (short stable code from `SystemStats::getMachineIdentifiers()`), `fingerprint=` added to `buildCanonical` + verifier match-check, `LemonSqueezyClient` (activate/validate over `juce::URL`, background thread, never audio), persistent `{key,instance_id}` storage, non-blocking Activation overlay in `EditorShellBase` (→ all products). **LS store (owner-supplied):** store **#377845** (`transwarp.lemonsqueezy.com`); products mu-Clid **1134518** / mu-Tant **1134546**. Still owner-gated for live testing: per-variant IDs + activation-limit config + a real test key. **PROGRESS (in flight, this session):** ✅ shared [LicenseCanonical.h](mu-core/License/LicenseCanonical.h) (signer≡verifier, `fingerprint=` always present); ✅ [MachineFingerprint.h](mu-core/License/MachineFingerprint.h) (juce_core `hashCode64` short code — MD5/SHA256 are in juce_cryptography which the verifier TU doesn't link); ✅ verifier now reads `fingerprint` + rejects a mismatched machine ([LicenseManager.cpp](mu-core/License/LicenseManager.cpp)); ✅ **[MuLicenseTool](tools/license-tool/CMakeLists.txt)** JUCE GUI built (keygen + issue, Monocypher signing, headless `--keygen` flag) — **replaces+retires `keygen.ps1`/`gen_license.ps1`/`verify_license.ps1` (deleted, OpenSSL dependency dropped)**; ✅ fresh Ed25519 keypairs generated for both products, public keys embedded ([mu-clid](mu-clid/Source/License/LicenseKey.h)/[mu-tant](mu-tant/Source/License/LicenseKey.h)), secrets in git-ignored `tools/keys/`; ✅ mu-clid+mu-tant+tool Debug build green. ✅ [LemonSqueezyClient](mu-core/License/LemonSqueezyClient.cpp) (activate/validate over `juce::URL`, background-thread, 8s timeout) + [ActivationStore](mu-core/License/ActivationStore.h) + [OnlineActivation](mu-core/License/OnlineActivation.cpp) orchestrator (activate / validateStored w/ 30-day offline grace / hasLocalActivation), all compiled per-licensed-product; ✅ non-blocking [ActivationPanel](mu-core/UI/ActivationPanel.cpp) wired into `EditorShellBase` (demo banner now click-to-activate; paste key→activate off the message thread; shows the offline machine-code challenge; on success drops the banner + relayouts); ✅ `ProcessorBase` gained `activateOnlineFn`/`onlineActivated`/`licenseChallengeCode`; ✅ both products' `isLicensed()` = offline `.lic` **OR** online-activated, startup uses a LOCAL-only activation check (no network → no plugin-load hang), with the real network activate behind the overlay; ✅ **full Debug+Release green, all products @ v1.0.837** (deployed to OneDrive tester share — testers idle pre-launch, per owner). **Phase 1 CODE COMPLETE.** **Remaining to close #980:** owner supplies one LS **test license key** → prove the live activate/validate round-trip in-app; then commit. **Phase 1.5 follow-ups (noted):** background online re-validate/revocation pass at startup (currently optimistic local-trust within grace); in-app "Buy" checkout link (needs variant URL, ties to #983). | ✅ Closed | 837 |

| 978 | **[macOS distribution] Mac bundles must ship as a `ditto` zip — copying CI artifacts through Windows breaks them.** Owner (no Mac) asked to refresh the `TDP/Mac` OneDrive folder (stale 9 June). Downloading the mac-validate `mac-plugins-release` artifact and inspecting it revealed every inner Mach-O is `-rw-r--r--` — the GitHub artifact download path **strips the Unix executable bit, symlinks, and the arm64 ad-hoc code signature**. Copying those into `TDP/Mac` would ship **broken** bundles: the `.app` won't launch (no +x), and Apple Silicon refuses an arm64 slice whose signature was invalidated — a **likely contributor to testers' earlier "can't open"** (beyond Gatekeeper #99). Can't repair Unix perms/signatures from Windows. **Fix:** [mac-validate.yml](.github/workflows/mac-validate.yml) now packages the bundles on the Mac runner with `ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent` (preserves perms/symlinks/signature) into `mu-family-mac.zip`, uploaded as `mac-plugins-release`. **New distribution flow:** owner downloads the artifact, places `mu-family-mac.zip` in `TDP/Mac` **without extracting on Windows**; testers extract it **on their Mac** (Finder), install the bundles, `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`. Requires a re-dispatch of mac-validate to produce the zip (the current Windows-side TDP/Mac bundles can't be made correct without a Mac run).  **✅ PROVEN: mac-validate run 27304718168 fully green** (universal build, lipo arm64+x86_64, pluginval, auval, mu-Tant + mu-Clid renders all passed); mu-family-mac.zip built via ditto, **verified all 19 Mach-O binaries executable (0o755)**, and **delivered to OneDrive TDP/Mac** + READ-ME-FIRST.txt. | ✅ Closed | 831 |

| 977 | **[deploy reliability] VST3 OneDrive deploy can silently fail on a stale/dehydrated destination bundle.** Owner reported the OneDrive tester files still dated 9 June. Investigation: most products redeployed fine at v1.0.831, but **two were stranded** — `mu-Toni.vst3` (the deploy's `cmake -E copy_directory` in [cmake/DeployRelease.cmake](cmake/DeployRelease.cmake) runs with `ERROR_QUIET` and only emits a `message(WARNING)` on failure; the stale OneDrive bundle — likely OneDrive cloud-dehydrated / a locked sub-file — couldn't be overwritten, so the copy failed into a buried warning and the 9-June bundle persisted), and `mu-link.exe` (mu-link has **no `increment_build_number` dependency** and doesn't read the build number, so with unchanged source it never relinks → its POST_BUILD deploy never refreshes; its date tracks the last actual mu-link code change, which is correct-but-confusing). **Resolved this session manually:** removed the stale OneDrive `mu-Toni.vst3` and force-copied the fresh local bundle; force-rebuilt mu-link (deleted the exe) → redeployed. **All OneDrive plugin files now today @ v1.0.831.** **Owner clarification → no code fix needed:** mu-toni is a not-yet-worked-on scaffold (its stale date is irrelevant), and mu-link is largely independent of mu-core so its date correctly tracks its OWN last source change, not the family version (no version-sync wanted). The dehydration/silent-copy failure only struck **because** those targets are inactive — actively-deployed products (mu-clid/tant/on) stay hydrated and copy fine — so the `DeployRelease.cmake` remove-then-copy hardening is **dropped as low-value** (and it carried partial-removal risk on a tester-locked bundle). Closed: the immediate staleness is fixed; no deploy-script change. | ✅ Closed | 831 |

| 976 | **[tooling] mu-Tant headless `--render` → guaranteed-audio Mac smoke (no sample dependency).** The mac-validate render evidence (#975) initially used the mu-Clid A-suite, whose presets can expect samples not present on CI → silent clips. mu-Tant is a wavetable synth, so a headless render produces a content-independent oscillator drone. Added [mu-tant/Source/Plugin/RenderMode.{h,cpp}](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/RenderMode.cpp) (mirrors mu-clid's: `--render --out <wav> [--seconds/--samplerate/--blocksize]`), wired into [StandaloneApp.cpp](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/StandaloneApp.cpp) (initialise → parse/execute/quit) + [CMakeLists](mu-tant/CMakeLists.txt) (Standalone-only TU). **Key gotcha found:** mu-Tant is **silent on load by design** — the gater returns Silence when stopped (`gateModeFor: !playing → Silence`) and when playing an empty pattern; the raw drone only passes with the **gater bypassed**. So `execute()` sets `v0_gate_bypass=1` before rendering (matches the owner's "open mu-Tant, click bypass, it drones"). Also corrected the **stale [PluginProcessor.h](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.h) comment** that claimed "stopped → gate held open (audition)" — it's the opposite. New [tests/expectations/mutant_drone.json](tests/expectations/mutant_drone.json) (rms_dbfs ≥ −60 over 0.5–3.5 s). [mac-validate.yml](.github/workflows/mac-validate.yml) now renders the mu-Tant drone as a **hard gate** (mu-Clid A-suite demoted to a best-effort bonus). **Verified locally on Windows:** clean build → render → analyse PASS (drone ≈ **−14 dBFS**). The CI step itself only runs on a Mac dispatch.  **✅ PROVEN: mac-validate run 27304718168 fully green** (universal build, lipo arm64+x86_64, pluginval, auval, mu-Tant + mu-Clid renders all passed); mu-family-mac.zip built via ditto, **verified all 19 Mach-O binaries executable (0o755)**, and **delivered to OneDrive TDP/Mac** + READ-ME-FIRST.txt. | ✅ Closed | 831 |

| 975 | **[CI/tooling] On-demand macOS validation workflow — test Mac builds before testers, without a Mac, minimising cost.** Owner has no Mac and macOS GitHub runners bill at **10× the minute rate**, so the goal is a cheap, opt-in way to vet the Mac build + produce an evidence pack to analyse before sending to testers. **Done:** (1) new [.github/workflows/mac-validate.yml](.github/workflows/mac-validate.yml) — **`workflow_dispatch` only** (manual, runs only when fired). One macOS job: configure+build **universal Release** (VST3/CLAP/Standalone/AU, all products) → **`lipo` hard gate** (arm64+x86_64 present) → **pluginval** the VST3s (headless host harness: instantiate, audio at many SR/block, state save/restore, param fuzz — hard gate, `strictness` dispatch input) → **`auval`** the AUs (report-only) → **render the mu-Clid A-suite to WAVs + `analyse.py`** (report-only — real Mac-rendered audio to download & listen to) → upload two artifacts: `mac-validation-report` (lipo/pluginval/auval logs + rendered WAVs) and `mac-plugins-release` (the built universal bundles). (2) [run-listening-tests.py](tests/scripts/run-listening-tests.py) made **cross-platform** (finds the `.app` binary on macOS / bare exe on Linux, not just `*.exe`) so the render pipeline runs on the Mac runner. (3) **Trimmed macOS off the every-push [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) matrix** (Linux+Windows remain the cheap net) — the universal `lipo` gate from #972 relocated into mac-validate.yml. **Tradeoff:** no per-push Mac *compile* coverage — dispatch mac-validate before a release / after Mac-affecting changes. Does NOT sign/notarize (#99) — testers still need `xattr` quarantine-strip. Both workflows YAML-lint clean; only provable on an actual dispatch (owner-gated, costs minutes). **Follow-up fix:** added `set -o pipefail` to the configure/build/pluginval/mu-Tant-render steps — without it a `cmd \| tee log` pipeline returns *tee's* exit (always 0), so the "hard gates" (pluginval, the mu-Tant render→analyse) would have gone **green even on failure**; pipefail makes them actually gate. Also tee the configure+build output into `report/` so a build-stage failure lands in the downloadable artifact, not only the Actions console. **First real dispatch (run 27291697372) result:** universal build compiled (first-ever Mac compile ✓), `lipo` universal ✓, pluginval all VST3s ✓, auval ✓, mu-Tant render wrote the WAV ✓ — **only** the analyse step failed: `analyse.py` imports scipy but the step pip-installed only numpy → `ModuleNotFoundError`. Fixed → `pip install numpy scipy`. Verified by downloading the run artifact and analysing the **actual Mac-rendered WAV** locally: drone = **−14.06 dBFS PASS** (the Mac build genuinely makes sound; only the dep was missing). The run's `mac-plugins-release` (universal, pluginval+lipo-validated) is already shippable; re-dispatch gives a clean green.  **✅ PROVEN: mac-validate run 27304718168 fully green** (universal build, lipo arm64+x86_64, pluginval, auval, mu-Tant + mu-Clid renders all passed); mu-family-mac.zip built via ditto, **verified all 19 Mach-O binaries executable (0o755)**, and **delivered to OneDrive TDP/Mac** + READ-ME-FIRST.txt. | ✅ Closed | 831 |

| 974 | **[Fixed, family-wide via mu-core] External (DAW) sidechain produced no ducking / dead GR — the buffer clear was wiping the sidechain input.** Tester confirmed on **mu-tant in both VST3 and CLAP** (Amount full, kick on the SC bus) — so not CLAP-specific and not the three originally-hypothesised causes (Amt=0 / pre-824 build / CLAP bus disabled). **Real root cause:** every product declares a stereo **Sidechain input** + stereo **Output** bus — equal channel counts, so JUCE maps **both to the same process-buffer channels [0,1]**. Each product's `processBlock` calls `buffer.clear()` at the top, then read the sidechain via `getBusBuffer(buffer,true,0)` — but the clear had already **zeroed the shared channels**, so `extScL` pointed at silence → never crossed the duck threshold → no GR. **Fix (one place):** mu-core `MixerEngine` now owns a private `extScCapture` buffer (sized in `prepare`) + `copyExternalSidechain()`; `ProcessorBase::captureSidechainAndClear(buffer)` copies the SC bus into it **before** clearing. Each product's `processBlock` now calls that single shared primitive as its first line (replacing the bare `buffer.clear()`), and the ~12-line per-product extraction block was **deleted** (it was duplicated in all four — a prior parity violation now removed). Internal channel-to-channel sidechain (e.g. mu-on Bass↔Kick) was unaffected (reads mixer channel bufs, not the host buffer). All four products Debug+Release clean; ships v1.0.828. **Tester-confirmed working in Bitwig** (mu-tant, v1.0.828). | ✅ Closed | 828 |

| 973 | **[UI→Fixed] Mixer channel strips showed stale "inactive" dimming (only channel 1 bright) after a preset/host-state load changed the rhythm count.** Tester (Bitwig) loaded a 5-rhythm preset but the mixer dimmed channels 2–5 as if inactive, even though audio was flowing. Root cause: each strip's `active`/name/colour (the dim overlay in [MixerChannel::paint](mu-core/UI/MixerChannel.cpp)) was set **only** in `MixerOverlay::buildChannels()`, which runs at construction and on `refresh()` — and `refresh()` is gated behind `isMixerVisible()` ([PluginEditor.cpp](mu-clid/Source/Plugin/PluginEditor.cpp)). `loadFromAPVTS()` (which runs on `visibilityChanged` + preset reload) refreshed params/sidechain sources but never the active state, so a count change while the mixer was hidden left the dim overlays stale when it was next shown. Fix (mu-core, family-wide): `loadFromAPVTS` now re-syncs every strip's `setActive`/`setChannelName`/`setChannelColour` from the live `getNumChannels()` each call (added a `setChannelColour` setter to [MixerChannel](mu-core/UI/MixerChannel.h)); lightweight (no component recreation, unlike buildChannels). Benefits mu-clid/mu-tant/mu-on/mu-toni mixers. | ✅ Closed | 827 |

| 972 | **[macOS] Universal (arm64 + x86_64) builds so Intel Macs can load the plugins.** Testers reported the Mac binaries won't open (Gatekeeper warning that won't bypass). Two causes: (a) unsigned/un-notarized — the Apple side of #99, worked around tester-side via `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`; (b) **this item** — no `CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES` was set, so the build only targets the CI runner's native arch (`macos-latest` = Apple Silicon → **arm64-only**), and an Intel Mac can't run an arm64-only binary at all (no Gatekeeper trick helps). Fix: set `CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES "arm64;x86_64"` (guarded `if(APPLE AND NOT DEFINED …)` so a local dev build can still override to a single arch for speed) in the root [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt) **before `project()`** so the arch is honoured during toolchain setup; applies family-wide (every product builds universal with no per-product change). The `lipo -archs` arm64+x86_64 hard gate now lives in [mac-validate.yml](.github/workflows/mac-validate.yml) (#975). Verifiable only on a macOS runner (no local Mac); Windows/Linux configure unchanged (APPLE-guarded). | 971 | **[pluginval→Fixed] mu-Clid Lite crashed (null deref) on host state restore.** pluginval (#970) immediately caught it: `mu-Clid Lite.vst3` segfaulted (`0xC0000005`) in the **"Plugin state"** test — i.e. the host save→restore cycle a DAW runs every time a project reloads. Root cause: [PresetIO::restoreRhythmSample](mu-clid/Source/Plugin/PresetIO.cpp) dereferences `proc_.voiceEngines[i]` unconditionally (`->clearSample()` / `->loadFile()`), but the **Lite** (MIDI-effect) build never creates the voice engines (`#if !MUCLID_LITE_BUILD voiceEngines[0]=…` in [PluginProcessor.cpp](mu-clid/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp)), so on restore (empty sample path → the `clearSample()` branch) it hit a null pointer. The sibling restore site `forceSyncRhythmFromAPVTS` was already null-guarded (`if (voiceEngines[ri])`); this one wasn't. Fix: early-return in `restoreRhythmSample` when `voiceEngines[i]` is null — Lite has no sample player to load into, and `loadedSamplePaths` is maintained by the caller. Full build unaffected (engine always non-null there). Verified: Lite VST3 now passes pluginval state test (5/5 family VST3s green). | ✅ Closed | 825 |

| 970 | **[Tooling→Fixed] pluginval headless VST3 validation — Phase 1 shipped.** Added Tracktion's [pluginval](https://github.com/Tracktion/pluginval) to autonomously validate the family's built **VST3** binaries (mu-clid, mu-clid-lite, mu-tant, mu-toni, mu-on). pluginval hammers each plugin in a real host harness: instantiate, fuzz every parameter, run audio at many sample-rates/buffer-sizes, open/close editor, multiple instances, and **save→restore state and verify identity** — directly enforcing the "Everything in APVTS" cardinal rule (an un-persisted param fails restore) and the "audio thread never allocates / no NaN" rule (param-fuzz + denormal audio). **Coverage caveat:** pluginval validates VST3 + AU only — **not CLAP, not Standalone**; all formats wrap the same `ProcessorBase`, so VST3 covers the shared engine, but CLAP-*wrapper* bugs (cf. #969 CLAP sidechain) need a separate `clap-validator` pass (Phase 3). **Delivered:** (1) [tests/scripts/run-pluginval.ps1](tests/scripts/run-pluginval.ps1) — auto-downloads a pinned pluginval (or honours `$env:PLUGINVAL_PATH`), globs the per-product `build/<product>/<target>_artefacts/<Config>/VST3/*.vst3` bundles, runs `pluginval --strictness-level N --validate` per VST3, aggregates pass/fail, exits non-zero on any failure; flags `-Config Release` (default), `-Strictness`, `-SkipGui`; absent products (lite/toni in CI) are skipped not failed. (2) A Windows-only CI step in [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) running the script at strictness 5 as a hard gate. Caught #971 (Lite state-restore crash) on first run; after the fix **5/5 family VST3s pass at strictness 5**. **Follow-ups (Open, future):** Phase 2 — Linux (xvfb) + macOS (replace/complement `auval`), raise strictness toward 8–10; Phase 3 — `run-clapval.ps1` for CLAP-wrapper coverage. CI step proven only once pushed (no local green for the workflow itself). **CI fix (v1.0.830):** the first real CI run failed because JUCE leaves an **empty `.vst3` bundle skeleton** for an unbuilt target (CI builds a product subset), and pluginval failed that stub with "No types found"; the script now **skips any bundle with no compiled module inside** (checks for the inner `Contents/<arch>/<name>.vst3` file). Also added `mu-clid-lite_VST3` to the CI build so the shipping Lite variant is actually validated (not skipped) — it's the product that had #971. | ✅ Closed | 825 |

| 969 | **[Fixed] CLAP sidechain input now exposed to hosts (was VST3-only).** The sidechain showed in **VST3** (via `SidechainVST3Extensions::getPluginHasMainInput()=false`) but NOT in **CLAP** (Bitwig) — the CLAP wrapper flags input port 0 as `CLAP_AUDIO_PORT_IS_MAIN` unless the processor implements `clap_juce_audio_processor_capabilities::isInputMain()`. Added the parallel CLAP capability in mu-core's [ProcessorBase](mu-core/Plugin/ProcessorBase.h) (one place → all four products): conditionally inherits `clap_juce_extensions::clap_juce_audio_processor_capabilities` and overrides `isInputMain(int)→false` so the lone input is a sidechain, not main. Guarded by `__has_include(<clap-juce-extensions/...>)` so only the `_CLAP` targets pull it in — VST3/Standalone/tests compile with **zero** CLAP dependency (verified: pragma fires on all 4 CLAP builds, absent on VST3/Standalone). All 4 CLAP + VST3 + Standalone Debug-clean; mu-clid 140 · mu-tant 132 · mu-on 15. Needs in-host (Bitwig) confirmation of the sidechain button on the CLAP. | ✅ Closed | 824 |

| 967 | **[Fixed] Stepped-mode modulator now tiles by step length too (follow-up to #963).** Extended the step-length tiling from Smooth to Stepped mode: [getStepCount](mu-core/Sequencer/ControlSequence.cpp) → `ceil(loop/step)` (with a 1e-9 guard so exact divisions don't round up) — 6 steps for Step 1/16×3 in a 1-bar loop (3,3,3,3,3,1), was `round`=5; [evaluateStepped](mu-core/Sequencer/ControlSequence.cpp) indexes by `phase / stepFraction` (tile by width) not `phase*count` (equal); [StepEditor](mu-core/UI/Components/StepEditor.cpp) gained `setStepFraction` and tiles its dividers/bars/hit-test at `k·stepFraction` with a narrower partial final cell; [ModulatorEditor::syncStepValues](mu-core/UI/ModulatorEditor.cpp) feeds it the fraction. Integer loop/step configs are byte-identical (ceil==round, `phase/frac`==`phase*count`); only non-integer (the broken case) changes. New tests: `getStepCount` 16/3→6 + an `evaluateStepped` per-cell read-back → mu-tant 132/132, mu-clid 140, mu-on 15. | ✅ Closed | 821 |

| 963 | **[Fixed] Smooth-modulator step grid now tiles by the actual step length (partial final cell) instead of equal division.** Added [ControlSequence::getStepFraction()](mu-core/Sequencer/ControlSequence.cpp) (= `step/loop`, clamped to (0,1]); [LFOEditor](mu-core/UI/Components/LFOEditor.cpp) replaced its equal-`stepCount` grid + `snapX` with a `stepFraction` model — a grid line at each `k·stepFraction < 1`, so Step 1/16×3 in a 1-bar loop draws lines at 3/6/9/12/15 sixteenths = five 3/16 cells + a 1/16 remainder (was 5 equal cells from `round(16/3)=5`), and node X-snap lands on those real boundaries. | 962 | **[Fixed] Modulator smooth editor: double-click an existing node to delete it.** Added a `mouseDoubleClick` override to the shared [LFOEditor](mu-core/UI/Components/LFOEditor.cpp) that hit-tests the cursor and erases the node under it — same interior-only guard as right-click (the pinned x=0/x=1 boundary anchors are never deleted), resetting `dragIndex` so the trailing `mouseUp` (set by the second click's `mouseDown`) doesn't re-notify against shifted indices. | 961 | **[Audit→Fixed] HIGH** — ChorusEffect out-of-bounds read at high sample rates. [ChorusEffect.h](mu-core/Audio/FX/Send/ChorusEffect.h) no longer hard-codes a 4096-sample delay line: `prepareInner` now sizes each line to `jmax(4096, ceil(0.07·sr))` (covers the ~`0.06·sr` worst-case read offset + the Hermite +2 lookahead at any SR), `assign`s it (touches the pages — no first-touch fault), and the write-pos wrap uses the runtime `delaySize`. Above ~68 kHz the old fixed buffer made `hermiteDelay`'s `(writeP - offset + bufSize) % bufSize` go negative → heap over-read on the audio thread (UB/garbage/crash at 88.2/96/192 kHz); now the buffer always exceeds the max offset so the modulo stays in range. SendFXSmokeTests green (mu-clid 140, mu-tant 130). | ✅ Closed | 815 |

| 957 | **[Fixed] Modulation curves clamped to the visible range — no more overshoot when bending or switching uni↔bipolar.** A bent segment's Catmull-Rom + `handleY` bezier control points, or a curve point's `y` after a polarity flip, could land outside the editor's 0..1 (unipolar) / -1..1 (bipolar) range, so the curve drew past the panel and the audio over/undershot the destination's swing. Fixes, all matched so drawing == audio: (1) [ControlSequence::evaluate](mu-core/Sequencer/ControlSequence.cpp) now clamps the output to the matrix contract (`0..100` / `-100..100`, not just the old unipolar floor); (2) [evaluateSmooth](mu-core/Sequencer/ControlSequence.cpp) + [LFOEditor::buildCurvePath](mu-core/UI/Components/LFOEditor.cpp) clamp the bezier control points `c1y`/`c2y` to the visible range (a bezier lies within its control hull → the segment can't overshoot); (3) anchors re-clamped on [LFOEditor::setUnipolar](mu-core/UI/Components/LFOEditor.h) + `setPoints`, and the stored `cs->curvePoints` re-clamped under lock on the polarity toggle in [ModulatorEditor](mu-core/UI/ModulatorEditor.cpp). 2-point/linear ramps unaffected (control points already in range) → all suites green (mu-clid 140, mu-tant 130, mu-on 15). Family-wide (every modulator + mu-on's Rumble bar envelope). | ✅ Closed | 813 |

Since `kTantModParams` + the `D_*` enum are file-local in [PluginProcessor.cpp](mu-tant/Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp) (a runtime test can't see them), added a `constexpr` `static_assert` that `kTantModParams[i].destId == kModDestTable[i].id` for every `i` (plus representative `D_*`→dest pins), so any reorder/insert that would seed `resolveLane` with the wrong atom/range for a dest id now **fails to compile** instead of silently mis-routing modulation — stronger than the requested runtime test, and it can't be skipped. | 947 | **[Fixed] Drawable curve editor now bends smoothly through the points (no kinks).** The shared smooth-curve editor (`LFOEditor`) + its audio evaluator (`ControlSequence::evaluateSmooth`) interpolated each segment independently, so multi-point curves kinked at the anchors. | 945 | **[Fixed] mu-on: new "Rumble" lane — classic techno rumble framework.** Added a 5th lane ([MuOnChannels.h](mu-on/Source/Plugin/MuOnChannels.h): `Rumble=4`, `kNumChannels=5`, `kNumStepLanes=4`) that **processes the Kick's audio** rather than stepping. [RumbleEngine.h](mu-on/Source/Audio/RumbleEngine.h) runs the kick feed, in order, through: **(1)** input drive (the same MultiModeFilter valve), **(2)** three tempo-synced **delay taps** at 1/16·2/16·3/16, each with a level, **(3)** a **dark reverb** (mu-core `ReverbSlot` + a low-pass, with a **size** + dry/wet **mix** control, `r_revmix`), **(4)** a per-bar **volume envelope** — a **drawable smooth curve** (mu-core `LFOEditor`) that sits in the **step-grid slot** for the Rumble lane (the lane has no steps), persisted in state + evaluated audio-side under a try-lock, **(5)** a final multimode **filter**. The kick feed is stashed by [GrooveVoices](mu-on/Source/Audio/GrooveVoices.h) (Kick renders before Rumble) and fed in; the mixer strip gives Rumble a sidechain pre-wired to the Kick (amount 0 by default → optional kick-pumping). 9 engine params (`r_drive`/`r_d1..3`/`r_size`/`r_revmix`/`r_revlp`/`r_cut`/`r_res`) + per-lane mod dests ([MuOnModDest](mu-on/Source/Modulation/MuOnModDest.h), `.prop`); EnginePanel + sidebar + reset wired. **Framework status:** chain is audible end-to-end; the reverb tone + envelope curve-eval are basic and the per-block envelope is coarse (fine for now). Build clean; mu-on-tests 14/14; boundary PASS. | ✅ Closed | 807 |

Dests are now **proportion-space (scale 1.0)**: [registerDepthScales](mu-tant/Source/Modulation/MuTantModDest.h) registers the mu-tant engine ids (`osc*`/`level`) at 1.0 instead of 6/24/200/255/66 — **those old scales already equalled each param's range width, so the modulation magnitude is unchanged; the only behaviour change is that mod now clamps at each param's legal range instead of overflowing it** (owner-signed-off, #944 was On Hold for this). Dest **ids unchanged → no preset migration**. Shared `filter.cutoff` (1.0) / `filter.resonance` (0.99) registry entries left untouched so a co-loaded mu-clid keeps its scales (only cost: full-depth resonance mod reaches ~0.98 vs 0.99 — imperceptible). Integer pitch dests now round (not truncate) the proportion round-trip → no dropped semitone. Snapshot/live-arc block rewritten to publish from the resolved `out[]` unconditionally. mu-tant-tests **130/130** (added a `resolveLane` rail-clamp test; updated the depth-scale test to proportion-space); mu-clid 140/140 (shared `filter.resonance` intact); all standalones Debug-clean; boundary PASS (161). | ✅ Closed | 810 |

| 938 | **[Audit→Fixed] MED — boundary leak removed: mu-core no longer enumerates product param ids in the modulation depth-scale table.** `ModulationMatrix::depthScaleFor` previously hardcoded mu-tant ids (`osc1.*`/`osc2.*`/`xmod`/`noise.level`/`level`) and mu-clid ids (`ks.*`/`voc.*`/`euclid.a/b/c.*`), so the shared platform "knew" each plugin's params (the boundary checker missed it — it scans includes/symbols, not string literals). Fixed **without** touching persisted ids, seed/write-back, or presets: mu-core now keeps only (1) the generic `.prop` rule (scale 1.0), (2) its own shared voice/filter/insert vocabulary (`filter.*`/`amp.*`/`pitch.*`/`fenv.*`/`accentDb`/`insert.*`) seeded into a [registry](mu-core/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L16-L70), and (3) a 100 default. Products register their engine-specific scales via the new `ModulationMatrix::registerDepthScale(id, scale)`, called once on the message thread from each `PluginProcessor` ctor (`mu_tant::registerDepthScales` / `mu_clid::registerDepthScales`, guarded by `std::call_once` → race-free vs. concurrent instances + before any audio; chosen over a header static, which can be deferred if unused and would miss the headless/no-editor path). mu-on needs nothing — its dests are all `.prop` (the `.prop` early-return never touches the registry, so no audio-thread map access either). Behaviour byte-identical (same scale values, just relocated). Note: `xmod`=127 was already dead (mu-tant uses `xmod.fm/am/ring` → default 100) and was dropped. Test added (mu-tant: registered `osc1.semi`→24 swing) → mu-tant-tests **129/129**; mu-clid 140/140, mu-on 14/14; boundary PASS (157 files); all products Debug-clean. **Unblocks #942** (the per-lane routing helper can now assume `.prop`/registry, not mu-core-hardcoded scales). | ✅ Closed | 800 |

COMPILE_OPTIONS "/wd4244")` guarded by `if(MSVC)` in [mu-clid/CMakeLists.txt](mu-clid/CMakeLists.txt) (covers both mu-clid + mu-clid-lite, the two targets that compile it). | 933 | **[Fixed] Filter Drive onset made gradual (shared mu-core — mu-tant + mu-clid).** Reported the LP filter drive "kicks in instantly". Confirmed the drive path is identical shared code in both products — the saturation stage lives once in [MultiModeFilter::process](mu-core/Audio/MultiModeFilter.cpp#L74-L97): pre-gain → asymmetric soft-clip (`tanh` positive / `x/(1−x)` negative, for even harmonics) → `1/√preGain` makeup, bypassed at drive≈0. The harshness was the **linear** pre-gain ramp `1 + drv*5`, so low knob values already added a lot. Owner approved a gentler curve: changed the pre-gain to **squared** `1 + drv*drv*5`. Same endpoints (drv=0 → 1× clean, drv=1 → 6× full) so the max-drive ceiling and existing full-drive presets are unchanged, but the lower half of the knob is far gentler (drv=0.5 → 2.25× vs the old 3.5×; drv=0.2 → 1.2× vs 2×). Applies family-wide (it's the shared filter). NB the stage is still memoryless (not anti-aliased) — fine for warmth, can alias at extreme drive+input; oversampling is a separate future item if needed. mu-tant-tests 128/128; Debug clean across mu-tant + mu-clid. | ✅ Closed | 795 |

| 932 | **[UI→Fixed] Shared ModulatorEditor — "N steps" readout was permanently half-hidden behind the dice button (all products).** [ModulatorEditor::paint](mu-core/UI/ModulatorEditor.cpp#L678-L691) drew the Stepped-mode step-count ("N steps") right-anchored at `getWidth() - s(58)`, but the randomise **dice** button is also right-anchored at `getWidth() - headerH` and paints an **opaque** panel-coloured fill — so the dice always covered the right ~26 px of the readout at any panel width (reported on mu-tant: the value "appears on the right, mostly overlapped by the dice", visibly changing behind it). Fixed: the readout is now **left-justified immediately after the step group's × multiplier** (`stepReadoutX` captured in `resized()`), bounded on the right by the dice so it never underlaps it — reads "Step 1/16 ▼ × 1   16 steps" left-to-right next to its own controls. Central mu-core fix → benefits mu-clid / mu-tant / mu-on. Verified Debug-compiling across all three products. | ✅ Closed | 795 |

| 931 | **[Fixed] mu-tant: insert-slot modulation destinations now show the per-algo names instead of generic "Insert P1..P4".** Root cause: the shared `ModulatorEditor`/`ModMatrixPanel` re-label the four insert destinations from `mu_ui::kInsertAlgoSlots[driveChar]` only after `setInsertAlgorithm(driveChar)` is called; mu-clid wired this but **mu-tant's [VoicePanel](mu-tant/Source/UI/VoicePanel.cpp) never did**, so `currentDriveChar` stayed 0 and the dropdown always showed the generic aliases. No explicit voice-select call is needed — `insertSub.setChannel()` (called from `setVoice`) → `configureInsertAlgorithm()` already fires `onInsertAlgorithmChanged`, so the names track the selected voice's insert algo + initial show automatically (mirrors mu-clid). **Root-cause was a documentation gap:** the family docs described `InsertSubsection` and `ModulatorPanel` each in isolation but never stated that a product using both must connect `onInsertAlgorithmChanged → setInsertAlgorithm` — so it was dropped when mu-tant mirrored mu-clid. Fixed the gap: [docs/design-ui-family.md](docs/design-ui-family.md) §9 now marks this wiring **REQUIRED** on the InsertSubsection row and adds a per-voice modulator-panel row documenting the `setVoiceSlot` + `setDestProvider` + `setInsertAlgorithm` contract, so future siblings can't miss it. | ✅ Closed | 795 |

| 930 | **[Fixed] mu-tant: Filter 2 cutoff/resonance are now modulation targets (parity with Filter 1).** Added a "Filter 2" section to [MuTantModDest.h](mu-tant/Source/Modulation/MuTantModDest.h) with `filter2.cutoff.prop` + `filter2.resonance.prop`, using the generic `.prop` proportion-space convention (`depthScaleFor`=1.0 — **no mu-core edit**, boundary-clean; the dual filter is mu-tant-only). The audio-thread map is pre-seeded from `kModDestTable` in the ctor, so the two new keys are pure overwrites (RT-safe). Live-arc snapshot on the F2 knobs deferred (modulation works; arcs are cosmetic). | ✅ Closed | 795 |

| 927 | **[Audit→Fixed] mu-on Bass filter envelope now opens on the onset block.** [BassEngine::render](mu-on/Source/Audio/BassEngine.h) computed the block-rate filter cutoff from the previous block's `t` (reset to 0 only inside the per-sample loop on `restart`), so the trigger block evaluated `fEnv≈0` and missed the filter-env "open" on the very attack it should brighten. | 925 | **[Audit→Fixed] mu-on SampleChannel no longer rewrites the ratio span every block.** [SampleChannel::render](mu-on/Source/Audio/SampleChannel.h) filled `ratios[i] = ratio` per sample each block although the tune is block-constant. | 924 | **[Audit→Fixed] mu-on sequencer onset is now sample-accurate end-to-end (offset is honored, not discarded).** The `GrooveSequencer` already computed a per-step `sampleOffset` (tested by the swing test) but the processBlock consumer ignored it and every engine restarted at sample 0. Threaded the offset through `GrooveVoices::trigger(track, vel, off)` into each engine's `trigger(vel, onset)`: Kick/Bass gate their per-sample restart on `i >= pendingOnset`; SampleChannel starts the sample + gate at the offset via a `scratch` sub-buffer view. So a step landing mid-block now sounds at its exact sample (≤ one-block onset jitter eliminated; swing lands precisely). Engine `trigger` onset defaults to 0 (existing call sites + tests unaffected). Tests added (KickEngine + SampleChannel onset: silent before the offset, sounds after) → mu-on-tests 14/14. | ✅ Closed | 799 |

Stop now silences all voices immediately. (Sustaining-while-playing across pattern gaps remains the documented no-note-off limitation — per-step note length/Release is the tracked future item.) Test added (`reset()` silences a ringing voice) → mu-on-tests 14/14. | ✅ Closed | 799 |

| 916 | **[Audit→Fixed]** `TransportClock` now ACCUMULATES beats incrementally instead of recomputing `samplePos × current tempo`, so a tempo change no longer retroactively rewrites the musical position. [TransportClock.h](mu-link/Source/Clock/TransportClock.h#L32-L40) `advance()` does `beatPos += frames/sr × bpm/60` at the block's tempo; `beats()` returns the accumulator; `prepare()`/`rewind()` reset it. The transport now carries the accumulated `ppqPosition` end-to-end: added `ppqPosition` to `TransportBlock` + `TransportSnapshot` and the seqlock read/write ([MuLinkProtocol.h](mu-core/Link/MuLinkProtocol.h)); `ServerEngine::snapshot` publishes `clock.beats()`; [MuLinkPlayHead.h](mu-core/Link/MuLinkPlayHead.h#L25-L38) reports the carried ppq (not a samples×tempo recompute); `MuLinkClient`'s consume-time projection advances ppq by the buffered frames too. Fixes a jittering bar position on slaved mu-clid/mu-tant under external-MIDI slave (continuous re-estimate). New test pins it (tempo halving → beats 2.0, not the old 1.5). | ✅ Closed | 787 |

| 915 | **[Audit→Fixed]** `AudioRing` capacity is now rounded **up to a power of two** in a single `roundedCapacity()` helper used by both `layout()` and `bytesFor()` ([AudioRing.h](mu-core/Link/AudioRing.h#L50-L77)), so the monotonic uint32 index always wraps seamlessly across the 2³² boundary regardless of the requested size (the shipped 8192 is unchanged; any future non-power-of-two request is made safe instead of silently corrupting after ~2³² frames). Test added: `prepare(2,100)` → capacity 128, still round-trips. | ✅ Closed | 787 |

| 914 | **[Audit→Fixed]** the transport seqlock `readTransport()` spin is now **bounded** (`kMaxSpins=4096`) and fails safe to a stopped snapshot if the writer is stuck odd (mu-link server died mid-write) ([MuLinkProtocol.h](mu-core/Link/MuLinkProtocol.h#L91-L116)) — the client's render-ahead thread can no longer hang there, so `detach()`/`stopThread` always completes and the bridge's stall watchdog detaches cleanly. Test pins the stuck-odd → `playing=0` fail-safe. | ✅ Closed | 787 |

| 906 | **Compiler warning: MSVC C4996 'createWriterFor' deprecated overload — mis-attributed; real sites migrated to the modern API** Investigated the reported C4996 at `HarnessMain.cpp:132`. **The attribution was wrong on two counts:** (1) [HarnessMain.cpp:132](mu-link/Source/Tools/HarnessMain.cpp#L132) already uses the modern `createWriterFor(std::unique_ptr<OutputStream>&, AudioFormatWriterOptions)` overload (the lvalue `std::unique_ptr` binds the non-deprecated virtual; the deprecated `OutputStream*` overloads aren't even viable — a `unique_ptr` lvalue can't implicitly convert to a raw pointer), and a fresh `/W4 /diagnostics:column` recompile of `mu-link-harness` in **both** Debug and Release emits **0 warnings**. (2) The only genuine deprecated 6-arg `createWriterFor(OutputStream*, sr, ch, bits, {}, 0)` calls were elsewhere and already wrapped in `JUCE_BEGIN/END_IGNORE_WARNINGS_MSVC(4996)` (so they suppressed, not emitted, the warning) — in [tools/wavetable-gen/WavetableGen.cpp:145](tools/wavetable-gen/WavetableGen.cpp#L145) and [mu-tant/Source/Tests/SynthDSPTests.cpp:138](mu-tant/Source/Tests/SynthDSPTests.cpp#L138)+[:162](mu-tant/Source/Tests/SynthDSPTests.cpp#L162). **Fix (eliminate deprecated usage rather than hide it):** migrated all three real call sites to the modern `AudioFormatWriterOptions` overload (mirroring [RenderMode.cpp:259](mu-clid/Source/Plugin/RenderMode.cpp#L259)) — raw `new FileOutputStream`/`new MemoryOutputStream` + manual `delete` replaced with `std::unique_ptr<juce::OutputStream>` (writer takes ownership on success), and the three `JUCE_*_IGNORE_WARNINGS_MSVC(4996)` guards deleted. `mu-tant-wavetable-gen` + `mu-tant-tests` rebuild clean at `/W4`, 0 warnings; **mu-tant 127/127 green** (incl. the two migrated WAV-loader tests). No deprecated `createWriterFor` call remains in the tree. | ✅ Closed | 786 |

| 904 | **mu-link Stage L7: external MIDI-clock sync (slave mode) — performance-critical** mu-link can now slave its master clock to incoming **MIDI clock**, selectable via a manual GUI toggle, without inheriting MIDI jitter — amends locked decision #4 (master-only) to master **or** external-MIDI-slave. **How it stays rock solid:** raw F8 pulses are never the timebase; new pure [MidiClockEstimator.h](mu-link/Source/Clock/MidiClockEstimator.h) is a **tempo PLL** — each F8 (24 ppqn) gives an instantaneous BPM from its interval, a one-pole filter (α=0.1, range-gated 20–400) smooths it, and only the transport *tempo* follows; the hardware frame counter remains the timebase, so clients + MIDI-clock-OUT stay sample-accurate. Handles FA/FB/FC (start/continue/stop) + Start→position-reset. [MidiClockInput.h](mu-link/Source/Clock/MidiClockInput.h) adapts a `juce::MidiInputCallback` to it (stamps pulses with monotonic hi-res time, not platform MIDI timestamps). `ServerEngine` gained `ClockSource` (Internal/ExternalMidi) — in external mode it pulls tempo/transport/reset from the estimator each block before publish/advance. `AudioServer` owns a `MidiClockInput`, registers it on the `AudioDeviceManager` for all enabled MIDI ins, exposes `setClockSource`/`externalBpm`/`externalRunning`. GUI: **Clock: Internal / Ext MIDI** toggle + MIDI-input options enabled in the device picker; external mode shows the detected BPM read-only on the tempo slider and locks the local tempo/play. Estimator unit-tested headless (converges 120→140 BPM, FA/FC transport edges) — **29/29 green**; mu-link-tests stays juce_core-only (the estimator is pure; the juce adapter lives only in AudioServer). | ✅ Closed | 781 |

| 903 | **mu-link: master safety soft-clip on the bus sum (gain-staging audit)** Audited the full mu-clid→bus gain path after a "distorted crackling" report: the path is **unity end-to-end** (bridge `onRender` → `MuLinkClient` interleave → `ServerEngine` sum), per-client + master gain default 1.0 linear, so nothing inflates the level. Gap found: the master sum had **no clip protection** — a hot client (or the sum of several) could exceed ±1.0 and hard-clip the device. Added `masterSoftClip()` in `ServerEngine`: bit-exact below a 0.8 knee (~ -1.9 dBFS), C1-continuous into a `tanh` knee that asymptotes to ±1.0, applied after master gain. Normal-level material is untouched; the bus can never hard-clip regardless of client levels. Test added (hot 2.0 → ~1.0, normal 0.5 → 0.5 transparent); two existing tests rescaled to sub-knee levels (they used 100+/1.0 just to check the sum arithmetic). 28/28 green; `verify-bus.ps1` 3/3 (tones are below the knee, unaffected). NB: the *crackling* itself is most likely Debug-build under-runs (the producer can't sustain real-time) — being verified with a deploy-free Release build; the soft-clip addresses the *distortion* half. | ✅ Closed | 780 |

Locked? Close any running …"* warning (the VST3 path was correct, using `EQUAL 0`). The files actually deployed fine (verified by MD5: built == dist for mu-Clid/mu-Tant .exe + .clap). | 890 | **docs: mu-tant hot-swap reference + deep-dive reconciliation** New [docs/mu-tant/design-hotswap.md](docs/mu-tant/design-hotswap.md) — mu-tant's APVTS-centric hot-swap in full: scope, how/why it differs from mu-clid (ValueTree payload + `replaceState` vs pre-built `VoiceEngine` + retire-tail; no `suspendProcessing`/blanket lock), the threading contract + readiness gate, boundary detection, the **no-blanket-lock commit + lock-discipline table** (which guard covers each mutated structure), the two-phase wavetable load (`findByPath`/`decodeFile`/`appendTable`), MIDI PC, staging badges, structural-edit cancellation, invariants, tests. Added the structural-edit-cancellation invariant to [docs/mu-clid/design-hotswap.md](docs/mu-clid/design-hotswap.md) §12 + the family [Hot-swap](docs/design-plugin-family.md) section; pointed mu-tant CLAUDE.md at the new doc.
