T12 (Karplus rings past env idle, spectral peak at C3 = 130.8 Hz) → 4/4. T13 (8-hit overlap with engine-level env retrigger) → 4/4. **Wider pattern**: this is the agreed test infrastructure for the mu-family (mu-clid → mu-tant → mu-toni). The render binary is per-plugin (each plugin links its own standalone + RenderMode); the JSON schema + analyse.py + run-listening-tests.py are plugin-agnostic and will move to a shared location during the mu-core extraction. **Trade-off**: only catches OBJECTIVE regressions ("Karplus tail audible at t=2s"); subjective sound quality still needs human ears, but the bulk of "did our DSP change break the audio shape" is now automated. Debug + Release built clean at 611. | ✅ Closed | 611 |

| 648 | **[Default rhythm RhythmCircle (main panel + sidebar mini) drew no hits on a fresh standalone open; audio played the pattern correctly]** Root cause: the audio thread only writes `lastEuclidOverrides[r]` inside the `runModulationPass` block, which is gated on `matrixHasAssignments \|\| prevMatrixHadAssignments[r]` ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:458-462](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L458-L462)). For a rhythm with no modulation assignments — i.e. the default rhythm on startup — that branch never runs, so `lastEuclidOverrides[0]` stays at the C++ default `EuclidGenOverrides{}` (hits=0, rotate=0…). [Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp:499-500](Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp#L499-L500) (and [Source/UI/SidebarItem.cpp:81](Source/UI/SidebarItem.cpp#L81)) fetched the overrides via `proc.getModulatedEuclidOverrides(...)` and called `r.genA.getStepTypes(ov.a)`, which passes `ov.hits=0` into `EuclideanGenerator::generate` → empty pattern. The audio thread, meanwhile, plays the rhythm using `r.genA.hits=4` directly, so the audio was correct while the visual was blank. Loading a preset masked the bug because the preset's recently-active modulation pass had populated the overrides; resetting to default broke it again. **Fix**: [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.h:276-303](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.h#L276-L303) `getModulatedEuclidOverrides(int)` now returns the rhythm's base genA/B/C values when the modulation matrix has no assignments, falling back to `lastEuclidOverrides[r]` only when modulation is actually live. Added a `const Rhythm& getRhythm(int) const` overload to [Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.h:34](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.h#L34) + [.cpp:83-87](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp#L83-L87) and forwarded it through [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.h:134](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.h#L134) so the const `getModulatedEuclidOverrides` can read the rhythm without violating const-correctness on the SidebarItem's `const PluginProcessor*` handle. **Wider pattern**: any future "UI reads modulated state" path should similarly fall back to base values when modulation isn't running — `lastEuclidOverrides` is a *live-modulated* snapshot, not a *canonical view*. The comment in `getModulatedEuclidOverrides` documents the gotcha. **Regression test**: open standalone with a fresh state (no preset loaded) → confirm the default 16-step / 4-hit pattern shows 4 hits on the outer ring in both the main RhythmCircle and the SidebarItem mini-circle. Add a hit count change via knob → confirm ring updates immediately. Assign a Uni mod to euclid.a.hits → confirm #642's modulated-arc behaviour still works. 0 failures across 19 test classes. Debug + Release built clean at 610. | ✅ Closed | 610 |

| 647 | **[Standalone — audio output device choice not persisted across launches; reverted to Windows default each open]** [Source/Plugin/StandaloneApp.cpp:122-130](Source/Plugin/StandaloneApp.cpp#L122-L130) `shutdown()` now explicitly calls `mainWindow->pluginHolder->saveAudioDeviceState()` BEFORE destroying the window and saving `appProperties`. Root cause: JUCE's `StandalonePluginHolder` writes the `audioSetup` XML key into the supplied PropertySet only on explicit `saveAudioDeviceState()` calls (which fire when the Audio/MIDI Settings dialog closes after a user change) — closing the standalone window without ever opening that dialog never triggers a save, so the device choice from `setupAudioDevices()`'s defaults-fallback path is what gets persisted… i.e. nothing. Pre-fix `~StandalonePluginHolder()` does NOT auto-save (verified by reading the JUCE source); the holder destructor only does `stopPlaying() + deletePlugin() + removeAudioCallback`. Forcing the save in `shutdown()` captures the currently-active device unconditionally. Then `appProperties.saveIfNeeded()` flushes the `.settings` file to disk. On next launch `setupAudioDevices()` finds the `audioSetup` key and initialises `deviceManager` with the user's last device. **Regression test**: open standalone, change audio device via the Audio/MIDI Settings dialog → confirm device works → close standalone → reopen → confirm the same device is selected. Repeat without opening the settings dialog (using the default device) — confirm it persists too. Debug + Release built clean at 610. | ✅ Closed | 610 |

| 646 | **[T12 fix-forward — signal chain reordered to `sample → filter → ampEnv → insert → output`; feedback-based inserts (Karplus, Vocoder, etc.) ring past env idle from their own internal state]** Andy's T12 finding ("output of Karplus is being shortened by the amp env") exposed that #627's post-insert env-gate cut intentional FX tails. Andy's chosen design: amp env sits BETWEEN filter and insert. Filter resonance / comb feedback in the filter stage stays env-gated (T11 behaviour preserved); insert FX live AFTER the env-gate, receive env-shaped input but their own state (delay-line feedback, etc.) decays at the FX's natural rate. Changes: (1) [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:223-232](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L223-L232) `ampEnv.applyEnvelopeToBuffer` moved before `insertProc.process`. (2) Header comment block at [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:180-196](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L180-L196) rewritten to describe the new chain + retire-drain reasoning. (3) Retired-engine drain extended: new `int retireDrainBlocks` member on VoiceEngine ([Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h:135-141](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h#L135-L141)), `markRetired()` sets it to ~2 s worth of process() blocks ([Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:268-270](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L268-L270)), `isFullyDrained()` ([Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:285-291](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L285-L291)) now requires both env-idle AND drain-counter-exhausted before reporting drained — gives Karplus / feedback FX time to decay audibly before engine destruction during hot-swap. **#416 leak still solved**: filter resonance in the retired engine still fades with env release (env-gates the filter), so it can't leak into the next active rhythm. Only the INSERT can ring after env idle, but its input is 0 (filter output is env-gated), so the ringing is bounded by the insert's own feedback decay (Karplus loopGain capped at 0.9999 — decays well within 2 s for typical settings). **Wider pattern**: the env-gate position is now a deliberate architectural choice ("env gates filter, not insert"). Any future insert algorithm with internal feedback inherits the "rings past env idle" property automatically. **Regression test**: T12 retest at 609 — Karplus 80% feedback / 300 ms decay → ringing extends past env release. T11 retest — filter resonance still fades with env release (no regression). 0 failures across 19 test classes. Debug + Release built clean at 609. **Design doc** [docs/design-627-filter-then-amp.md](docs/design-627-filter-then-amp.md) updated with the revision note at the top. | ✅ Closed | 609 |

| 645 | **[Crash — switching the MAIN (master-bus) Insert algorithm crashed the host; root cause = dangling reference capture in `MixerChannel::bindMaster`]** Reproduce: 6 rhythms playing, master Insert slot 1 = EQ, change algorithm to Compressor → host terminates. Andy captured the VS call stack — top frame at [Source/UI/MixerChannel_Bindings.cpp:295](Source/UI/MixerChannel_Bindings.cpp#L295) inside the `charBox.onChange` lambda invoked from `ComboBox::handleAsyncUpdate`. **Root cause**: the outer `wireInsertSlot(int slot)` lambda computed two local pointers (`snaps` → `insertSnapshots`/`insertSnapshots2`, `snapValid` → `insertSnapshotValid`/`insertSnapshotValid2`) via a ternary on `slot`, then bound `charBox.onChange = [this, proc, slot, &snaps, &snapValid, pSlot](){...}` — the inner lambda captured those locals BY REFERENCE. Once `wireInsertSlot(0)` and `wireInsertSlot(1)` returned (synchronously, two calls back-to-back), the stack frames holding `snaps`/`snapValid` were destroyed, leaving dangling references inside both `charBox.onChange` slots. Switching algorithm fired the lambda, dereferenced the dangle (`snaps[oldChar][s] = ...`), wrote into whatever stack memory had been reused → access violation. Manifested NOW because Step 0 of #598 ([v1.0.607](Source/UI/Voice/AmpSubsection.cpp)) shifted enough stack/binary layout that the previously-by-luck-still-valid memory got clobbered. Pre-existing bug, not introduced by Step 0 — but Step 0 was the catalyst. **Fix**: capture by VALUE — both are pointers (cheap to copy), so `[this, proc, slot, snaps, snapValid, pSlot]()`. Comment in [Source/UI/MixerChannel_Bindings.cpp:277-282](Source/UI/MixerChannel_Bindings.cpp#L277-L282) records the rationale so the bug doesn't return. **Wider pattern audit**: searched every `onChange =` / `onValueChanged =` lambda in `Source/UI/` for `&local` captures. The other `&state` / `&engine` / `&apvts` / `&k` captures all reference function parameters that the caller owns (long-lived members of MixerChannel / MixerEngine / APVTS / KnobWithLabel) — those don't dangle. This was the only instance. **Regression guard**: code-review rule documented in the comment — lambdas bound into long-lived `std::function` callback slots must capture computed-pointer locals by VALUE; reference captures are only safe for function-parameter references that the caller guarantees to outlive the binding. Static analysis (compile-time) would need `-Wdangling-reference` (GCC 13+, not available on MSVC) or Clang lifetime annotations; runtime AddressSanitizer would catch it but isn't part of the test rig. Debug build confirmed clean compile of the fix (standalone link locked by Andy's debugger session at the time of build; other artefacts deployed). | ✅ Closed | 608 |

| 644 | **[Stage 34 closure — VoiceEngine signal flow reworked to filter-then-amp (#627); per-voice ampEnvs collapsed to a single engine-level ampEnv; markRetired no longer resets filter/insert state — FX tails (filter resonance, comb feedback, reverb-style inserts) now ring naturally through hot-swap]** Per the plan in [docs/design-627-filter-then-amp.md](docs/design-627-filter-then-amp.md). Pre-fix the audio chain was: per-voice (sample → ampEnvs[i] applyEnvelopeToBuffer → mix) → shared filter → shared insert → output * ampLevel * accentGain. The final mix bypassed amp env entirely, so a high-feedback filter or sustained insert could self-feed past the env; #416 had to forcibly reset that state on retire to kill the "comb-filter overlay" symptom — at the cost of all legitimate FX tails. **New flow** ([Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:177-225](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L177-L225)): voices render raw sample audio additively into tempBuffer (no per-voice env shaping) → shared filter → low-cut → insert → engine-level `ampEnv.applyEnvelopeToBuffer(tempBuffer)` → `output.addFrom(..., ampLevel * accentGain)`. The env-gate at the END naturally drains filter/insert residual ringing when env hits idle, so [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:233-253](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L233-L253) `markRetired()` removes the `voiceFilter.reset()` / `lowCutFilter.reset()` / `insertProc.reset()` calls — filter + insert state survive the retire and ring through the env release. **Architecture change**: `ampEnvs[MaxVoices]` (per-voice envelope array) collapsed to a single `juce::ADSR ampEnv` ([Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h:93-104](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h#L93-L104)). The `voiceBuffers[MaxVoices]` per-voice scratch array was also removed — voices now write directly into the shared tempBuffer. `trigger()`, `syncEnvelopes()`, `isFullyDrained()` all updated. **Trade-off**: per-voice envelope independence is gone — rapid retriggers reset the engine env (no separate release tail on a still-decaying earlier hit). Acceptable for drum-style trigger model + pattern legato (#419) handles the pad case. **Wider pattern**: "amp env is the gate for ALL post-env audio" is now a design rule for the voice chain. Closes #627. 125/125 tests pass. Debug + Release built clean at 606. **Listening regression tests**: see new T11 / T12 / T13 in the Tests section. | ✅ Closed | 606 |

Save paths at [Source/Plugin/PresetIO.cpp:684](Source/Plugin/PresetIO.cpp#L684) (single-rhythm) and [Source/Plugin/PresetIO.cpp:1075](Source/Plugin/PresetIO.cpp#L1075) (full preset) no longer write the `presetVersion` property. Debug + Release built clean at 605. **Note**: when distribution starts, the version gate will need to come back (or a tagged-release format added). | ✅ Closed | 605 |

| 642 | **[Visual — Euclidean rhythm circles (main panel + sidebar mini) did NOT reflect modulation of hits/rotate/prePad/postPad/insSt/insLen; the underlying played pattern DID change but the user saw no visual feedback]** Pre-fix `RhythmCircle::setPatterns` was called only on user knob changes or rhythm switch, passing `r.genA.getStepTypes()` (BASE step types, no override applied). Modulation wrote to `lastEuclidOverrides[r]` and through `tryUpdatePatternFromModulation` into `safePatterns[r]` (which the sequencer plays from), so the AUDIO was correct — but the visual rings never moved. **Fix**: (1) Added override-aware `HitGenerator::getStepTypes(const EuclidGenOverrides&)` ([Source/Sequencer/HitGenerator.h:51](Source/Sequencer/HitGenerator.h#L51), [Source/Sequencer/HitGenerator.cpp:154](Source/Sequencer/HitGenerator.cpp#L154)) that uses the override values for hits/rotate/prePad/postPad/insertStart/insertLength (step count, mute, and pad-mode flags stay on the generator). The original `getStepTypes()` now delegates to this — single source of truth. (2) Exposed `PluginProcessor::getModulatedEuclidOverrides(int r)` ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.h:276-284](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.h#L276-L284)) — returns a struct copy of `lastEuclidOverrides[r]` for UI threads to read. (3) `RhythmPanel::refreshCircle` ([Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp:495-503](Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp#L495-L503)) now passes overrides through to `getStepTypes`, with a poll in `timerCallback` that detects override changes and re-refreshes the circle. (4) `SidebarItem::timerCallback` ([Source/UI/SidebarItem.cpp:73-100](Source/UI/SidebarItem.cpp#L73-L100)) extended with the same override comparison alongside the existing base-signature check, using override-aware `getStepTypes(ov.X)`. `RhythmSidebar::refreshItems` now calls `item->setProcessor(&proc)` so each sidebar item can fetch overrides ([Source/UI/RhythmSidebar.cpp:33](Source/UI/RhythmSidebar.cpp#L33)). **Race-condition note**: UI reads `lastEuclidOverrides` without a lock — torn reads on the 6-int struct are possible but benign for visuals (worst case: one frame of slightly-inconsistent ring). The audio path (`safePatterns`) is properly locked via `patternLock` so playback is unaffected. **Regression test**: assign Uni mod to euclid.a.hits with depth = 50, run sequencer → confirm both the main RhythmCircle's outer ring AND the sidebar mini-circle show the hits moving in sync with the audio. Repeat for rotate / prePad / postPad / insSt / insLen across rings A/B/C. 125/125 tests pass. Debug + Release built clean at 603. | ✅ Closed | 603 |

| 641 | **[Mod compliance audit — all euclid pattern destinations were non-compliant with the "50% mod = 50% knob turn" spec; 6 destinations corrected]** Systematic audit of every mod destination against Andy's design rule "modulation = controlling the knob, depth = knob turn proportion". 19 destinations checked. **13 compliant** (amp.*, filter.*, pitch.semi/oct/envDepth, fenv.*, insert.p1..p4 — all updated through #633/#638/#639/#640). **6 non-compliant fixed here**: (1) `euclid.*.prePad` + `euclid.*.postPad` had depthScale 6 on a 0..12 slider — only swept half range at full mod. Bumped to 12 ([Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp:84-87](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L84-L87)). (2) `euclid.*.insLen` had depthScale 4 on a 0..8 slider — bumped to 8. (3) `euclid.*.hits` + `euclid.*.rotate` + `euclid.*.insSt` had fixed depthScale 8 but the slider range is DYNAMIC (depends on the rhythm's step count). Converted these three to PROPORTION-SPACE modulation: seed = base/steps ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:516-535](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L516-L535)), depthScale = 1.0, write-back = round(proportion × steps) ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:679-700](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L679-L700)). Now 100% mod = 100% slider sweep regardless of step count (8 / 16 / 32 step patterns all behave identically per the depth knob). The previous "halved scales for less saturated feel" was a UX compromise that contradicted the design rule — user can dial depth down for subtler movement instead. **Wider pattern**: any future modulation destination with a dynamic slider range must use proportion-space + dynamic seed/write-back. Linear sliders with fixed range use additive-in-display with scale = range. Skewed sliders use proportion-space with scale = 1.0. **Regression test**: assign Uni + 50 depth to euclid.a.hits on patterns with 8 / 16 / 32 steps — confirm the arc shows 50% knob turn in all three cases. Repeat for prePad / postPad / insLen. 125/125 tests pass. Debug + Release built clean at 602. | ✅ Closed | 602 |

| 640 | **[Pitch ranges corrected — octave ±3 (was ±4), fine ±100 cents in 1-cent steps (was ±99 in 0.1-cent steps); combined max static pitch shift is ±4 octaves with engine-side clamp]** Per Andy's design spec: pitch.octave = ±3 octaves + pitch.semitones = ±1 octave (±12 semis) → combined static max = ±4 octaves. pitch.fine = 100 cents each way, stepped in single cents. [Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp:42-44](Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp#L42-L44) slider ranges updated. [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp:105-107](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp#L105-L107) APVTS params updated (pitchOct ±3 int, pitchFine ±100 int). [Source/Persistence/RhythmParamTable.h:122,126](Source/Persistence/RhythmParamTable.h#L122) `apply()` clamps updated: pitchOctave ±3, pitchFine ±100. [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:164-168](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L164-L168) — added `juce::jlimit(-48, 48, ...)` on `baseSemitones` so the combined pitchOctave×12 + pitchSemitones + pitchFine/100 saturates at ±4 octaves (Andy: "we accept that at full 4 octave change, adding with fine will be clamped"). [Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp:78](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L78) pitch.octave depthScale 96 → 72 (= ±3 octaves × 2 × 12 semis = full slider range, matches "50% mod = 50% knob turn" spec). [Source/Tests/RhythmParamBoundaryTests.cpp:86-93](Source/Tests/RhythmParamBoundaryTests.cpp#L86-L93) updated for new ±3 range. **Preset note**: existing `.muRhyth` / `.muclid` presets that stored pitchOct = ±4 will clamp to ±3 on load (per memory: library is throwaway test material, no migration needed). 125/125 tests pass. Debug + Release built clean at 601. | ✅ Closed | 601 |

| 639 | **[Mod arc — pitch.semitones with negative depth flipped direction depending on knob position (T6 finding); filter.cutoff still used multiplicative-in-octaves and didn't satisfy Andy's "50% mod = 50% knob turn" spec]** Two issues consolidated under the same design rule. (1) **pitch.semitones**: the snapshot stored only the OFFSET as a 0..1 proportion (with midpoint = no offset), but the UI's `setModulatedNorm(snap)` then compared this to `setNorm = (base + 12) / 24`. When base was negative (e.g. -12), the offset's normalised midpoint (0.5) sat ABOVE setNorm (0.0), so a negative-mod arc rendered upward. Fix: snap stores `modParams.pitchSemitones + modParamValues["pitch.semitones"]` (the ACTUAL modulated semitone value), UI uses `setModulatedActual` ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:570](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L570), [Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp:198](Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp#L198)). Same fix pattern as pitch.octave (#636). (2) **filter.cutoff** switched from multiplicative-in-octaves to proportion-space modulation: matches Andy's design rule that "50% mod at full = 50% knob turn" (multiplicative-in-octaves gave variable knob-turn depending on base position). Seed via new `propFromCutoff` ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:489-491](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L489-L491)), write-back via `cutoffFromPropWB` ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:638](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L638)), snapshot via `cutoffFromProp`. `isLogHzDest` emptied (kept for future log-Hz destinations). (3) **depthScaleFor spec compliance**: bumped `pitch.semitones` 12→24 and `pitch.octave` 36→96 (semitones) so full src + full depth = full slider turn (previously was half / 37.5% of range). Andy's design rule: "modulation = controlling the knob — 50% mod = 50% knob turn". Linear-slider destinations (resonance, accentDb, fenv.depth, pitch.envDepth) verified already satisfying the rule (their scales = display range). [Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp:74-78](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L74-L78). **Regression test**: T6 — sweep base pitch.semitones from -12 to +12 with Uni + -50 depth, confirm arc consistently BELOW needle and same length at each base position. Same for filter.cutoff swept across 20 Hz to 20 kHz. Debug + Release built clean at 600. | ✅ Closed | 600 |

| 638 | **[Mod arc — visual arc length varied with knob position on skewed-slider destinations (T6 root cause); switched amp.atk/dec/rel + fenv.atk/dec + filter.lowCut + amp.level to PROPORTION-SPACE modulation]** Symptom (Andy on T6): with Amp env decay, as the knob is turned up, the modulation arc length DECREASES. Same depth setting reads as different arc lengths at different base positions — also true for any skewed-slider destination. **Root cause**: pre-fix modulation was additive in display units (seconds for ADSR times, Hz for low-cut, gain for amp.level), but the corresponding sliders are SKEWED — the same display-unit delta covers a different visual proportion of the knob at different positions. At high knob positions, the skew compresses the display range, so the same absolute delta = smaller visual arc. **Fix**: for skewed-slider destinations, seed modParamValues with the slider's PROPORTION (0..1), apply modulation additively in proportion-space (depthScale = 1.0), then convert back via the slider's inverse skew at write-back. Same depth now produces the same visual arc length AND the same perceptual audio change (skew-space is close to log-time perception for ADSR, log-Hz for low-cut, linear-dB for amp.level). Affected: `amp.attack/decay/release` + `fenv.attack/decay` (skew 0.3 on 0..10 s), `filter.lowCut` (skew 0.35 on 0..1000 Hz), `amp.level` (linear -60..+6 dB but stored as 0..2 gain — mod was in gain units, switched to dB-proportion). [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:474-492](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L474-L492) seed via `propFromAdsr/propFromLowCut/propFromAmpLvl` lambdas, [.cpp:540-555](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L540-L555) snapshot via `adsrFromProp/lowCutFromProp/dbFromProp`, [.cpp:629-645](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L629-L645) write-back via `adsrFromPropWB/lowCutFromPropWB/gainFromPropWB`. depthScaleFor returns 1.0 for these destinations ([Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp:62-67](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L62-L67)). **Wider pattern**: any future modulation destination whose slider has a non-identity skew should use proportion-space mod. Linear sliders (resonance, sustain, accent display, env-depth display, semitones) keep additive-in-display mod since their proportion IS the display. **Regression test**: T6 — Uni + ±50 depth on amp.decay; sweep base from 0.1s to 9s, confirm arc length stays roughly constant (was decreasing pre-fix). Debug + Release built clean at 599. | ✅ Closed | 599 |

Debug + Release built clean at 598. | ✅ Closed | 598 |

| 636 | **[Mod — pitch.octave silently modulated (no live arc) → wired to the pitchOctave knob via setModulatedActual (#629 follow-up from T5 testing)]** Pre-fix [Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp:186-194](Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp#L186-L194) explicitly disabled the indicator on the pitchOctave knob (`setIsModulated(false)`, `setModulatedNorm(kNaN)`) — assigning a CS to `pitch.octave` gave audible modulation but zero visual feedback. | 633 | **[Mod — Bitcrusher (and ALL insert algorithms) modulation was effectively BINARY because `depthScaleFor("insert.pN")` fell through to the default 100 instead of returning 1.0 — T5 critical bug discovered when Andy tested Bitcrusher]** Root cause: Stage 36 (#611) collapsed insert destinations from semantically-named (insert.drive / .bits / etc., 100 / 1 / 24 etc. scales) to four generic slots (`insert.p1..p4`) stored in `voiceParams.insertParam[]` as NORMALISED 0..1. The depth-scale table in [Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp) was never updated for the new generic names — `depthScaleFor("insert.p1..p4")` fell through to the 0..100 default. Result: `amount = src × depth × 100 × 0.0001 = src × depth × 0.01` was in [0..100] units, added to a normalised 0..1 value, then `juce::jlimit(0.0f, 1.0f, ...)` saturated to 1.0 (or 0.0 for negative depth) for any non-trivial mod. Modulation was effectively binary on EVERY insert algorithm — Bitcrusher, Karplus, EQ, all algos. Fix at [Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp:74-75](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L74-L75) — explicit case returning 1.0 for insert.p1/p2/p3/p4. Full-depth modulation now spans the full normalised 0..1 range, which each algo's `normToActual` denormalises into its slot's actual range + skew. **Regression test**: T5 — for each insert algorithm, confirm Uni + 50 depth on any visible slot produces a smooth modulation (not a binary jump to max/min). | ✅ Closed | 597 |

Side effect: the Logic rect's right edge (= padX) sits 0 px from the Legato rect's left edge (= padX) — they share a vertical line. That mirrors how the Euclid block's right edge meets the Pad rect's left edge above (where the touching is invisible because the Euclid block has no border). The Legato-to-Mono gap is now `kPadInsertGap` (6 px, matching the Pad-to-Insert gap above) instead of the prior `kLogicGapW` (8 px). **Wider pattern**: vertical alignment between rows is a strong visual cue; any row layout should reuse the dominant row's column constants rather than recomputing its own widths from scratch. **Regression test**: visual — each Logic-row sub-panel border lines up pixel-for-pixel with the corresponding boundary in the Euclid row above. Debug + Release built clean at 595. | ✅ Closed | 595 |

| 631 | **[UI — Logic-row buttons (dropdown + Trig/Leg pills + Poly/Mono pills) had visibly uneven vertical spacing above vs below; equalised by shifting pills + sub-panel rects down by `kLogicVOffset = 3` px]** Pre-fix: pills were placed at `y + 3` inside the kLogicH=24 band, which sits in the inter-row gap between the Pad A sub-panel rect (bottom at y_pad+68) and the Euclid B label/Pad B rect (next row's content starts ~24 px below the band's top). Gap above/below pills now ~7 / ~9 px (close enough that the visual asymmetry is gone); rect bottom may sit 1 px past the next row's label baseline but the label text is mostly above the line so no visual collision. **Wider pattern**: any "row sandwiched between two labelled rows" needs a similar `kRowVOffset` that accounts for the next row's label height eating into the below-gap. **Regression test**: visual — Logic-row buttons sit visibly centred between the Pad sub-panel rects above and below. | 626 | **[Audit — Phase D deep-dive of Stage 34 seamless hot-swap; assessment of problem solved + fix-forward success + new issues introduced]** Audited the full Stage 34 implementation (#413/#414/#415/#416/#417) end-to-end per Andy's request. **Original problem (per [docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md](docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md))**: hot-swap during playback cut the old engine mid-sample, producing audible clicks on sustained material. **Architecture chosen**: extend `voiceEngines[r]` from single-owner to active + N retired tails (N=4 per slot). Old engine moves into a retired slot at swap commit, keeps rendering its in-flight sample / amp env tail; when fully drained, audio thread flags it for message-thread destruction. **Assessment of success**: (1) **Problem partially solved** — sample + amp env tails DO continue naturally past swap (the primary user-facing complaint is gone for percussive material). (2) **FX tail TRUNCATED** — #416's filter/insert reset trade-off sacrifices resonant filter rings + comb-filter / reverb-style insert tails to fix the never-drain + filter-self-feed bugs. Documented as a new Open issue #627 for a Stage 35+ proper fix (reorder amp-env application so it gates ALL post-env audio). (3) **Suspend gap (~1.33 ms)** still present per design — Step 4 (atomic-pointer swap) was deliberately deferred as optional optimisation. Acceptable on percussive material per docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md, "occasionally audible on sustained pads" per CLAUDE.md. **Fix-forwards quality assessment**: (1) **#416** is a SOLID fix — found two compounding root causes (drain-never-fires due to ADSR.isActive() semantics on a drum-style trigger model that never noteOff's; filter/insert state self-feeds independent of amp env) and addressed both. The trade-off it introduced (FX tail truncation) is the lesser evil — without #416 the swap-tail was unusable (overlay artefact on every swap). (2) **#417** is a SOLID fix for a pre-existing latent bug that was MASKED by the never-drain bug. Once #416 made engines drain, ampRelToEnd's "let sample play through unscaled" intent broke because the env was never noteOff'd in normal play either. Cleaned up. **New issues found by this audit**: (a) #627 — FX tail truncation (above). (b) **ampRelToEnd retired engines have ad-hoc drain semantics**: [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:284-285](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L284-L285) special-cases "voices-finished alone" for the retired ampRelToEnd path, bypassing the standard env-idle check. Consistent with the design (amp env never reaches idle in that mode), but the special case is the kind of code that drifts if the env model changes. Worth a comment that ties it to #417's logic. (c) **Tests 3.1–3.4 verification status unknown**: CLAUDE.md Stage 34 row says "Awaiting user re-verification of Test 3.1 after #416, plus Tests 3.2–3.4" — these are the back-pressure / stop-during-retire / 8-rhythm-stress listening tests. Could not be auto-verified. **Conclusion**: Stage 34 is FUNCTIONALLY COMPLETE for its narrow original scope (sample + amp env tails). The hot-swap experience is significantly better than pre-Stage-34 for percussive material. The FX-tail limitation is the only remaining "this should also work" gap, logged as #627. Recommend marking Stage 34 as Done in CLAUDE.md after Andy's manual Tests 3.2–3.4 verification, with #627 carried into the next stage as a follow-up enhancement. | ✅ Closed | 592 |

| 625 | **[Bug — Modulation snapshot/UI range mismatch across 7 destinations (Phase C audit follow-up to #623): fenv.atk/dec/depth, amp.level, accentDb, pitch.envDepth all had the same snap-vs-slider unit mismatch as amp.atk/dec/rel]** Found during the Phase C deep-dive that #623 triggered. Pattern: snapshot at [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:518-567](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L518-L567) stored a value pre-normalised against the modParamValues unit space (e.g. 0..48 semis for fenv.depth, 0..2 gain for amp.level, 0..12 dB for accentDb) but the UI slider uses different display units (0..100% for fenv.depth/accentDb/pitch.envDepth, dB for amp.level) and sometimes also a skew (0..10s skew 0.3 for fenv.atk/dec). Snap normalised to one range while `slider.valueToProportionOfLength(slider.getValue())` ran the SLIDER's range/skew → arcs drifted from the needle. Fixed by converting each snap to the slider's actual unit space and routing through `setModulatedActual` in the corresponding subsection: [Source/UI/Voice/AmpSubsection.cpp:243-256](Source/UI/Voice/AmpSubsection.cpp#L243-L256) (level + accent), [Source/UI/Voice/FilterSubsection.cpp:263-271](Source/UI/Voice/FilterSubsection.cpp#L263-L271) (fenv.atk/dec/depth), [Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp:194](Source/UI/Voice/PitchSubsection.cpp#L194) (pitch.envDepth). **Wider pattern**: any new mod destination must store snapshot value in SLIDER UNITS (not voiceParams units) and the UI must use setModulatedActual. The cleanest enforcement would be a small `MOD_SNAPSHOT(snap_idx, slider_value_expr)` macro that asserts ranges in debug, but that's a refactor for later. **Regression test**: visual — assign Uni CS with depth=+50 to each of fenv.atk/dec/depth, amp.level, amp.accent, pitch.envDepth; confirm arc only goes ABOVE the needle. Debug + Release built clean at 592. | ✅ Closed | 592 |

| 624 | **[Audit — Phase C deep-dive of modulation rings + ranges (Andy-initiated, follow-up to #623); also documents the broader insert + euclid snapshot patterns + identifies one remaining issue]** Done as part of the post-#623 sweep. Audited every entry in the snapshot block at [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:518-593](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L518-L593): (1) **Fixed in #623/#625**: amp.atk/dec/rel, fenv.atk/dec/depth, amp.level, accentDb, pitch.envDepth (see those entries). (2) **Verified correct**: filter.cutoff (#612 — actual Hz + setModulatedActual via slider midPoint skew), insert.p1..p4 (Stage 36 — `mu_ui::normToActual(norm, algo, slot)` matches the slider's per-slot skew exactly), amp.sustain + filter.resonance (linear 0..100 sliders, snap matches), pitch.semitones (linear -12..+12 slider, snap matches). So if you route a CS to pitch.octave the knob has NO visual feedback — silent modulation. | 623 | **[Bug — Modulation arc on Amp Env Decay sweeps BELOW the base value with a unipolar modulator + positive depth — root cause: snapshot range mismatch with the skewed 0..10 s slider; same bug affected amp.atk + amp.rel]** Root cause analysis (matches #612 filter-cutoff pattern exactly): `snap[kSnapAmpDec].store(sn(modParamValues["amp.decay"], 0.0f, 100.0f))` at [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:528](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L528) assumed a 0..100 range, but `modParamValues["amp.decay"]` is in the × 33.33 scaled form (0..333) AND the UI slider uses 0..10 seconds with `setSkewFactor(0.3)` ([Source/UI/Voice/AmpSubsection.cpp:47](Source/UI/Voice/AmpSubsection.cpp#L47)). For typical decay times (0.3 s), the snap value was ≈ 0.1 while the slider's `valueToProportionOfLength(0.3)` with skew 0.3 returned ≈ 0.39 — so the modulated arc started 0.39 (the needle) and ended 0.1 (the bogus snap) drawing the arc visually BELOW the needle. Fix: store the ACTUAL seconds value in the snapshot (× 0.03 to invert the scaling), let the UI's `setModulatedActual` route through the slider's own valueToProportionOfLength so the arc respects the skew by construction. Same pattern applied to amp.attack + amp.release ([Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:527-531](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L527-L531), [Source/UI/Voice/AmpSubsection.cpp:243-256](Source/UI/Voice/AmpSubsection.cpp#L243-L256)). **Wider pattern triggered Phase C deep-dive** (see #624) which uncovered + fixed the same class of bug in fenv.atk/dec/depth, amp.level, accentDb, pitch.envDepth (see #625). **Regression test**: visual — Uni CS with depth=+50 on amp.decay produces an arc ABOVE the needle only; Bi + ±50 covers both sides; depth=0 produces no visible arc. Manual verification at v1.0.592 required. Debug + Release built clean at 592. | ✅ Closed | 592 |

[Source/UI/EuclideanPanel.cpp:495-507](Source/UI/EuclideanPanel.cpp#L495-L507) (`resized()` Logic-row block) + [Source/UI/EuclideanPanel.cpp:566-583](Source/UI/EuclideanPanel.cpp#L566-L583) (`paint()` border block) now compute `subPanelW = (rowW - 2 * kLogicGapW) / 3` and lay out Logic / Legato / Mono at that equal width. | 621 | **[UI — Logic OR/AND/XOR/A not B/B not A converted from 5-pill SegmentControl to DropdownSelect; placed FIRST in the logic row]** [Source/UI/EuclideanPanel.h:69](Source/UI/EuclideanPanel.h#L69) `SegmentControl logicCtrl` → `DropdownSelect logicCtrl`. | 612 | **[Bug — Filter Cutoff modulation arc appeared to invert direction below vs above the slider midpoint; same mod amount visually went "negative" at low cutoff and "positive" at high cutoff]** Root cause: the snapshot for `kSnapFilterCutoff` was pre-normalised via a pure-log curve (`snLogHz(v) = log(v/20) / log(1000)`) but the slider uses `setSkewFactorFromMidPoint(640)` which is a different mathematical shape (power-law). These two curves agree at the midpoint (~640 Hz) but diverge everywhere else — at 43 Hz, snLogHz says 0.111 while the slider's `valueToProportionOfLength` says 0.259. The mod arc drew between those two proportions, appearing to extend counterclockwise from the needle at low cutoff and clockwise at high cutoff. Fix: [Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.h](Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.h) + [.cpp](Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.cpp) added `setModulatedActual(float actualValue)` which routes through `slider.valueToProportionOfLength(...)` — the SAME path as the needle's baseAngle in paintOverChildren, so the arc proportion always matches the visual slider scale by construction. [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp) snapshot for `kSnapFilterCutoff` now stores the ACTUAL Hz value (clamped to 20..20000). [Source/UI/Voice/FilterSubsection.cpp](Source/UI/Voice/FilterSubsection.cpp) `refreshModulatedIndicators` calls `filterCutoff.setModulatedActual(...)` (the other four filter knobs stay on `setModulatedNorm` — their sliders use linear-matched normalisation). Same fix applied to the four insert P1-P4 snapshots: [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp) now stores the per-algo denormalised actual via `mu_ui::normToActual(insertParam[N], algo, N)`; [Source/UI/Voice/InsertSubsection.cpp](Source/UI/Voice/InsertSubsection.cpp) routes via `setModulatedActual` — covers Log-skew LPF, IntStep Note / Wave, Linear Drive, etc. uniformly. 119/119 tests pass. Debug + Release built clean at 587. | ✅ Closed | 587 |

| 585 | **[Bug — Modulation indicator arc now respects slider skew; no longer draws through the needle on log/skewed knobs]** [Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.cpp](Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.cpp) `paintOverChildren()` — the live mod arc previously computed `baseAngle` from a LINEAR proportion `(value - min) / (max - min)`, but the slider's needle visually sits at `valueToProportionOfLength(value)` which respects the knob's skew (`setSkewFactor` / `setSkewFactorFromMidPoint`). Fix: use `slider.valueToProportionOfLength(slider.getValue())` for `setNorm` so `baseAngle` lines up with the visible needle. The modulator-snapshot side (`modulatedNorm`) is the actual UI-domain proportion already (snapshot lambdas in [Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:506-540](Source/Plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp#L506-L540) normalise to 0..1 with destination-appropriate curves), so no change needed there. 120/120 tests pass. | 583 | **[Bug — `LFOEditor` displayed Smooth-mode curves at 1% of intended height because it treated `CurvePoint::y` as -100..+100 while the DSP and on-disk format use -1..+1]** [Source/UI/Components/LFOEditor.cpp:25-42](Source/UI/Components/LFOEditor.cpp#L25-L42) `toScreen` divided by 200, `fromScreen` multiplied by 200 — so a curve with `y = ±1` (the canonical range used by [Source/Sequencer/ControlSequence.cpp:75-127](Source/Sequencer/ControlSequence.cpp#L75-L127) `evaluateSmooth`, which multiplies `y * 100` before returning to the matrix's -100..+100 contract) drew within ½ % of the centre line — visually flat. Conversely, any curve the user *did* edit in the LFOEditor would have stored `y ∈ -100..+100` and produced 100× the intended modulation. Fix wraps the display in the data range: bipolar `screenY = (1 - (y+1)/2) * h`, unipolar `screenY = (1 - y) * h`; matching inverse in `fromScreen`. The DSP path and on-disk schema are unchanged. Confirmed against [Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp:201](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L201) which documents CS-output range as -100..+100. Symptom that surfaced this: Tape Bend preset's sawtooth-like 4-point curve drove `insert.drive` correctly (cyan modulation ring visible) but rendered as 4 dots on the zero line in the LFOEditor. | ✅ Closed | 576 |

| 544 | **[Bug — EqInsert rewritten with per-sample-smoothed biquad coefficients; zipper noise on Mid-Hz sweep eliminated]** [Source/Audio/FX/Insert/EqInsert.h](Source/Audio/FX/Insert/EqInsert.h) replaced the JUCE `IIR::Filter` cascade (block-rate coefficient swap) with three custom `SmoothBiquad` instances per channel (6 total). Each `SmoothBiquad` carries five `juce::SmoothedValue<float, Linear>` members for its `b0/b1/b2/a1/a2` coefficients, all ramped over 15 ms. Per block: target coefficients are computed from the user knob values via the RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook formulas (peak / low shelf / high shelf) and pushed to the smoothers' `setTargetValue`. Per sample: each coefficient's `getNextValue` is read inside the biquad evaluation (transposed direct form II), so the filter response moves smoothly between samples — coefficient changes never step at block boundaries. First-block-after-prepare uses `setCurrentAndTargetValue` so the EQ snaps to its target response on initial use rather than ramping up from passthrough over 15 ms. Stability: peak/shelf at the Q values used (0.7–1.0) and the user-reachable gain range (±18 dB) keeps poles safely inside the unit circle across every intermediate coefficient set the smoother traverses. The previous per-block-`skip(ns)` dB/Hz smoothing from the earlier fix is no longer needed — replaced by per-sample coefficient smoothing. 120/120 tests pass. Debug + Release built clean at build 567. | ✅ Closed | 567 |

| 510 | **[Bug — Karplus-Strong feedback curve changed to cubic for even perceptual spread]** [Source/Audio/FX/Insert/KarplusStrongInsert.h](Source/Audio/FX/Insert/KarplusStrongInsert.h) loop gain mapping changed from linear `fbKnob * 0.9999` to cubic `1 - (1-fbKnob)³`, capped at 0.9999. The linear mapping compressed almost all audible range into the top 20% of the knob (decay time scales as 1/log(gain), so linear spacing produces logarithmic perceptual spacing). Cubic curve spreads the range: 0%=passthrough, 25%≈125ms pluck, 50%≈500ms pluck, 75%≈4s sustain, 100%=near-infinite sustain. Debug + Release built clean. 120/120 tests pass. | ✅ Closed | 551 |

Old mapping (0.95..1.0) meant even at minimum feedback (0%) the string resonated noticeably (~300 ms decay at 48 kHz). New mapping (0..0.9999) gives: 0% = pure passthrough (no resonance), 100% = near-infinite sustain. The audibly interesting pluck range is now ~80–100 %. [Source/UI/InsertAlgoDefaults.h](Source/UI/InsertAlgoDefaults.h) Karplus first-visit default `insertDither` changed from `70.0f` to `0.0f` so the algorithm produces no resonance on first use (consistent with all other insert algorithm defaults). | 477 | **[Bug — Mixer insert algorithm clamped to Tape Sat for indices > 10]** [Source/UI/MixerChannel_Bindings.cpp](Source/UI/MixerChannel_Bindings.cpp) `loadFromAPVTS` clamped `mst_insChar` and `mst_ins2Char` APVTS values with `jlimit(0, 10, ...)`. When Vocoder St (index 13) was selected on a master insert slot, any knob interaction reloaded the algorithm display with `jlimit(0, 10, 13) == 10` (Tape Sat), visually resetting the algorithm name and applying Tape Sat defaults on top of the live audio. The upper bound of 10 matched the last algorithm when the clamp was written; Karplus (11), Vocoder (12), and Vocoder St (13) were added without updating it. | 471 | **[Bug — `loadPreset` version check runs after sequencer resize]** `requireSupportedPresetVersion` was called roughly half-way through `loadPreset`, after the sequencer had already been resized and voice engines re-created to match the incoming preset's rhythm count. A v0 preset would therefore wipe the user's existing rhythm slots (growing/shrinking the sequencer, destroying running VoiceEngine instances, clearing mixer state) before being rejected with the "legacy format" error — leaving the project in a half-loaded default state rather than the pre-load state. Fix: moved `requireSupportedPresetVersion` to the very first action inside the `MuClidPreset` branch, before any sequencer mutation. The check was previously duplicated at the old early-return site (an artefact of the code path); that duplicate was removed. Discovered after #458 rejection messages were silent/dismissed — user loaded a v0 preset, saw no audio, and had to re-add rhythms manually. | ✅ Closed | 526 |

| 470 | **[Bug — Hot-swap preset load ignores embedded sample, plays silent]** Loading a `.muRhyth` preset while the transport was playing produced UI activity (RhythmCircle animating, sequencer firing) but no audio. Root cause: [`PluginProcessor::stageRhythmPreset`](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp) (the hot-swap entry point) only read the `r0_sample` *path* property and never looked at the `<sampleData>` child element. Presets saved with `embedSample=true` (or auto-embedded via #439's temp-dir detection) write `r0_sample=""` by design — the bytes live in `<sampleData>` — so the hot-swap path silently staged a `VoiceEngine` with no sample. `applyRhythmPreset` (stopped-state entry) had handled both since #439. Fix: mirror `applyRhythmPreset`'s embedded-first / path-second policy in `stageRhythmPreset`. Also added the "linked sample missing" `onLoadError` warning when stored path + same-basename fallback both fail to resolve — previously silent, made the silent-audio case completely unexplained. Discovered by Andy mid-session loading a preset against a running transport. Built Debug + Release clean. | ✅ Closed | 525 |

| 469 | **[Audit — `VoiceSlot`/`Rhythm` copy-op gymnastics removed]** `VoiceSlot` had an explicit copy-constructor and copy-assignment operator to skip copying `mutable std::atomic<bool> modLock` (non-copyable; copies must always start unlocked). `Rhythm` had a matching pair delegating to `VoiceSlot::operator=`. Both were error-prone: any new member added to either class needed manual inclusion in four copy-op bodies. Fix: new `CopyableSpinLock` struct in [Source/Sequencer/VoiceSlot.h](Source/Sequencer/VoiceSlot.h) wraps `std::atomic<bool> v` with copy operations that always produce a new unlocked instance, and forwards `.exchange`/`.store`/`.compare_exchange_strong` so all call sites are unchanged. `VoiceSlot::modLock` type changed from `std::atomic<bool>` to `CopyableSpinLock`; both `VoiceSlot` and `Rhythm` drop their explicit copy-ops entirely (compiler-generated ops are now correct). The one site that took `&r->modLock` as `std::atomic<bool>*` ([Source/UI/ModulatorPanel.cpp:70](Source/UI/ModulatorPanel.cpp#L70)) updated to `&r->modLock.v`. `Rhythm : public VoiceSlot` inheritance preserved — composition refactor deferred (would ripple across 24 files with no functional benefit at current stage). Debug + Release built clean. | ✅ Closed | 542 |

| 446 | **[Branding bug — follow-up to #421]** Standalone window title bar showed `?-Clid` instead of `μ-Clid` (Greek lowercase mu, U+03BC, UTF-8 `0xCE 0xBC`). **Root cause:** `getApplicationName()` returned `juce::CharPointer_UTF8(JucePlugin_Name)` ([StandaloneApp.cpp:87](Source/StandaloneApp.cpp#L87)), where `JucePlugin_Name` is the macro `"μ-Clid"` defined by JUCE's CMake helper. That macro reaches MSVC via the `-D JucePlugin_Name="μ-Clid"` command-line argument — and the cmd/console host re-encodes multibyte characters through the system codepage en route, so the μ byte pair gets mojibake'd into `?` before the compiler ever sees it. Same root cause as the mojibake'd Inno-Setup console output noted in #421. **Fix:** hard-code the UTF-8 byte sequence `"\xce\xbc-Clid"` inside `getApplicationName()` so the title bytes come directly from source rather than via the CMake → MSVC `-D` round-trip. `MUCLID_LITE_BUILD` guard selects `"\xce\xbc-Clid Lite"` for the Lite standalone. Matches the existing escape used on [StandaloneApp.cpp:27](Source/StandaloneApp.cpp#L27) for the "Close μ-Clid?" dialog. Settings filename at [:76](Source/StandaloneApp.cpp#L76) (uses `JucePlugin_Name` for the `.settings` filename — only ever appears on disk, not in any user-visible chrome) left as-is — even if mangled, it just changes the filename `?-Clid.settings` which still works as a filesystem path on Windows. Built Debug + Release clean. | ✅ Closed | 513 |

| 444 | **[Phase 2 for #423 Vocoder]** Three Vocoder Phase-2 items landed. **(1) Modulation destinations — `voc.note` / `voc.octave` / `voc.unison`** added to `ModDest::kTable` ([ModulatorEditor.h](Source/UI/ModulatorEditor.h)) at indices 41–43. `ModDest::populate()` case 12 now exposes them under a "Vocoder" section heading in the destination dropdown. `depthScaleFor` ([ModulationMatrix.cpp:71-78](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.cpp#L71)) returns 6 / 4 / 6 so depth=100% × src=100% spans the full integer range (note 0..6, octave 1..5, unison 0..6). [`PluginProcessor::processBlock`](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L518) modulation pass seeds the new dest paramValues from voiceParams when `driveChar == 12` (`voc.note = drvBits - 1`, `voc.octave = drvDither`, `voc.unison = (driveOutput + 24) / 4` so the user-facing 0..6 unison index is what the matrix actually offsets); after the matrix runs, the write-back ([PluginProcessor.cpp:644-651](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L644)) clamps each back to its algorithm range and re-encodes unison (`vIdx * 4 - 24`) into the driveOutput storage. Other algorithms (driveChar != 12) pay zero matrix-process cost since their `voc.*` entries stay at 0 and the dropdown doesn't expose them. **(2) UI grey-out for noise carriers.** When Vocoder's Wave knob is set to White (2) or Pink (3), the Note / Octave / Unison knobs are now `setEnabled(false)` + `setAlpha(0.45f)` so the user can see they're inactive. Implemented in both the per-rhythm Voice page ([VoiceSection.cpp](Source/UI/VoiceSection.cpp) case 12) and the mixer master-insert page ([MixerChannel_Insert.cpp](Source/UI/MixerChannel_Insert.cpp) case 12). The Wave knob's `onValueChanged` re-runs the grey-out sync each time, so live waveshape changes update the disabled state immediately. `configureInsertAlgorithm` resets enabled=true on all four insert knobs at function entry, so switching FROM Vocoder back to a different algorithm doesn't inherit the grey state. **(3) Voice-entry gain ramp on Unison-up.** Added `voiceGainSmooth[kMaxUnisonVoices]` per-voice state to `VocoderInsert` ([VocoderInsert.h](Source/Audio/Processing/InsertFX/VocoderInsert.h)). Each sample, every voice's smoothed gain ramps exponentially (~5 ms time constant via `kEntryRampMs`) toward its target — `voiceGain[v]` for v < unisonN, 0 for v >= unisonN. The carrier sum uses `voiceGainSmooth[v]` instead of `voiceGain[v]` directly. Result: turning the Unison knob UP makes new voices fade in over 5 ms instead of snapping in at full level. Also smooths Unison-DOWN (voices that just left the active range fade out instead of cutting). `reset()` zeroes the array so `markRetired()` / hot-swap don't inherit stale gain envelopes. Pitched carriers only — the noise-carrier path doesn't use per-voice gains. Built Debug + Release clean. Phase-2 stereo-aware analysis split off as #445. | ✅ Closed | 512 |

| 430 | **[Bug — preset back-compat]** Loading any `.muRhyth` / `.muclid` preset saved before #422/#423 reinterpreted `drvChar` and `drvBits` against the new wider ranges, shifting integer algorithm selectors up. Symptom (user-reported): default preset works fine; switching to a "more complex preset" plays white-ish hash on every hit; subsequent preset switches stay noisy. **Root cause:** preset files store `param->getValue()` (normalised 0..1). When the APVTS range for `drvChar` was widened 0..10 → 0..12 in #422/#423, an old normalised 1.0 (TapeSat=10) now resolves to 12 → Vocoder. Whatever `drvDrv` (0..100) the legacy TapeSat preset held got read as Vocoder waveshape — clamped to 0..3, so anything ≥ 67 % loads as **Pink Noise carrier** = noise on every hit. Same shift applies to `drvBits` (1..16 → 0..16 in #429) and to the master inserts `mst_insChar` / `mst_ins2Char` / `mst_insBits` / `mst_ins2Bits`. The default preset works only because `drvChar=0` is a fixpoint under any range. **Fix:** added `kCurrentPresetVersion = 1` + `migrateLegacyPresetNorm(suffix, norm)` / `migrateLegacyGlobalNorm(id, norm)` helpers in [PluginProcessor_Internal.h](Source/PluginProcessor_Internal.h). All four load paths — `applyRhythmPreset` ([PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp:281](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp#L281), stopped-mode `.muRhyth`), `stageRhythmPreset` ([:32](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp#L32), playing-mode `.muRhyth` hot-swap), `loadPreset` ([:873](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp#L873), `.muclid` rhythm tree + GlobalState child) — read `state.getProperty("presetVersion", 0)`. If absent or below `kCurrentPresetVersion`, each normalised value is run through the migrator before `setValueNotifyingHost` / `convertFrom0to1`. Migration math: `drvChar` legacy → current `newNorm = oldNorm * 10/12` (so a value V in 0..10 resolves back to V); `drvBits` legacy → current `newNorm = (1 + oldNorm * 15) / 16`. All four save paths — `saveRhythmPreset`, `saveRhythmPresetToFile`, `savePreset` (the two .muRhyth writers + the .muclid writer) — now tag the file with `presetVersion = kCurrentPresetVersion`, so any preset newly saved on this build skips the migration on next load. **Host-state path (DAW project state) was already correct:** APVTS's state-tree stores de-normalised actual values, not normalised, so range widening doesn't shift values there — confirmed by inspection of `migrateLegacyHostState` and `apvts.replaceState` semantics. Built Debug + Release clean. **Test plan:** (1) open standalone, load a pre-#422 preset that used TapeSat or Limiter — should now sound correct (was: noise). (2) open standalone, switch through several pre-#422 presets — should each sound correct. (3) save a new preset, reload it — should sound correct (verifies new-format saves migrate to themselves correctly). (4) any `.muclid` full preset saved before #422 should load with correct master-insert algorithms. | ✅ Closed | 510 |

| 428 | **[#422/#423 bug fixes + deploy hardening]** Three reported bugs in the new insert effects, plus a build-script improvement. **(1) Karplus Feedback didn't reach max sustain:** loop gain was capped at 0.999 (`0.95 + fbKnob * (0.999 - 0.95)`). Bumped to reach 1.0 at full knob — the LP filter in the feedback path always removes some energy per cycle, so the loop is stable at 1.0 without explosive growth. Below 0.95 the string still dies in a few ms; above that the user now has full control over the long-sustain range. [KarplusStrongInsert.h:80](Source/Audio/Processing/InsertFX/KarplusStrongInsert.h#L80). **(2) Karplus LPF control:** previously the feedback-path LP cutoff was hardcoded at 4× target freq. Now exposed as a 4th UI knob ("LPF") wired to `driveTone` (20 Hz – 20 kHz log range, same as other inserts' LPF knob). Lower cutoff = darker / quicker decay; 20 kHz effectively bypasses the LP so the feedback gain alone shapes the envelope. UI knob added in both [VoiceSection.cpp](Source/UI/VoiceSection.cpp) and [MixerChannel_Insert.cpp](Source/UI/MixerChannel_Insert.cpp) case 11. **(3) Vocoder unison stuck at 13 voices + reset on note change:** root cause was the unison index 0..6 being stored in `driveTone`, whose APVTS range is 20..20000. When the snapshot system tried `apvtsSet("drvTon", 1.0)` for the default unison index 1, JUCE clamped to 20.0. The algorithm's `juce::jlimit(0, 6, (int)20.0)` then yielded 6 → 13 voices. Every parameterChanged-triggered `configureInsertAlgorithm` re-read this stuck 20.0 and reset the unison knob. **Fix:** moved unison storage from `driveTone` to `driveOutput` (range -24..0, which freely holds the encoded value `unisonIdx * 4 - 24`). Algorithm reads `juce::jlimit(0, 6, (int)((p.driveOutput + 24) / 4))`. UI knob value (0..6) encodes via `v * 4 - 24` on write. Frees up `driveTone` for the Note label — the existing Note storage in `drvBits` now drives the "Note" knob shown in the leftover `extra` UI slot. [VocoderInsert.h:50](Source/Audio/Processing/InsertFX/VocoderInsert.h#L50). **(4) Build-script hardening:** the OneDrive deploy step at [cmake/DeployRelease.cmake](cmake/DeployRelease.cmake) was aborting the entire build if any destination file was locked (user running the standalone, antivirus scan mid-build, OneDrive sync). Wrapped each `file(COPY_FILE)` with `RESULT` capture (and the VST3 bundle copy with `execute_process(... copy_directory)` since `file(COPY)` lacks a result-capture variant), downgrading lock-failures to warnings. The build now completes and the user gets a clear message ("close any running μ-Clid") instead of an MSB3073 wall. **Default values updated** in kInsertDefaults[11/12] in both [VoiceSection.cpp](Source/UI/VoiceSection.cpp) and [MixerChannel_Insert.cpp](Source/UI/MixerChannel_Insert.cpp): Karplus now defaults driveTone=20000 (LPF wide open); Vocoder defaults driveOutput=-20 (unison index 1 = 3 voices). Built Debug + Release clean. | ✅ Closed | 506 |

| 427 | **[Refactor]** [MultiModeFilter](Source/Audio/MultiModeFilter.cpp) migrated from a single 200-line if/else cascade over `typeCodeValue` into a class-per-algorithm dispatch table mirroring #425 / #426. New folder [Source/Audio/Processing/Filters/](Source/Audio/Processing/Filters/) contains `FilterAlgorithmBase.h` (abstract base — `prepare/reset/process(cutoffHz, resonance)`) plus 16 concrete algorithm headers — one per dropdown entry, named after what the user sees in the UI: `Lp12Filter`, `Hp12Filter`, `Bp12Filter`, `Notch12Filter`, `Lp24Filter`, `Hp24Filter`, `Bp24Filter`, `Lp6Filter`, `CombPlusFilter`, `Ap12Filter`, `Notch24Filter`, `Hp6Filter`, `PeakFilter`, `LowShelfFilter`, `HighShelfFilter`, `CombMinusFilter`. Naming policy: each file describes the FILTER TYPE, not the underlying DSP primitive — so "looking up LP24 in the code" is a direct one-step lookup (`Lp24Filter.h`) instead of "I think 24dB filters use Ladder, let me find that". Each class owns its own DSP state (`StateVariableTPTFilter`, `LadderFilter`, `BiquadFilter`, `OnePoleLP`/`OnePoleHP`, or comb delay buffer + write pointer). `MultiModeFilter` itself shrinks from 80 lines of `.h` + 200 lines of `.cpp` to 60 lines of `.h` + 65 lines of `.cpp`; it's now just an orchestrator that pre-allocates `std::array<std::unique_ptr<FilterAlgorithmBase>, 16>` in the constructor and dispatches via `algorithms[typeCode]->process(...)`. **Public API unchanged** — `prepare/reset/setType/setCutoff/setResonance/process` signatures identical, so [VoiceEngine](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp)'s `voiceFilter` member needs no edits. **Trade-off accepted:** previously SVF-family modes (LP12/HP12/BP12/Notch12) shared a single internal SVF instance — switching between them carried the integrator state across. Now each has its own SVF (and similarly each Ladder mode has its own Ladder, each biquad-mode has its own biquad). Practical effect: switching filter type mid-tone briefly loses the previous filter's state. The SVF integrators settle in microseconds, the Ladder topology smooths internally, and the comb pair share nothing anyway — so the audible difference is negligible. The win is that filter type lookup is now a 1:1 file mapping, and adding a 17th filter mode in the future is a drop-in new file + one line in the constructor + one entry in the APVTS dropdown choice list. **Per-mode coefficient-recompute skip preserved:** the #368 change-detection cache (`lastCutoffHz` / `lastResonance` per algorithm) is now per-class state instead of a shared cache on MultiModeFilter — every algorithm that benefits (Lp6/Hp6/Ap12/Peak/LowShelf/HighShelf) carries its own. `CMakeLists.txt` unchanged — `MultiModeFilter.cpp` was already on the source list; the new headers propagate via include chain. Built Debug + Release clean. | ✅ Closed | 499 |

| 423 | **[Feature]** Insert effect **Vocoder** — driveChar = 12. New class [VocoderInsert.h](Source/Audio/Processing/InsertFX/VocoderInsert.h). 20-band parallel vocoder: analysis biquad bandpass on mono down-mixed input → one-pole envelope follower (5 ms attack / 30 ms release) → multiplies a matching synthesis biquad on the carrier; band outputs summed; result broadcast to both channels. Band centres log-spaced 80 Hz – 10 kHz at Q≈5 using the project's existing `BiquadFilter` (no new DSP primitive). **Carrier:** four waveshape options (Saw / Square / White Noise / Pink Noise via Paul Kellet's filter). Pitched carriers (Saw / Square) use SPN-anchored pitch from C@Oct1=65.4 Hz (same convention as #422). **Unison:** up to 13 parallel detuned phase accumulators (1/3/5/7/9/11/13 voices) with symmetric placement around the centre frequency; spread `D(N) = 0/8/16/24/32/40/50 cents`; per-voice gain falloff `1 - 0.6 * \|pos\|/D(N)` so outer voices sit at 0.4× the centre; total output normalised by `1/sum(gain)` so loudness is consistent across unison settings. Phase-continuous oscillators mean no click on frequency change. **Param encoding (driveChar=12):** `driveDrive` = waveshape 0..3, `drvBits` = note index+1 (1..7 → C..B), `drvDither` = octave 1..5, `driveTone` = unison index 0..6. UI knobs step in integer increments and display the readable label (note letter, octave number, voice count, waveshape name) via `textFromValueFunction`. Registered in [InsertProcessor.cpp](Source/Audio/InsertProcessor.cpp) (kNumAlgorithms 11→13); dropdowns in `VoiceSection` and `MixerChannel` get a "Vocoder" item; `configureInsertAlgorithm` cases added in both. CPU is non-trivial (40 biquads + 20 envelope followers + N≤13 phase accumulators per voice per sample) — usable but a candidate for "high-CPU FX" categorisation later. Phase 2 work tracked in #423-followups: modulation destinations, noise-carrier UI grey-out, voice-entry gain ramp on Unison-up, stereo-aware analysis. Built Debug + Release clean. | ✅ Closed | 501 |

| 422 | **[Feature]** Insert effect **Karplus–Strong** — driveChar = 11. New class [KarplusStrongInsert.h](Source/Audio/Processing/InsertFX/KarplusStrongInsert.h). Classic K-S loop: short circular delay line (sized for lowest pitch C@Oct1=65.4 Hz → 1024 samples capacity at 48 kHz prepare time, so a sample-rate change up to ~89 kHz fits without realloc) plus a one-pole LP inside the feedback path. Excites with the incoming voice signal so each trigger plucks the string. Linear-interpolated fractional delay reads + `juce::SmoothedValue<float>` on `target_freq` with ~15 ms ramp means pitch changes (knob or future modulation) turn into a fast smooth slide instead of a phase-discontinuity click. **Pitch math (SPN-anchored at C=65.4 Hz for Octave 1):** notes ascend C→B chromatically with semitone offsets 0/2/4/5/7/9/11; octave-knob position N maps to SPN octave (N+1). LP cutoff in the feedback path auto-tracks at 4× target freq for natural high-frequency damping. **Param encoding (driveChar=11):** `driveDrive` = note index 0..6, `drvBits` = octave 1..3, `drvDither` = feedback 0..100% mapped internally to loop gain 0.95..0.999. UI knobs step in integers and display via `textFromValueFunction` (note letter, octave number, feedback %). Registered in [InsertProcessor.cpp](Source/Audio/InsertProcessor.cpp) (kNumAlgorithms 11→13 — shared bump with #423); dropdowns in [VoiceSection.cpp](Source/UI/VoiceSection.cpp) and [MixerChannel.cpp](Source/UI/MixerChannel.cpp) get a "Karplus" item; `configureInsertAlgorithm` cases added in both. | 420 | **[Bug]** Envelope Attack knob (and any other ADSR time knob) set to 0 visibly crept up by a tiny amount as soon as another envelope control was touched. Symptom was the slider re-displaying 0.001 instead of 0 — audio effect inaudible at that resolution, but the visual was wrong. Root cause: `applyRhythmSuffix` in [PluginProcessor_Internal.h](Source/PluginProcessor_Internal.h) applied `juce::jmax(0.001f, v)` to all six ADSR time fields (`pEnvAtk/Dec/Rel`, `fEnvAtk/Dec/Rel`, `aEnvAtk/Dec/Rel`) before writing them into `voiceParams`. The floor existed because JUCE's `ADSR::Parameters` struct rejects zero — but it was being applied in the WRONG layer (the data layer that the UI reads from). An APVTS value of 0 round-tripped through `voiceParams.ampEnvAtk` as 0.001; when an unrelated parameterChanged fired and triggered `VoiceSection::refreshSuffix`, the slider read back the floored 0.001 and visibly bumped off the floor. Fix: removed the floor from all six setters in `applyRhythmSuffix` so `voiceParams` faithfully stores the user's chosen value; moved the floor INTO `VoiceEngine::syncEnvelopes` at [VoiceEngine.cpp:288-308](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L288) where it's applied inline on each `setParameters(...)` time arg via `juce::jmax(kMinAdsrSec=0.001f, ...)`. Sustains are amplitude (not time) so they pass through unchanged — 0 sustain is a legitimate user choice (the "silence after decay" semantic, see #417). Audio-thread modulation path at [PluginProcessor.cpp:605-612](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L605) already applied the floor when building per-block `modParams` — left as-is (that path writes to a local, not back to voiceParams, so it can't cause UI creep). Built Debug + Release clean. | ✅ Closed | 490 |

| 419 | **[Feature]** Pattern-aware legato for the sequencer. **Problem:** every step that fires a hit called `VoiceEngine::trigger()` → `ampEnv.noteOn()`. The existing #221 per-envelope `ampEnvLegato` / `filterEnvLegato` / `pitchEnvLegato` flags only chose "reset env to 0 vs continue from current level" before `noteOn` — `noteOn` always fired, so Attack always restarted on every step. Effect: envelope time was capped by step length. A 4s decay could never breathe past one step before the next hit interrupted it. **Solution:** new per-rhythm **Pattern Legato** mode. When enabled, the sequencer marks "tied" hits — adjacent steps that are both hits with no rest between — and the audio engine skips the envelope retrigger on those hits. The sample voice still retriggers on every hit (rhythmic pulse preserved); a short linear fade-in ramps the sample-voice restart against the running envelope tail to avoid the waveform-discontinuity click. **Implementation:** (a) `Rhythm` gains `bool patternLegato` at [Source/Sequencer/Rhythm.h:55](Source/Sequencer/Rhythm.h#L55) (copy/copy-assign updated). (b) `BlockResult` gains `int tiedMask` at [Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.h:7](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.h#L7); always populated. (c) `SequencerEngine` tracks `wasLastStepHit[MaxRhythms]` per audio-thread state, set/cleared per step walked in `processBlock` at [SequencerEngine.cpp:283-322](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp#L283); reset to false alongside `lastStepIndex = -1` in `resetStepTrackingForSwap` / `removeRhythm` / `setNumRhythms` so post-swap / post-shrink rhythms never see a stale tied bit. (d) `VoiceEngine::trigger(bool isAccented, bool tied)` at [VoiceEngine.cpp:70-100](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L70) — when `tied` is true, skip all three `env.reset() / env.noteOn()` blocks (env continues uninterrupted); always pass `fadeInSamples` to `SamplePlayer::trigger` (64 samples ≈ 1.3 ms @ 48k for tied, 0 for untied to preserve drum transients). (e) `SamplePlayer::trigger(int fadeInSamples)` at [SamplePlayer.cpp:5](Source/Audio/SamplePlayer.cpp#L5) — publishes the fade length atomically alongside the triggered flag; `process()` applies a per-sample linear ramp `1 - remaining/total → 1.0` over `fadeInSamples` then runs at unity. (f) `PluginProcessor::processBlock` trigger call at [PluginProcessor.cpp:421-431](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L421) gates the tied bit on `getRhythm(r).patternLegato` so the flag controls the behaviour; tiedMask itself is always computed (cheap — one branch per step). (g) APVTS: new `r{i}_patLeg` boolean param registered at [PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp:99](Source/PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp#L99); push/pull wired through `kRhythmSuffixes`, `applyRhythmSuffix`, and `pushRhythmToAPVTS` so the flag persists in host state and `.muRhyth` preset files. (h) UI: new `legatoCtrl` 2-segment SegmentControl `{"Trig","Leg"}` in `EuclideanPanel`, placed FIRST on the logic row with an 8 px sub-panel divider before the existing logic pills. Layout constants (`kLegatoW`, `kLogicGapW`, `kLogicMP`) hoisted to the header so `resized()` and `paint()` stay in sync; `paint()` draws two separate rounded-rect outlines for the sub-panel look. `loadFromRhythm` + `refreshSuffix("patLeg")` keep the toggle in sync with preset loads + parameter changes. Built Debug + Release clean. **Test plan (user listening):** (1) set sustain=0, decay=4s, dense pattern with adjacent hits → with Trig: envelope retriggers every step (no decay tail); with Leg: contiguous hits keep the envelope alive so the 4s decay breathes across the run. (2) Tied hit immediately after a rest should retrigger normally (rest broke the tie). (3) Pad / pluck samples should not click on tied hits (1.3 ms fade-in does its job); transient drum sounds should remain transient when Pattern Legato is off (zero fade-in path). | ✅ Closed | 487 |

| 418 | **[Feature]** Configurable primary sample library location, separate from the My Documents content folder. **Why:** the prior default sample folder was `<Documents>/TDP/muClid/Samples` inside the content directory — designed to host factory / preset-linked material, not the user's personal sample collection. Users typically keep their library on a different drive (e.g. `D:\Samples`). **Implementation:** (a) New appSettings key `primarySampleDir` with accessor pair `PluginProcessor::getPrimarySampleDir()` / `setPrimarySampleDir()` at [PluginProcessor.cpp:1196-1224](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L1196).
