| 417 | **[Envelope bug — pre-existing, surfaced during Stage 34 listening]** With Release knob at max (`ampRelToEnd = true`), the amp envelope was being skipped entirely — not just during the release phase. Symptom: Sustain=0 + Decay=4s + a long pad sample → user expected the sample to silence after 4s of decay, but it played at full level forever. Root cause at [VoiceEngine.cpp:140](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L140): the prior gate `if (!activeParams.ampRelToEnd) ampEnv.applyEnvelopeToBuffer(...)` treated "release-to-end" as "bypass the envelope entirely" rather than its intended meaning of "let the sample play through on RELEASE instead of fading over the release time." Since this codebase never calls `noteOff` during normal play (drum-style trigger model — env holds in Sustain forever after each hit), the env's release phase only happens for Stage 34 retired engines via `markRetired()`. So the `ampRelToEnd` gate's job is to control behaviour at noteOff, not at applyEnvelopeToBuffer. Fix: unconditionally apply the envelope in `process()`. The "release-to-end" semantic now lives entirely in `markRetired()` at [VoiceEngine.cpp:165](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L165) — when `ampRelToEnd == true`, the amp env is NOT noteOff'd, so it stays at its current value (sustain level, or wherever decay left it) and `applyEnvelopeToBuffer` keeps multiplying by that level → sample plays through to its natural end at the user-set sustain volume. When `ampRelToEnd == false`, `noteOff` fires as before → env enters release → sample fades over the user's release time. `isFullyDrained()` updated at [VoiceEngine.cpp:189](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L189) to handle the new mode: for retired ampRelToEnd engines (where amp env never reaches idle because there's no noteOff), drain on voices-finished alone — the sample running out is the sole signal that the engine has nothing left to render. User's scenario after fix: trigger → attack peaks → decay over 4s down to sustain=0 → sample silent thereafter (env still ticks during sustain hold, multiplying buffer by 0). Hot-swap during decay: env continues decaying naturally; sample plays through to natural end at whatever the env value reaches; engine drains. Filter / pitch envelopes still get noteOff'd in markRetired regardless of ampRelToEnd — they don't have a release-to-end equivalent. Built Debug + Release clean. | ✅ Closed | 486 |

| 416 | **[Stage 34 Step 3 fix]** Retired engines were producing an audible "effect overlay" (comb-filter ring / bitcrusher tail) on the new active rhythm — symptom: load a comb-filter / bitcrusher preset, play, swap to a clean kick preset, the kick sounds like it's going through the previous preset's effects. Two compounding causes, both now fixed: **(1) Engines never drained.** `juce::ADSR::isActive()` returns true throughout Attack/Decay/Sustain/Release and only goes false in IDLE. The codebase never calls `noteOff()` anywhere (drum-style trigger model — sample plays through, amp env holds in Sustain forever). So `isFullyDrained()` checked `ampEnv.isActive() == false`, which was never true post-trigger → retired slot leaked, engine rendered until plugin destruction. **(2) Filter / insert state kept ringing.** `VoiceEngine::process()` applies amp env BEFORE the filter, but the final `output.addFrom(... ampLevel * accentGain)` does NOT include amp env. So a high-feedback comb filter's delay line (or compressor envelope / DC-block / bitrate-hold from the InsertProcessor) kept self-feeding into the channel buffer at full amp level even after the sample finished — independent of the amp envelope state. Fix: added `VoiceEngine::markRetired() noexcept` at [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h:50](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h#L50) / [.cpp:165](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L165). Calls `noteOff()` on amp/filter/pitch envelopes (so amp env progresses Sustain → Release → Idle and the drain check eventually fires) AND `voiceFilter.reset()` + `insertProc.reset()` (clears comb buffers, ladder/SVF state, compressor envelope, ringmod phase, DC-block, bitrate accumulators — eliminates the audible overlay without touching the SamplePlayer voices or the amp env's release phase, which together are the legitimate "sample + envelope tail" Stage 34 is supposed to give). `handleAsyncUpdate`'s retire path at [PluginProcessor.cpp:1077](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L1077) calls `oldEngine->markRetired()` BEFORE placing the engine into the retired slot (still under suspendProcessing, so direct state mutation is safe — audio thread cannot be mid-`process()`). **Secondary fix at [VoiceEngine.cpp:144-156](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L144):** when `ampRelToEnd == true`, amp env was never `applyEnvelopeToBuffer`'d → never ticked → a retired ampRelToEnd engine would sit in Release forever and never drain. Added an explicit per-sample `getNextSample()` tick gated on `retired == true` so the release progresses without applying the env to the buffer (preserves ampRelToEnd's "let the sample play through unscaled" intent for the sample audio). Built Debug + Release clean. User-facing test: 3.1 listening verification confirmed clean-kick-after-comb-preset symptom is the next thing to check. | ✅ Closed | 485 |

| 415 | **[Stage 34 Step 3]** Retire-on-swap — the actual user-facing seamless hot-swap feature. Modified `handleAsyncUpdate`'s swap-commit block at [Source/PluginProcessor.cpp:1051-1095](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L1051): the prior `voiceEngines[r] = std::move(sw.pendingVoice)` (which silently destroyed the old engine mid-render) now does retire-then-swap. The old engine is `std::move`d into a local `oldEngine`, the new engine moves into the active slot, then `oldEngine` is placed into the first empty `retiredVoiceEngines[r][i]` slot. Step 2's render loop picks it up next block and continues rendering its in-flight sample / amp envelope tail; when `isFullyDrained()` returns true, the audio thread sets the cleanup flag and the next `handleAsyncUpdate` destroys it off the RT thread. Back-pressure: all 4 retired slots full → force-cut by overwriting slot 0 (matches pre-Stage-34 abrupt-cut behaviour for that one engine; system stays stable on spam-swap). The displaced slot's cleanup flag is store-released to `false` so a stale ready-flag can't trigger a wasted suspend+move on the freshly placed engine. Frozen retired state preserved by the existing design: only `voiceEngines[r]` (the active slot) gets `setActiveParams` / `trigger` / `setParams` / `loadFile`, so retired engines never see parameter writes, MIDI triggers, or APVTS sync. `oldEngine` nullness is guarded — Lite build (where `voiceEngines[r]` is always null pre-swap) skips the retire path cleanly. Effect on user-facing behaviour: load a long-sustain preset (pad, drone, long crash) while playing → click a different preset; the old sample audibly continues playing into the new rhythm's hits instead of being abruptly cut at the loop boundary. The `suspendProcessing` silence gap (~1.33 ms at 48k/64) still creates a single-block pause in the retired engine's mid-sample playback, which is Step 4's optional optimisation; in practice imperceptible on percussive material and only occasionally audible on sustained pads (matches the trade-off documented in CLAUDE.md). Built Debug + Release clean, no warnings. Test gates: Test 3.1 (long-sample swap during playback), 3.2 (spam-swap back-pressure), 3.3 (stop during retire), 3.4 (8-rhythm stress) — all require user listening verification; per the plan they're not unit-testable. Plan: [docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md](docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md). | ✅ Closed | 484 |

| 414 | **[Stage 34 Step 2]** Retired-engine infrastructure (slots + render loop + cleanup drain, no retire-on-swap yet — that's Step 3). Added per-rhythm retired storage to PluginProcessor at [Source/PluginProcessor.h:213-225](Source/PluginProcessor.h#L213): `kMaxRetiredEngines = 4`, `retiredVoiceEngines[MaxRhythms][4]` (`std::unique_ptr<VoiceEngine>`), and parallel `retiredReadyForCleanup[MaxRhythms][4]` (`std::atomic<bool>`). C++17 `std::atomic<bool>` default ctor leaves the value indeterminate, so the PluginProcessor ctor now stores `false` into every flag unconditionally (also outside the LITE guard so Lite's handleAsyncUpdate can't ever read an indeterminate atomic). MixerEngine gained an optional `const RetiredVoices*` parameter ([Source/Audio/MixerEngine.h:10-22](Source/Audio/MixerEngine.h#L10)) carrying a flat row-major matrix of engine ptrs + cleanup flags + perSlot count — taking `.data()` of the outer std::array's first inner array yields the contiguous start of the 2D matrix that the audio thread indexes as `[r * perSlot + i]` (std::array of std::array has no inter-row padding). MixerEngine's Phase 1 voice loop ([MixerEngine.cpp:107](Source/Audio/MixerEngine.cpp#L107)) now iterates retired slots immediately after the active engine and BEFORE `applyGain(kHeadroomTrim)`, so retired tails ride the same channel fader / pan / sidechain / sends / inserts as the active engine. After each retired `process()`, `isFullyDrained()` is checked; true → flag store-released so the message thread can destroy the engine off the RT thread. ProcessorBase::processCoreBlock forwards the descriptor through ([ProcessorBase.h:30](Source/ProcessorBase.h#L30) / [.cpp:18](Source/ProcessorBase.cpp#L18)). PluginProcessor::processBlock builds the descriptor once per block from the 2D arrays' `.data()` pointers ([PluginProcessor.cpp:704-712](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L704)). handleAsyncUpdate gained a cleanup-drain block at the top that scans `retiredReadyForCleanup` for set flags; if any, suspendProcessing fences the audio thread, the engines are moved out into local unique_ptrs (audio thread sees nullptr next block), the flags are cleared (release), suspendProcessing resumes, and the local container destructs at scope exit — fully off the audio thread. Empty-fast-path: the scan returns false in zero retired engines so suspendProcessing is skipped entirely (which is every block in Step 2 — nothing populates retired slots until Step 3 — and the steady state in later steps once tails have drained). Defensive prepareToPlay loop re-prepares any populated retired engines on sample-rate / block-size changes (no-op in Step 2). Built Debug + Release clean, no warnings. Behaviour unchanged per Test 2.1 (no populator yet). Plan: [docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md](docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md). | ✅ Closed | 483 |

| 413 | **[Stage 34 Step 1]** Foundation for seamless hot-swap with polyphonic voice tail — added `bool VoiceEngine::isFullyDrained() const noexcept` at [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h:39](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.h#L39) / [VoiceEngine.cpp:168](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L168). Returns `true` only when every `SamplePlayer` voice is inactive (`playPos < 0` AND no pending trigger — `SamplePlayer::isActive()` already encapsulates both) AND `ampEnv.isActive()` is false (JUCE's idle/post-release state). `noexcept`, no side effects, no state mutation — purely an inspection that an audio-thread caller can run each block on retired engines without risking allocation or a parameter touch. No callers in this commit by design: Step 1 is foundation-only, behaviour unchanged. Step 2 wires the retired-engine slots + render loop; Step 3 wires retire-on-swap (the actual feature). Built Debug + Release clean, zero warnings. Plan: [docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md](docs/design-seamless-hotswap.md). | ✅ Closed | 477 |

Now cued at the loop boundary like every other preset-load path. `stageRhythmPreset` takes the immediate-apply branch when stopped, so stopped behaviour is unchanged. Fix at [Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp:368-378](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp#L368). | ✅ Closed | 471 |

| 404 | **[Audit]** **MED** — Removed dead audio-thread allocation in `VoiceEngine::process`. The "defensive grow" at [Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp:121-122](Source/Audio/VoiceEngine.cpp#L121) was unreachable in practice: `ns` is already clamped to `tempBuffer.getNumSamples()` at the top of `process()` (line 106), and both `tempBuffer` and `pitchRatioBuffer` are sized from the same `blockSize` argument in `prepareToPlay`. So `pitchRatioBuffer.size() < ns` was always false. Audit removed the dead `assign()` and added a comment explaining the size-coupling invariant — eliminates the latent Tier 2 hazard that would have fired if the surrounding clamp ever regressed. | ✅ Closed | 469 |

| 403 | **[Audit]** **MED** — `std::string` temporaries from `modParamValues[]` lookups eliminated. Changed the map type from `std::unordered_map<std::string, float>` to `std::unordered_map<std::string_view, float>` at [Source/PluginProcessor.h:325](Source/PluginProcessor.h#L325). All write/read sites in `processBlock` use `const char*` string literals (`modParamValues["amp.attack"]`) which have static storage — `string_view` of a literal is alloc-free and the literal's lifetime exceeds the map's. Previously each `operator[]` constructed a temp `std::string`, heap-allocating for keys >15 chars (MSVC SSO limit) — affected ~30 of the 38 keys, ~20 k allocs/sec on the audio thread at 44.1k/64. Updated `ModulationMatrix::process` signature ([Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.h:50](Source/Modulation/ModulationMatrix.h#L50)) to match. `find(a.destinationId)` still works because `std::string` converts implicitly to `string_view`. `workMap` inside ModulationMatrix stays as `unordered_map<string, float>` — its keys are concatenated at runtime (`cs.id + "_output"`) so `string_view` of a temp would dangle. | ✅ Closed | 469 |

| 402 | **[Audit]** **HIGH** — `EffectSlot::setAlgorithm` no longer allocates on the audio thread. Previously `make_unique<ChorusEffect>()` etc. plus `make_unique<OversampledProcessor>(1)` were called from `syncFXParam` → `setAlgorithm`, which `parameterChanged` can fire on the audio thread when a DAW automates `eff_algo` (per #354 — DAW automation runs `parameterChanged` on whatever thread called `setValueNotifyingHost`, often the audio thread). Fix: pre-allocate all 4 algorithms (Chorus / Flanger / Phaser / Echo) in the `EffectSlot` ctor at [Source/FX/EffectSlot.cpp:5-15](Source/FX/EffectSlot.cpp#L5), store as `std::array<std::unique_ptr<EffectAlgorithmBase>, kNumAlgorithms>`, and prepare all of them together in `prepare()`. `setAlgorithm(index)` now just flips `algorithmIndex` — single `juce::jlimit` clamp, no allocation. `processReturn` / `setParam` dispatch through `currentAlgorithm()` which indexes the array. State carries over between activations (minor click possible on swap) which is acceptable vs the audio-thread `new` it replaces. `ReverbSlot::setAlgorithm` re-audited and found NOT to allocate — it uses one Signalsmith reverb instance with a parameter-snapshot pattern (#358); the audit's original "same risk" claim was incorrect. | ✅ Closed | 469 |

| 401 | **[Audit]** `RhythmPanel::parameterChanged` did an O(N=31) linear scan of `kEuclidSuffixes` for every parameter change. Fired on every host-automation event + every knob drag tick. Fix: introduced static `isEuclidSuffix(const juce::String&)` at [Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp:18-33](Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp#L18) backed by a lazy-init `std::unordered_set<std::string_view>` built once from the existing `kEuclidSuffixes` table. `juce::String::toRawUTF8()` returns a pointer into the String's storage (no copy) — the `string_view` wraps it for an O(1) hash lookup. Suffixes are ASCII so UTF-8 ≡ char bytes. The `parameterChanged` call site now reads `if (isEuclidSuffix(suffix))` instead of the inline 8-line loop. The register/deregister sites still iterate the table directly (they need the full list, not just membership), so the const char* table stays. | ✅ Closed | 465 |

| 400 | **[Audit]** SettingsOverlay master vol knob used linear 0..1 with no skew or dB display, while the MixerChannel master fader is a tall linear strip with a live dB readout (`updateDbLabel` at [Source/UI/MixerChannel.cpp:585](Source/UI/MixerChannel.cpp#L585)). Same APVTS param (`mstr_lvl`, registered linear 0..1 at [Source/PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp:240](Source/PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp#L240)) — the underlying scale matched, but the small rotary knob compressed the useful -6..0 dB range into the top quarter of rotation. | 399 | **[Audit]** SettingsOverlay master vol knob comment said "centred horizontally within the column to feel anchored" but the code anchored it at the column-left edge — looked off-balance under a centred section divider line. | 398 | **[Audit]** Magic numbers in `SettingsOverlay::resized()` (`80, 60` master-vol size, `90, 8` folder button width + gap, `26, 70` close button, `12` label-to-control gap) moved to named `constexpr` in [Source/UI/SettingsOverlay.h:66-73](Source/UI/SettingsOverlay.h#L66) alongside the existing layout constants: `kMasterVolW/H`, `kCloseBtnW/H`, `kFolderBtnW`, `kFolderBtnGap`, `kLabelCtrlGap`. `paint()`'s hint-position calculation now uses `kLabelCtrlGap` instead of two more hardcoded `12`s. | 397 | **[Audit]** SettingsOverlay constructor had four near-identical 5-line label setup blocks (text + font + colour + justification + addAndMakeVisible) — 20 lines of boilerplate. | 396 | **[Audit]** Standardised all atomic declarations on `std::atomic<T>` — the codebase had been mid-migration with adjacent fields using `juce::Atomic<T>` (RhythmPlayState fields, beatFraction/sequencerPlaying/lastBeatPos, midiClockIsPlaying/midiClockBpmEst, modSnapshot, mixer/insert peaks + GR) and `std::atomic<T>` (numActiveRhythms, swapModeAtomic, multiBusEnabled, pendingSwap atomics, internalPlaying/internalBeatPos). Migration spanned 11 files: PluginProcessor.h, Audio/InsertProcessor.h, Audio/MixerEngine.h, UI/MixerChannel.h+cpp, UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.h+cpp, UI/RhythmCircle.h+cpp, UI/SidebarItem.h+cpp. Mechanical replace: declarations `juce::Atomic<T>` → `std::atomic<T>`; write sites `.set(v)` → `.store(v)`; read sites `.get()` → `.load()`. Default seq_cst ordering preserved (matches `juce::Atomic` semantics — no behaviour change). Function signatures that take pointers/refs to atomics (`SidebarItem::setPlayState`, `RhythmCircle::setPlayState`, `MixerChannel::bindRhythm/bindReturn`, `KnobWithLabel::setGRSource`) updated end-to-end. | ✅ Closed | 467 |

| 395 | **[Audit]** Consolidated four near-identical "select rhythm + refresh chrome" blocks in `PluginEditor.cpp` (preset load, new preset, sidebar reorder, add rhythm) into a single `selectRhythmAndRefresh(int idx, bool fullSidebarRefresh, MixerRefresh mixerRefresh)` helper at [Source/PluginEditor.cpp:285-300](Source/PluginEditor.cpp#L285). Three-state `MixerRefresh` enum (`Skip` / `RefreshOnly` / `FullReload`) captures the per-site variation cleanly — preset loads and reorders need `FullReload` (loadFromAPVTS rebuilds the mixer's APVTS-backed state), add-rhythm only needs `RefreshOnly` (no APVTS state changed). Replacing the four call sites removed ~12 lines of duplication and made the per-site variation explicit at the call. Future call sites can't silently skip the mixer reload step. | ✅ Closed | 465 |

| 394 | **[Audit]** UAF risk in `PluginEditor` callbacks — `processorRef.onSaveAndQuit` captured raw `[this]` but wasn't cleared in the editor dtor. In a DAW close-window-keep-plugin scenario the processor outlives the editor, and a deferred host-shutdown `onSaveAndQuit` invocation would UAF into the destroyed editor. Fix: dtor now nulls every `processorRef.on*` callback (`onRhythmHotSwapCommitted` + `onSaveAndQuit`) with a comment reminding future contributors to mirror the pattern when adding new callbacks. `onContentDirChanged` / `onMidiPresetsClicked` etc. are settings-overlay-owned, not processor-owned, so they're scoped to the overlay's lifetime and don't need this treatment. | ✅ Closed | 463 |

| 393 | **[Audit]** `pushRhythmToAPVTS` fires APVTS broadcasts → `RhythmPanel::parameterChanged` marshals each via `juce::MessageManager::callAsync` (#354). The marshalled `refreshSuffix` calls were landing AFTER `handleAsyncUpdate`'s #386 `onRhythmHotSwapCommitted` callback had already re-bound the panels via `setRhythm()` — so each of ~30 queued per-param refreshes re-ran `setValue` on already-bound sliders. Pure waste per swap commit. Fix: added early-out `if (proc.isApvtsLoading()) return;` at the top of `RhythmPanel::parameterChanged` ([Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp:496](Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp#L496)). During the bulk push, listeners skip per-param refresh entirely; the #386 callback's `setRhythm()` (called inside the same scope, now under the same `ScopedApvtsLoading` guard as the APVTS push, see #391/#392) handles the full panel re-bind. Same gating now also covers state-restore and swap-rhythms-reorder paths — three call sites that previously fired a UI-refresh storm now no-op cleanly. | ✅ Closed | 465 |

| 392 | **[Audit]** `handleAsyncUpdate` called `suspendProcessing(true/false)` INSIDE the per-rhythm loop — a MIDI program-change burst hitting multiple slots could stall the message thread for ~80 ms (8× 1–10 ms suspends back-to-back) and produce N audible dropouts. Plus `sequencer.getRhythm(r) = sw.pendingRhythm` was a copy-assign that deep-copied every modulator + control sequence vector under the suspend. Fix: restructured into three passes at [Source/PluginProcessor.cpp:951-1005](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L951): (1) collect all ready slots into a stack-allocated `std::array<int, MaxRhythms>`; (2) ONE `suspendProcessing(true)` → swap them all (with `std::move(sw.pendingRhythm)` instead of copy) → ONE `suspendProcessing(false)`; (3) post-commit APVTS push + `onRhythmHotSwapCommitted` callback for each, all under ONE `ScopedApvtsLoading` guard (so every panel's `parameterChanged` sees `apvtsLoading=true` throughout — see #391/#393). Single-swap case (the common path) pays the same suspend cost as before; multi-swap case (MIDI burst) collapses to one suspend instead of N. | ✅ Closed | 465 |

| 391 | **[Audit]** `apvtsLoading` was a plain `bool` written on the message thread and read by `parameterChanged` listeners which can fire on the audio thread (DAW host automation, per #354). True cross-thread access with no atomic semantics. Worse, the `apvtsLoading = true; ...work...; apvtsLoading = false;` pattern at 6 sites was non-RAII — if anything in the push threw, the flag latched true and ALL subsequent parameter changes silently dropped their engine syncs. Fix: (a) declared `apvtsLoading` as `std::atomic<bool>` at [Source/PluginProcessor.h:283](Source/PluginProcessor.h#L283); (b) added `bool isApvtsLoading() const noexcept` public accessor for UI listener gating (used by #393); (c) added `mu_pp::ScopedApvtsLoading` RAII guard at [Source/PluginProcessor_Internal.h:16-32](Source/PluginProcessor_Internal.h#L16) that stores true in the ctor and false in the dtor with `memory_order_release`; (d) replaced all 6 set/clear pairs across PluginProcessor.cpp / PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp / PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp with `{ mu_pp::ScopedApvtsLoading guard(apvtsLoading); ...work... }` scope blocks. Read site at `syncRhythmParam` now uses `apvtsLoading.load(std::memory_order_acquire)`. | ✅ Closed | 465 |

| 390 | **[Audit]** Renamed inner variable `p` → `param` in `masterVolKnob.onValueChanged` lambda at [Source/UI/SettingsOverlay.cpp:17](Source/UI/SettingsOverlay.cpp#L17). The outer `proc` is a reference member but the ctor parameter is also `p`, so `auto* p = proc.apvts.getParameter(...)` shadowed nothing concrete at runtime — but reading the lambda meant mentally distinguishing the ctor-param `p` from the local `p`. The rename removes the cognitive overhead. | ✅ Closed | 463 |

| 389 | **[Audit] HIGH** — `stageRhythmPreset` (hot-swap-while-playing) silently dropped modulator state from the loaded preset. `applyRhythmPreset` (stopped path) at [Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp:281-285](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp#L281) deserialised the preset's `Modulators` child into the target rhythm; `stageRhythmPreset` (playing path) at [Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp:32-119](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp#L32) had no equivalent block. Result: hot-swapping a rhythm preset while playing kept the previous rhythm's modulator assignments + control sequences in place, overlaid on the new rhythm's voice/pattern params. A preset designed with a specific LFO modulating cutoff arrived with the wrong LFOs. Behaviour silently differed depending on whether the user was stopped or playing at load time. Fix: replicated the `if (auto mods = state.getChildWithName("Modulators"); mods.isValid()) { clearModulators(newRhythm); deserialiseModulators(mods, newRhythm); }` block in `stageRhythmPreset`, populating `newRhythm` before the `pendingRhythm = std::move(newRhythm)` commit. Safe because `newRhythm` is a local copy — `VoiceSlot`'s copy ctor explicitly leaves `modLock` at its default-initialised `false` ([Source/Sequencer/VoiceSlot.h:27-33](Source/Sequencer/VoiceSlot.h#L27)), so the spin-acquire inside the modulator helpers resolves on the first attempt with no contention against the live rhythm's audio-thread reader. Legacy `.muRhyth` files with no `Modulators` child are left alone (same opt-in policy as `applyRhythmPreset`). Sibling issue noted for follow-up: `applyDefaultRhythm` calls `applyRhythmPreset` directly regardless of play state — should also route via `stageRhythmPreset` for consistency. | ✅ Closed | 461 |

| 388 | Window minimum size raised from 780×580 to 1024×720 (build entry). The prior floor let the user drag the window small enough that the Mixer's channel strips overlapped, the Voice section's knob columns squashed into each other, and the rhythm panel's circle + euclidean panel collided. Min width derivation: sidebar (82) + rhythm-panel content (circle ~220 + euclidean grid + voice knob row) ≈ 940 → 1024 leaves breathing room. Min height: transport (36) + status (20) + sample bar (32) + circle row (250) + voice section (240) + modulator (80) ≈ 660 → 720 leaves a 60 px buffer. Aspect (1.42:1) close to default 1170×870 (1.34:1) so the layout doesn't have to stretch awkwardly at min. Updated `setResizeLimits` in [Source/PluginEditor.cpp:278](Source/PluginEditor.cpp#L278) and the spec line in [docs/design-ui.md:12](docs/design-ui.md#L12). Default opening size unchanged. | ✅ Closed | 459 |

| 387 | Settings overlay visual polish — the prior layout looked ad-hoc: 10 pt section headers, orphaned Master Vol knob at the top-left with no section, controls running to the full window width, "(host rescan required)" hint floating awkwardly, and a brittle layout where section heading Y values in `paint()` had to be hand-mirrored from `resized()` — easy to break on edits. Redesigned [Source/UI/SettingsOverlay.cpp](Source/UI/SettingsOverlay.cpp): (a) introduced a `LayoutY` struct + `computeLayout()` helper that's the single source of truth for both `resized()` (sets control bounds) and `paint()` (draws section headers). (b) Centred content column with `kContentMaxW = 620` cap so settings don't sprawl across wide windows. (c) Six labelled sections — Audio, Hot-swap, MIDI Clock, MIDI Program Change, Output, Content Folder — each with a 13 pt bright-text header and a thin divider line, in place of the previous 10 pt grey section labels. (d) Consistent 26 px row height with label-right / control-left layout at fixed widths (kLabelW=140, kControlW=220). (e) Master Vol knob now lives under an "Audio" section header instead of floating. (f) Section labels simplified ("Timing" / "Source" / "Messages" instead of "Hot-swap timing:" / "Clock source:" / "MIDI messages:") since the section header already provides context. (g) Content Folder path takes its own full-width row; Browse / Default buttons right-aligned on the row below at consistent 90 px width. (h) Rescan hint repositioned to sit vertically centred next to the multi-bus toggle rather than awkwardly above. (i) Close button vertically centred in the 44 px header bar. Constants moved into the header as `kSectionGap`, `kSectionHeadH`, `kRowH`, `kRowGap`, `kLabelW`, `kControlW`, `kContentMaxW`. | ✅ Closed | 457 |

| 386 | Hot-swap commit didn't refresh the rhythm name label (and other non-APVTS UI state) — symptom: load a new rhythm preset while playing; the sound swaps correctly but the name label still shows the old rhythm's name (e.g. "Kick" instead of "Crushed Snare"). Loading while stopped worked because `RhythmPanel`'s preset-dropdown `onChange` handler at [Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp:317-329](Source/UI/RhythmPanel.cpp#L317) takes the stopped branch and calls `setRhythm(currentRhythmIndex)` directly, which re-binds the name label + sample bar + sub-panels. The playing branch only stages the swap and bails out — relying on `pushRhythmToAPVTS`'s parameter-change broadcasts to refresh the UI. But `rhythm.name` / `rhythm.colourIndex` / `loadedSamplePaths` aren't APVTS parameters, so the listener path skips them entirely. Fix: added `std::function<void(int)> PluginProcessor::onRhythmHotSwapCommitted` at [Source/PluginProcessor.h:154](Source/PluginProcessor.h#L154), fired from `handleAsyncUpdate` at [Source/PluginProcessor.cpp:980](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L980) immediately after the APVTS push. Wired in `PluginEditor` ctor at [Source/PluginEditor.cpp:140](Source/PluginEditor.cpp#L140): if the swapped rhythm is the one currently displayed, re-call `rhythmPanel.setRhythm(r)` (re-binds name + sample + sub-panels); always repaint the sidebar (its items show name + colour); refresh `mixerOverlay` if visible (channel strips show rhythm names). UAF guard: editor dtor clears the callback at [Source/PluginEditor.cpp:275](Source/PluginEditor.cpp#L275) because the processor outlives the editor in DAW close-window-keep-plugin scenarios. Added `RhythmPanel::getCurrentRhythmIndex()` accessor. | ✅ Closed | 454 |

| 385 | Hot-swap commit dropped the first hit of the cued rhythm — symptom: queue a rhythm B from the browser while A is playing; at the loop boundary B swaps in correctly, but B's first audible hit is one (or several) steps later than expected. Root cause: the absorb-the-current-step logic in `SequencerEngine::processBlock`'s snapshot pass at [Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp:226-228](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp#L226) was written generically for "any update that sets `patternUpdated[r]=true`," intended to guard mid-step knob changes from retroactively firing the in-progress step. Hot-swap commit at [Source/PluginProcessor.cpp:968](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L968) calls the same `sequencer.updatePattern(r)`, so the snapshot pass treated the step-aligned swap identically to a mid-step knob change and absorbed B's first step. But the swap IS step-aligned (cued at the wrap, committed under `suspendProcessing`) — there's no retroactive-trigger risk to guard against. Fix: (a) added `SequencerEngine::resetStepTrackingForSwap(int r)` at [Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.h:65](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.h#L65) which sets `lastStepIndex[r] = -1` (the same sentinel #384 introduced for cold-start). Safe to call from message thread because `handleAsyncUpdate` already holds `suspendProcessing(true)` — audio thread is paused. (b) simplified the snapshot guard from `!(effectiveStep==0 && lastStepIndex==-1)` to just `lastStepIndex[r] != -1` (the cold-start case is a strict subset — if lastStepIndex is -1 we never want to absorb regardless of effectiveStep). (c) `handleAsyncUpdate` calls `resetStepTrackingForSwap(r)` immediately after `sequencer.updatePattern(r)` inside the suspendProcessing block. Result: the new pattern fires its step at the commit `effectiveStep` (instead of the next-step-after). One residual artifact NOT addressed: the OLD pattern still fires its step 0 at the wrap, because wrap-detect happens in the same audio block where the OLD step-walk processes the wrap and triggers the old voice engine; the async commit lands a few blocks later. Eliminating that requires synchronous-on-audio-thread commit (deferred OLD-VoiceEngine destruction, message-thread cleanup queue) — invasive, not done here. So user hears: OLD-step-0 at the boundary (small unavoidable artifact), then NEW-step-K cleanly (K = effectiveStep at commit, typically 1-3 steps post-wrap depending on message-loop latency). | ✅ Closed | 453 |

| 384 | First-play step 0 absorbed by the pattern-update snapshot — root cause of the bulk of #280's "~500 ms before first sound" complaint. Trace: `addRhythm` calls `updatePattern` which sets `patternUpdated[r]=true`. On the very first `processBlock` after launch, `SequencerEngine::processBlock`'s snapshot pass at [Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp:212-228](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp#L212) saw `patternUpdated[r]=true`, snapshotted `cachedPatterns→safePatterns`, and unconditionally absorbed the current step (`lastStepIndex[r] = effectiveStep % patLen` = 0). The main step-walk then short-circuited on `stepIndex == prevStep`, so step 0 of the default rhythm never fired. First audible hit waited until step 1 — **~125 ms at 120 BPM, ~188 ms at 80 BPM, ~250 ms at 60 BPM**. Stacked on top of JUCE standalone's WASAPI device init (~200-300 ms), that's the bulk of the perceived first-play lag. The absorb was correct for mid-play knob changes (avoid retroactive hit on the step you're sitting on) and for DAW resume-from-mid-bar (same reason), but wrong for cold-start / restart-from-zero where step 0 IS the user-requested first hit. Fix: guard the absorb with `!(effectiveStep == 0 && lastStepIndex[r] == -1)`. `lastStepIndex` is filled to -1 by the ctor and only set ≥0 once a rhythm has fired, so the guard fires only on the very first block from a fresh state. Result: cold-start and standalone restart-from-zero fire step 0 inside the first audio block; mid-play knob changes and DAW mid-bar resume retain the absorb behaviour. Hot-swap commits are unaffected (`lastStepIndex` is whatever step was just playing, never -1). Tested mentally against: cold-start (fires), stop-then-start (fires, since `internalBeatPos` is reset to 0 on stop), DAW play-from-start (fires), DAW resume-from-7.5 (absorbs — no retroactive fire), knob change at step 30 (absorbs — no retroactive fire), hot-swap commit (absorbs — no off-by-one against the new pattern). | ✅ Closed | 451 |

| 383 | Hot-swap rhythm preset (mid-play, via sidebar) committed with the wrong voice sound — symptom: queue a different rhythm from the browser while playing, it swaps at the loop boundary, but the audible filter/drive remained whatever the previous rhythm had until the user touched any knob on the new rhythm (the example was a comb-filter preset still sounding like the previous LP12 until cutoff was nudged). Root cause: `stageRhythmPreset` ([Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp:82](Source/PluginProcessor_Preset.cpp#L82)) created the staged `VoiceEngine` and called `prepareToPlay` but never pushed `newRhythm.voiceParams` to it; the swap commit in `handleAsyncUpdate` ([Source/PluginProcessor.cpp:965](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L965)) then `std::move`-d that default-constructed engine in. The follow-up `pushRhythmToAPVTS` runs under `apvtsLoading=true`, and `syncRhythmParam` ([Source/PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp:311](Source/PluginProcessor_APVTS.cpp#L311)) deliberately skips the `voiceEngines[ri]->setParams` call while that flag is set (intentional — bulk-load path batches a single sync at the end). So the swapped-in engine kept its default VoiceParams (`filterType=0` LP12, `driveChar=0` None, default ADSRs) until the next un-guarded `syncRhythmParam` from a real user knob change. Fix: in `stageRhythmPreset`, after `newVoice->prepareToPlay`, call `newVoice->setParams(newRhythm.voiceParams)` to prime `pendingParams`/`paramsDirty`. The `setParams` state survives the `std::move` (it's owned by the same VoiceEngine instance), and the first `process()` after the swap calls `applyPendingParams` → `syncFilter` → `syncEnvelopes` with the new values. `InsertProcessor` reads `activeParams` per-block so re-syncs automatically once `applyPendingParams` updates `activeParams`. | ✅ Closed | 449 |

| 382 | Adjusting the number of steps on Ring B muted hits triggered by Ring A. Root cause: same as #360 cascade. Trace — user moves `stepsB` knob → `EuclideanPanel::stepsB.onValueChanged` calls `apvtsSet("stepsB", v)` (1st `updatePattern`), then `updateRangesB(v)` runs `hitsB.setRange(0, v, 1)`. JUCE's `Slider::setRange` clips the current `hitsB` value if it sits outside the new range and fires `onValueChange` regardless of any `dontSendNotification` the caller set elsewhere. That spurious callback re-enters `apvtsSet("hitsB", clipped)` → 2nd `updatePattern`. Each `updatePattern` sets `patternUpdated[r]=true`; the next `SequencerEngine::processBlock` snapshots the new pattern AND resets `lastStepIndex[r] = effectiveStep % patLen`. The main step-walk then short-circuits on `if (stepIndex == prevStep) continue;` — the current step's hit is intentionally absorbed (per "Absorb the current step so we don't retroactively fire a hit", [SequencerEngine.cpp:223](Source/Sequencer/SequencerEngine.cpp#L223)). While the user drags the knob, this fires every block across both rhythms (combined pattern uses LCM(A,B) so B-changes recompute A's contribution too), so every block in flight skips its hit → audible muting of A. Fix lives in [KnobWithLabel](Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.cpp) — see #360. | ✅ Closed | 436 |

| 381 | `mu-clid_installer` CMake target only depended on `mu-clid` (the JUCE shared-lib target), not on the format outputs `mu-clid_VST3`/`mu-clid_CLAP`/`mu-clid_Standalone`. MSBuild ran the installer in parallel with the Standalone build and the Inno Setup script failed: "Source file `Release\Standalone\mu-Clid.exe` does not exist". Surfaced only on clean builds — incremental builds masked it because Standalone always existed from a prior build. Same latent issue for `mu-clid-lite_installer`. Fix: explicit `add_dependencies(... mu-clid_VST3 mu-clid_CLAP mu-clid_Standalone)` in [CMakeLists.txt:168](CMakeLists.txt#L168) and mirror for the Lite installer at [CMakeLists.txt:277](CMakeLists.txt#L277). | ✅ Closed | 432 |

| 380 | **[Audit]** `MixerEngine::processBlock` called `peakOf(effectSendBuf)` and `peakOf(delaySendBuf)` purely as `> 1e-9f` gates before computing the post-fader meter peak — two full-buffer magnitude scans where one short-circuiting `hasSignal()` would do (the reverb path already used this pattern). | 369 | **[Audit]** Dead in-place `process()` paths in `EffectSlot`/`DelaySlot`/`ReverbSlot` and `FXChain::process` — MixerEngine only calls `fxChain.processSends`, so the insert-style overrides + their `dryBuffer`/`scratchBuf` members were unreachable (~150 lines + a per-block buffer copy). Fix: (a) deleted `FXChain::process` and the `scratchBuf` member entirely (no callers); (b) replaced the 50-line `DelaySlot::process` body with a thin forward to `processReturn`, removed the `dryBuffer` member + its allocation in `prepare`, marked `blockSize` unused; (c) replaced the 30-line `ReverbSlot::process` body with a thin forward to `processReturn`; (d) added explanatory comments to all three forwards. | 368 | **[Audit]** `MultiModeFilter::process` recomputed per-channel coefficients every block even when cutoff/resonance were unchanged: LP6/HP6 one-pole `prepare()` calls hit `std::exp`, and AP12/Peak/LoShelf/HiShelf biquad `setAllPass`/`setPeak`/`setLowShelf`/`setHighShelf` all hit `cos`/`sin`/`pow`. Fix: added `lastCutoffHz` / `lastResonance` / `lastTypeCode` members, reset to -1 in `prepare()`, then a single `coeffsDirty` check at the top of `process()` gates the per-channel coefficient computes inside the LP6 (case 7), HP6 (case 11), and biquad (cases 9, 12-14) branches. SVF and Ladder paths intentionally still re-set cutoff every block — JUCE smooths internally and those calls are O(1). Mirrors the EQ change-detection pattern at [InsertProcessor.cpp:172-187](Source/Audio/InsertProcessor.cpp#L172). | ✅ Closed | 438 |

| 367 | **[Audit]** `PluginProcessor::getTailLengthSeconds()` returned 0 despite reverb tails of several seconds and delay feedback that can run for tens of seconds. Fix: return a fixed `10.0` (covers `DelaySlot::MaxDelaySamples` = 4 s @ 192 kHz + largest-preset Signalsmith FDN decay with margin). Conservative but safe; avoids coupling the tail-length contract to FX-internal state. | ✅ Closed | 444 |

| 360 | **[Audit]** [Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.cpp:15-22](Source/UI/Components/KnobWithLabel.cpp#L15) — when `setRange()` clips the slider's current value to the new range, JUCE fires `onValueChange` regardless of any prior `dontSendNotification` the caller had set. `EuclideanPanel::updateRangesA/B/C` triggered this every time the user changed steps, cascading through `apvtsSet` → APVTS broadcast → audio-thread `updatePattern` and the message-thread `RhythmPanel::parameterChanged` reload. Fix: added a `bool settingRange` re-entrance flag to `KnobWithLabel`. `setRange()` sets the flag around the inner `slider.setRange()` call; the slider's `onValueChange` lambda short-circuits when the flag is set, so the spurious clip-callback can't propagate to `onStatusUpdate` or `onValueChanged`. The owning panel's subsequent `loadFromRhythm` reloads canonical APVTS values, so no data is lost. Closing this also closed [[#382]] (audible side-effect of the same cascade — Ring A hits dropped while user dragged Ring B steps). | ✅ Closed | 436 |

| 359 | **[Audit]** `NudgeInput::showEditor` heap-allocated a `juce::TextEditor` and wired three async lambdas (`onReturnKey`/`onFocusLost`/`onEscapeKey`) that captured raw `this` without `Component::SafePointer<NudgeInput>`. If the parent `NudgeInput` died between editor creation and dismissal (panel switches rhythm, preset reload tears down the panel), the lambdas UAF on `this` via `removeChildComponent` / `setValue`. Fix: captured a `SafePointer<NudgeInput>` in all three lambdas; `removeChildComponent` / `setValue` only fire when the SafePointer still resolves, otherwise the orphaned editor is just async-deleted. | ✅ Closed | 440 |

| 358 | **[Audit]** `ReverbSlot::setParam` / `updateReverb` wrote `impl->reverb.roomMs`/`rt20`/`early`/`highDampRate`/`lowDampRate`/`detune`/`lowCutHz`/`highCutHz` directly from the message thread while `processReturn` ran `impl->reverb.process()` concurrently on the audio thread — undefined per typical embedded reverb single-threaded-access assumptions. Fix: introduced a `PendingParams` snapshot inside the pimpl, written by `updateReverb` (message thread) under a `juce::SpinLock` and gated by `pendingDirty` atomic. New `applyPendingReverbParams()` (audio thread) try-locks at the top of `processReturn` and copies the snapshot into the reverb's public fields BEFORE `reverb.process()` runs — single point where Signalsmith state is mutated. TryLock on contention defers one block instead of blocking audio. Also promoted `enabled`/`level`/`dirt`/`preDelay` to `std::atomic` for torn-read protection (they're read in the same processReturn / runPreDelay paths). `setAlgorithm` flow + `prepare` flow both still route through `updateReverb` so the first audio block applies the new snapshot. | ✅ Closed ||

| 357 | **[Audit]** `voiceEngines[r]->setActiveParams(modParams)` ran every block per rhythm at [PluginProcessor.cpp:904](Source/PluginProcessor.cpp#L904) regardless of whether the modulation pass actually executed. For an unmodulated rhythm `modParams ≡ rhythm.voiceParams ≡ activeParams` (already kept in sync by `VoiceEngine::applyPendingParams`'s dirty-flag path), so each call was pure waste — `syncEnvelopes()` + `syncFilter()` re-running on identical state. Fix: wrapped the call in `if (runModulationPass)` so unmodulated rhythms only sync via the `paramsDirty` exchange path. Material per-block CPU save proportional to (unmodulated rhythm count × ADSR/filter sync cost). | ✅ Closed | 438 |

| 356 | **[Audit]** `RhythmPanel::commitNameFromLabel` wrote `proc.getRhythm(idx).name = newName.toStdString();` directly from the message thread, bypassing all serialisation with audio-thread state. Investigation found no audio-thread reader of `rhythm.name` today (state save/load, UI display, and MixerOverlay labels are all message-thread; MidiOutputEngine doesn't reference name), so the audit's "MIDI PC matcher" concern was speculative. Still applied a defensive fix: routed the write through new `PluginProcessor::renameRhythm(int, juce::String)` which takes `rhythmsLock` — the project's canonical "message thread mutates Rhythm" serialiser, paired with the audio thread's `ScopedTryLock(rhythmsLock)` in `processBlock`. Stays correct if a future audio-path consumer (e.g. MIDI program-change preset matcher) reads name. No UI-thread modLock spin. | ✅ Closed | 440 |

| 355 | **[Audit]** `RhythmPanel::confirmReset` spun on `r.modLock.compare_exchange_weak` on the UI thread. If the audio thread was preempted while holding `modLock` (OS scheduler / DAW low-priority audio mode) the UI froze. Worse, after acquire, `r = Rhythm{}` triggered `std::vector` destructors in `modulationMatrix`/`controlSequences` while a concurrent in-flight `modulationMatrix.process()` may already have cached references to the old assignments — acquire/release on `modLock` doesn't save you once `process()` is already past the try-lock. Fix: extracted the reset into new `PluginProcessor::resetRhythm(int)` using the same `suspendProcessing(true)` + `ScopedLock(rhythmsLock)` pattern already used by `removeRhythm` / `swapRhythmSlots`. `suspendProcessing` halts new audio-thread entries; `rhythmsLock` waits for the in-flight `processBlock`'s `ScopedTryLock` to release. UI-thread spin gone; safe atomic swap of the Rhythm struct. | ✅ Closed | 440 |

| 354 | **[Audit]** `RhythmPanel::parameterChanged` was invoked by JUCE on whatever thread called `setValueNotifyingHost` — in some DAWs that's the audio thread for host automation — and the handler called `euclidPanel.loadFromRhythm()` / `voiceSection.loadFromRhythm()` which mutate `juce::Slider` state. Slider ops are not audio-thread-safe → potential crash / UB. Fix: handler now captures a `Component::SafePointer<RhythmPanel>` + the suffix, then either runs inline if already on the message thread or marshals via `juce::MessageManager::callAsync`. SafePointer guards against panel teardown between the audio-thread enqueue and the message-thread dispatch (preset reload / rhythm switch). | ✅ Closed | 437 |

| 353 | **[Audit]** Every rhythm parameter change reset the *entire* euclidean panel (21 knobs + 9 segment controls) or voice section (28+ knobs) via `loadFromRhythm` — one knob touch ≡ whole panel rewrite, multiplied by every parameterChanged event in the cascade. Fix: added `EuclideanPanel::refreshSuffix(suffix)` and `VoiceSection::refreshSuffix(suffix)`, each an if/else chain mapping a single APVTS suffix to the one knob/segment that owns it. `RhythmPanel::parameterChanged` (now message-thread-marshalled per [[#354]]) calls `refreshSuffix` instead of `loadFromRhythm`. Insert-knob suffixes (`drvDrv`/`drvOut`/`drvDit`/`drvTon`/`drvBits`/`drvRate`/`eqMidGain`) re-run `configureInsertAlgorithm` because the layout depends on `driveChar` — still cheaper than a full reload. `loadFromRhythm` retained for `setRhythm`/preset-load paths that genuinely need a full refresh. | ✅ Closed | 437 |

| 352 | **[Audit]** `MixerOverlay` registered an APVTS listener for *every* parameter in the entire tree (hundreds across all rhythms / voices / mods) and set `apvtsDirty=true` on any change. Each dirty-flag flush called `loadFromAPVTS` which rebuilds every mixer channel strip — wasted work on every rhythm/euclid/voice/mod knob change, and a feedback-storm risk via the universal listener. Fix: added `isMixerRelevantParam(id)` helper that recognises only mixer-relevant prefixes — `ch{N}_*` rhythm channels, `ret_eff_*`/`ret_dly_*`/`ret_rev_*` returns, `mstr_*`/`mst_ins*` master + inserts, `eff_*`/`dly_*`/`rev_*`/`echo_*` FX algorithm + params. Constructor + destructor parameter-listener loops filter through this predicate. Verified the prefix list against the actual `addParameter` registrations in `PluginProcessor.cpp` — no mixer-affecting IDs missed. Rhythm/euclid/voice/mod knob movements no longer trigger spurious mixer reloads. | ✅ Closed | 444 |

| 351 | **[Audit]** Apparent policy contradiction between `.claude/commands/bug.md`/`update.md` ("never use suffix notation") and the MEMORY.md index entry for `feedback_backlog_single_issue.md` ("MANDATORY: split combined rows using suffix notation #178a/b"). Investigation: the actual `feedback_backlog_single_issue.md` body already says **"Never use suffix notation"** — only the one-line index summary in MEMORY.md was wrong. Fix: corrected the MEMORY.md index line to "split into next sequential whole numbers — NEVER use suffix notation". Bug.md / update.md unchanged (already correct). | ✅ Closed | 433 |

Fix: moved #338/#337/#336 down to slot between #339 and #335 so the section is strict descending. Verified by awk pass — 327 Fixed rows all in order. | ✅ Closed | 433 |

Testers were receiving Debug builds for an unknown period. Fix: changed the three Copy-Item paths from `\\Debug\\` to `\\Release\\` so the hook now mirrors CMake's deploy semantics. Hook remains as a belt-and-braces fallback. Verified by full clean rebuild — tester folder now holds only Release artifacts (build 432). | ✅ Closed | 432 |

| 348 | Euclid modulation scales too aggressive (sibling of #336) — fixed scales of 16 (hits / rotate / insSt) covered the full slider range at typical steps=16, so any moderate depth saturated the pattern. Halved scales: hits/rotate/insSt 16→8, prePad/postPad 12→6, insLen 8→4. Same proportions, half the magnitude — user dials depth higher to get the old feel. | ✅ Closed | 427 |

| 347 | Return solo doesn't suppress rhythm dry passthrough (sibling of #337) — when a return channel (Effect/Delay/Reverb) was soloed, the user heard the soloed return's wet PLUS the rhythm channels' dry going to master, because the rhythm-channel mute logic only considered rhythm-channel solo state. Fix: rhythm channels now skip the addFrom to master (but still feed FX sends, so the soloed return has source material) when any return is soloed. Hard-mute path (mute \|\| rhythm-solo-and-not-this) unchanged. | ✅ Closed | 427 |

| 346 | Runtime-verify #345 fix — confirmed in standalone: removing the last `euclid.*` modulation assignment mid-play causes the pattern to snap back to base within one buffer. Stage A/B/C wiring + #345 polish work as designed. | ✅ Closed | 426 |

| 345 | Removing all euclid pattern modulation assignments while playing left a stale modulated pattern (sibling of #336) — root cause was the `if (!getAssignments().empty())` guard in `PluginProcessor::processBlock`'s modulation loop, which skipped the `lastEuclidOverrides[r]` write-back when the matrix became empty. Fix: drop the guard so the modulation pass always runs (ModulationMatrix::process() already returns early when assignments is empty — cost is ~40 hash writes per rhythm). lastEuclidOverrides now re-converges to base values one block after assignment removal; Stage B change-detection then recomputes the safe pattern back to base. Cleaner than UI-side `updatePattern()` plumbing because it works for every removal path (state restore, programmatic removal, dropdown-change-source). | ✅ Closed | 425 |

| 344 | Save dialog "Save as Default" breaks Save button — `saveBtn.onClick` returned early when `nameEditor.getText().trim().isEmpty()`, but in Save-as-Default mode `updateDefaultModeState()` disables `nameEditor` so the user can't type a name. Fix: skip the empty-name guard when `isSaveAsDefault()` is true — the filename is hard-coded to `_default.muclid` in that branch. | ✅ Closed | 425 |

| 343 | Comb filter cutoff clicks when manually swept — the comb filter's delay line read position jumps discontinuously when the cutoff parameter changes, causing audible clicks. The delay length needs per-sample smoothing (e.g. one-pole lowpass on the target delay time) so the read position glides rather than steps. | ✅ Closed | 416 |

| 342 | Reverb tail gated — `reverb.processReturn` is only called when `reverbSendBuf` has fresh input signal, so the Signalsmith FDN stops advancing between hits and the reverb tail cuts off abruptly instead of decaying naturally. Same root cause as #339 (echo) — fix is to always run `reverb.processReturn` every block so the internal FDN drains freely. | ✅ Closed | 414 |

| 341 | ModDest::ids renamed to ModDest::kTable — two call sites (`ModulatorEditor.cpp` and `ModMatrixPanel.cpp`) still used the old `ids[0]` accessor, causing compile failure. Updated to `kTable[0].id`. | ✅ Closed | 412 |

| 340 | EFX type dropdown hidden when Echo mode active — switching EFX algo to Echo hides the effectRow (including algo dropdown), leaving no way to switch back to Chorus/Flanger/Phaser. Fix: keep effectRow visible in header-only mode (knobs hidden), echoRow positioned in the knobs area with no header; effectRow On button syncs echo_en when Echo is active. | ✅ Closed | 412 |

| 339 | Echo (EFX→Echo) feedback loop broken between hits — `effect.processReturn` was gated on `doEffect` (input signal present), so the echo's circular buffer was never advanced between hits and feedback echoes were silently dropped. Fix: `needsContinuousProcessing()` forces processReturn every block when Echo is active; MixerEngine checks signal post-processSends (matching delay slot behaviour). | ✅ Closed | 412 |

| 336 | Euclid pattern modulation audio wiring — all 18 euclid pattern destinations (euclid.*.hits, euclid.*.rotate, euclid.*.prePad, euclid.*.postPad, euclid.*.insSt, euclid.*.insLen) now affect the audio pattern in real time. Stage A: added the 18 keys to `modParamValues` so `ModulationMatrix::process()` no longer silently drops them; per-block reseed + write-back into a new `lastEuclidOverrides` snapshot. Stage B: added non-allocating override-aware overloads of `EuclideanGenerator::generate`, `HitGenerator::getPattern`, and `Rhythm::getCombinedPattern`; new `SequencerEngine::tryUpdatePatternFromModulation` uses a try-lock on `patternLock` and writes directly into `safePatterns`/`safeCPatterns` (pre-reserved to 256 in ctor — zero allocation on the audio thread). Change-detection compares integer-rounded overrides to last block, skipping no-op recomputes (typical LFO triggers ~1 recompute/sec, not 100+). Pattern recompute path bypasses `cachedPatterns` so message-thread move-assign cannot clobber a modulated pattern.
