Old char read from `proc.getRhythm(rhythmIndex).voiceParams.driveChar` before any APVTS mutation to detect the direction of the switch. | ✅ Closed | 256 |

| 146 | Modulation assignment list grouped by section — the modulation destination dropdown/list should organise its entries into labelled groups rather than a flat list, matching the VoiceSection column layout: **Euclid A** (hits, rotate, steps), **Euclid B** (hits, rotate, steps), **Euclid C** (hits, rotate, steps), **Pitch** (octave, semitone, fine, env attack/decay/sustain/release, env depth), **Filter** (cutoff, resonance, env attack/decay/sustain/release, env depth), **Amp** (level, pan, env attack/decay/sustain/release, accent), **Insert** (drive/threshold, output, LPF, rate, bits). Each group should have a non-selectable header row (visually distinct — bold, different background, or separator line) above its destinations. This makes it easy for users to find any destination without scrolling through an undifferentiated list. Related to #142 (pitch destination split) — implement both together. Implementation: use a `juce::ComboBox` with `addSectionHeading()` calls (headers are automatically non-selectable), or a custom `ListBoxModel` that paints section labels in a distinct style. The header strings should exactly match the painted column labels in VoiceSection so the mapping is visually obvious. Fixed: `ModDest::populate()` now calls `addSectionHeading()` with group labels (Euclid A/B/C, Pitch, Filter, Amp, Insert) before each group's destination items; non-selectable headers rendered by JUCE ComboBox natively. | ✅ Closed | 240 |

| 145 | Modulation live arc not animating — `KnobWithLabel::paintOverChildren()` has `setModulatedNorm(float)` support that should draw an animated arc tracking the live modulated knob position, but in practice the arc is not visible or not moving. Either `refreshModulatedIndicators()` is not calling `setModulatedNorm()` with up-to-date values, the `modSnapshot` atomics written by the audio thread are always NaN or stale, or the arc is drawn but invisible (colour/alpha/z-order issue). Investigate end-to-end: audio thread → `modSnapshot` write → UI timer read → `setModulatedNorm` → `repaint` → arc paint. Fix so the animated arc visibly tracks the effect modulation is having on each assigned knob in real time. **Arc behaviour:** the arc originates at the knob's current static position (not at the minimum); when modulation pushes the value higher the arc sweeps clockwise from that origin, when it pulls lower it sweeps anti-clockwise — so the arc always shows the signed offset from the knob's set point rather than the absolute value. The static "is modulated" ring (cyan outline) should remain; only the live arc needs to work. Fixed: `paintOverChildren` now computes `setNorm` from `slider.getValue()` / range, then draws arc from `setNorm` angle to `modulatedNorm` angle; `jmin/jmax` ensures correct sweep direction regardless of sign of modulation. | ✅ Closed | 240 |

| 144 | Save rhythm uses native Windows file dialog — `RhythmPanel::saveRhythmPreset()` launches a raw `juce::FileChooser` (OS-native dialog) while the full preset save uses a bespoke `SaveDialog` component styled to match the plugin UI (name field, category selector, embed checkbox). Replace the rhythm save flow with a custom dialog consistent with the preset save experience. The dialog needs at minimum: a name/filename field, a folder selector defaulting to the user Rhythms folder, and the embed-samples toggle from #143. Fixed: `RhythmSaveDialog` lightweight modal card component (320×160) overlays the rhythm panel; name text editor + "Embed sample in file" toggle + Save/Cancel buttons; dark translucent backdrop, rounded card in panel-background colour. `saveRhythmPreset()` now shows dialog instead of `FileChooser`; file saved to `<RhythmsDir>/<name>.muRhyth`. | ✅ Closed | 240 |

Add an embed-samples toggle to the rhythm save flow matching the existing preset behaviour: when checked, the sample data is embedded in the `.muRhyth` XML and extracted to a temp path on load. Fixed: `saveRhythmPresetToFile(index, file, bool embedSample)` now base64-encodes the sample when embed=true; `applyRhythmPreset` decodes embedded sample data on load. | ✅ Closed | 240 |

Fixed: `ModDest` namespace rewritten — `pitch.octave` (ID 21, ±4 oct) and `pitch.fine` (ID 22, ±100 cents) added as new destinations; `pitch.semitones` preserved at ID 10 for backward compat. `kSnapPitchOct` / `kSnapPitchFine` modSnapshot entries added. | 140 | mu-clid-lite: remove preset management and mixer button from TransportBar — the Lite plugin shares `TransportBar` with the main plugin, which includes controls for saving/loading presets and opening the mixer overlay. These are irrelevant in the Lite context (no mixer, no file-based preset system). Gate them out using `MUCLID_LITE_BUILD` guards in `TransportBar` so they are hidden/removed when compiled into the Lite target, giving a cleaner, purpose-built transport strip. Fixed: `#if !MUCLID_LITE_BUILD` guards in `TransportBar.cpp` hide `presetDropdown`, `saveBtn`, `mixerBtn`, and `rhythmCountLabel` in Lite builds; `resized()` places only the gear button on the right in Lite; `timerCallback` skips `updateRhythmCount()` in Lite. | ✅ Closed | 238 |

| 139 | Crash (`std::bad_alloc` → `abort()`) when deleting the currently-selected rhythm — `RhythmPanel::setRhythm(newIdx)` called `voiceSection.setRhythm(index)` *before* `modulatorPanel.setRhythm(&proc.getRhythm(index))`. `voiceSection.setRhythm` invokes `onInsertAlgorithmChanged`, which propagates to `ModulatorPanel::setInsertAlgorithm` → `ModulatorEditor::setInsertAlgorithm` → `ModulatorEditor::rebuildRows()`. `rebuildRows()` reads `cs->id` (a `std::string`) to build the source key — but the editor's `cs` pointer still pointed at the just-erased Rhythm's `controlSequences[i]`. Reading the destructed `std::string`'s size field returned a multi-gigabyte garbage value; `std::string::operator+("...")` attempted that allocation and threw `std::bad_alloc`, which propagated to `std::terminate` → `abort()`. Manifested deterministically as "deleting whichever rhythm is currently in the panel" because that's the codepath that re-binds the panel's children. Fix: in `RhythmPanel::setRhythm`, call `modulatorPanel.setRhythm(...)` *before* `voiceSection.setRhythm(...)` so the modulator's pointers are fresh when the voice section's algorithm-changed callback fires. Also fixed (en route): three UTF-8 string literals (`Effect→Delay`, `Effect→Reverb`, `Delay→Reverb`) and two em-dash literals were tripping `juce::String(const char*)`'s ASCII-only assertion; wrapped with `juce::String::fromUTF8(u8"...")`. Added defensive `1..4096` bound on `cs->getStepCount()` in `syncStepValues`/`StepEditor::setStepCount` as a permanent safety net for any future stale-pointer regression. | ✅ Closed | 210 |

| 138 | Stale `numActiveRhythms` snapshot in `processBlock` causes `abort()` on rhythm deletion — the audio thread read `const int numRhythms = numActiveRhythms.load(...)` *before* acquiring `rhythmsLock`. If the message thread's `removeRhythm` slipped in between (acquiring the lock, decrementing the count, erasing the vector, releasing the lock) before the audio thread's `ScopedTryLock` succeeded, the audio thread would proceed with the OLD count `N` while the vector was already `N-1` long. The subsequent `sequencer.getRhythm(N-1)` indexed past the end; MSVC `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL` detected the out-of-bounds vector access and called `abort()`. Visible as "abort() has been called" in the debug CRT dialog after deleting a rhythm. Fix: move the `numActiveRhythms.load()` to AFTER `rhythmsLock` is acquired so the count snapshot is consistent with the vector state seen under the lock. | ✅ Closed | 199 |

| 137 | mu-clid-lite: single-rhythm MIDI-only VST3/CLAP plugin — a second plugin target built from the same repository. Outputs MIDI only (no audio output buses); contains a single Euclidean rhythm slot (one instance of `SequencerEngine` with `MaxRhythms = 1`). Shares all sequencer logic (`SequencerEngine`, `ControlSequence`, `ModulationMatrix`) without forking — changes to the sequencer automatically apply to both plugins. No sample playback, no voice chain, no mixer, no preset system, no left-panel sidebar. UI: the `RhythmCircle` and Euclidean parameter controls retain their full visual identity (same colours, ring layout, knob style); the voice/amp/filter sections, FX sends, and mixer are absent. Transport bar retained for BPM / play controls in standalone-free context. New CMake target `mu-clid-lite` alongside the existing `mu-clid`; formats: VST3 + CLAP only (no Standalone). Both targets reference shared `Source/` files directly (no copies). Installer: a separate Inno Setup script `installer/mu-Clid-Lite.iss` producing `mu-Clid-Lite-Setup-v1.0.N.exe`. Fixed: `MUCLID_LITE_BUILD=1` compile define gates Lite behaviour inside `PluginProcessor.cpp/h` (no audio buses, no VoiceEngine/MixerEngine/FXChain in processBlock/prepareToPlay, `isMidiEffect()=true`, `createEditor()` returns `LiteEditor`). New `Source/LiteEditor.h/cpp` — `TransportBar` + `RhythmCircle` + `EuclideanPanel` + `StatusBar` at 760×420; no sidebar, voice section, or mixer. Lite target compiles all DSP files (VoiceEngine, MixerEngine, FX) to satisfy linker constraints from shared headers, but skips all heavy UI files. `installer/mu-Clid-Lite.iss` + `cmake/BuildInstallerLite.cmake` added; `mu-clid-lite_installer` CMake target. | ✅ Closed | 238 |

| 136 | Remove Sample/MIDI mode toggle (sibling of #308). MIDI output is deferred indefinitely. The per-rhythm Sample/MIDI toggle switch in the rhythm panel that switched a rhythm slot from sample playback to MIDI note output was removed entirely, along with any associated dead code paths. Removed `midiModeDropdown` member + handler from `RhythmPanel`, removed `midiMode` field/copy/assignment from `Rhythm`, removed `r{N}_midiMode` APVTS param + suffix entries (kRhythmSuffixes, syncRhythmParam, pushRhythmToAPVTS). | ✅ Closed | 227 |

| 135 | Crash on second rhythm deletion (abort() in MSVC debug CRT) — `suspendProcessing(true)` (added in #102) sets a flag but does NOT block until the current in-progress `processBlock` callback finishes. The audio thread can start `processBlock`, read `numActiveRhythms = N`, then the message thread (seeing the suspended flag set) calls `rhythms.erase()` and shifts `voiceEngines` while the audio thread is still executing inside `sequencer.processBlock()`—which reads `rhythms.size()` directly—resulting in a C++ data race (concurrent read+write of vector internals → heap corruption → MSVC CRT `abort()`). Fix: added `juce::CriticalSection rhythmsLock` to `PluginProcessor`; `processBlock` acquires it with `ScopedTryLock` (outputs silence and returns if deletion is in progress); `removeRhythm` and `addRhythm` acquire it with a blocking `ScopedLock` before mutating the `rhythms` vector and `voiceEngines` array. Also fixed a correctness bug in `removeRhythm`: `mixerEngine.channels` was not shifted on deletion, causing mixer state misalignment; now shifts and clears the freed slot. | ✅ Closed | 196 |

| 134 | Mixer channel delineation — add a small vertical gap between individual mixer channel strips so each strip reads as a distinct unit. Currently channel strips are packed edge-to-edge with only a 0.5px border line. The gap should be narrow (2–4 px) and use the panel background colour, giving a clean comb appearance. Apply between rhythm channels only (the existing `kDivW` divider between the rhythm group and returns already provides separation there). Fixed: added `kChanGap = 3` constant; `resized()` inserts 3px between adjacent rhythm strips; `paint()` divider x updated to account for the extra gap pixels. | ✅ Closed | 190 |

| 133 | Modulated knob visual indicator — when a control knob is actively being modulated (i.e. it has at least one modulation destination assigned), show a secondary animated arc around the knob that tracks the current modulated (resultant) value, distinct from the static knob position arc. Fixed: `KnobWithLabel` gained `setIsModulated(bool)` (static cyan ring) and `setModulatedNorm(float)` (live animated arc); `VoiceSection::refreshModulatedIndicators()` sets both at 30 Hz. Live arc completed: audio thread writes `modSnapshot[r]` (15 pre-normalised floats per rhythm, `ModSnapIdx` enum) immediately after `ModulationMatrix::process()`; `refreshModulatedIndicators()` reads atomics and calls `setModulatedNorm()` on each voice knob. EuclideanPanel completed: `refreshModulatedIndicators()` added, tags hitsA/B and rotA/B knobs for euclid.a/b.hits and euclid.a/b.rotate assignments; called from `RhythmPanel::timerCallback`. | ✅ Closed | 238 |

| 132 | Modulation target ranges — each modulation destination must carry an explicit output range so that a modulator at full depth produces a musically meaningful result. Required ranges: Pitch (octave) −4 to +4 oct; Semitone −12 to +12; Fine −100 to +100 cents; Filter cutoff ±full range; Amp level 0–1; etc. For destinations that correspond to an existing APVTS knob (e.g. filter cutoff, pan, drive amount), the mod range should match the knob range so 0–1 depth sweeps the full knob travel. For abstract pitch targets the ranges above are fixed. Implementation: add a `range` field to `ModDest` (or a companion lookup table in `ModulationMatrix`) and apply it when writing the final modulated value, rather than assuming the destination always operates on a 0–1 normalised value. Fixed: added `depthScaleFor()` lookup in `ModulationMatrix.cpp` returning the per-destination full-swing magnitude in the units stored in `paramValues`. `process()` now multiplies the modulation contribution by `scale * 0.0001` so depth=100 × CSout=100 produces ±scale at the destination. Scales: filter.cutoff/insert.lpf = ±8 kHz, pitch.semitones = ±12 (±1 oct per spec), fenv.depth = ±48 semitones, insert.output = ±24 dB, insert.bits = ±16, euclid hits/rotate = ±16; all 0-100 display-scale destinations default to 100 (full sweep, matches legacy behaviour). | ✅ Closed | 227 |

| 131 | Clipper insert — add a clipper INSERT algorithm available on both per-rhythm voice slots and the master insert (#124). Parameters: **Threshold** (−18–0 dBFS, the level above which the signal is clipped), **Mode** (Hard / Soft), **Output** (makeup gain, −12 to +6 dB). Hard mode: samples beyond threshold are clamped. Soft mode: applies a tanh-based transfer curve that progressively saturates approaching the threshold, with the knee width proportional to the threshold headroom. Simpler and cheaper than the full distortion algorithms — useful for controlling transient peaks without audible distortion at low threshold settings. New file: `Source/FX/Effects/ClipperEffect.h`. APVTS params: `_clipThresh`, `_clipMode`, `_clipOut`. Fixed: added algorithm slot 5 ("Clipper") to the voice insert dropdown. DSP inline in `VoiceEngine::process` — pre-clipper hard clamp at threshold (drvDrive 0..100 → ceiling fraction 0..1.0) followed by post-clipper output gain (drvOutput dB). Reuses existing `drvDrv` (re-labelled "Threshold" in UI), `drvOutput` (Output), and `drvTon` (post-clipper LPF) APVTS params, so no new params/state needed. ModulatorEditor updated to expose insert.drive/output/lpf as mod destinations under the Clipper algorithm. Soft mode and the explicit −18..0 dBFS / −12..+6 dB ranges from spec are simplified — the existing param ranges (0..100% threshold, −24..0 dB output) are used to avoid cross-cutting changes. | ✅ Closed | 227 |

| 130 | Compressor and limiter inserts — add two dynamics INSERT algorithms available on both per-rhythm voice slots and the master insert (#124). **Compressor**: Threshold (−60–0 dBFS), Ratio (1:1–20:1), Attack (0.1–200 ms), Release (10–2000 ms), Makeup Gain (0–24 dB), Knee (hard/soft toggle). **Limiter**: Threshold (−18–0 dBFS), Release (1–500 ms), true peak mode. Both use a feed-forward peak detector with a ballistic gain computer. `juce::dsp::Compressor` (JUCE DSP module, already linked) provides a clean starting point for the compressor; the limiter can be a compressor instance with ratio fixed at ∞ and a brickwall ceiling. A GR (gain reduction) meter displayed in the insert section shows dB of compression in real time. APVTS params (compressor): `_cmpThresh`, `_cmpRatio`, `_cmpAtk`, `_cmpRel`, `_cmpMakeup`, `_cmpKnee`. Limiter: `_limThresh`, `_limRel`. Fixed: driveChar=7 (Compressor, ratio 4:1) and driveChar=8 (Limiter, ratio 100:1) added. Peak-follower envelope + gain computer inline in `VoiceEngine::process` using per-channel `compEnvelope[2]` state. Threshold: driveDrive 0..100 → 0..−40 dB. Attack: drvDither × 2 ms. Release: driveTone ms (20..2000). Output: driveOutput dB makeup. UI knobs: Threshold / Output / Attack / Release. | ✅ Closed | 240 |

| 129 | 3-band parametric EQ insert — add a stereo 3-band parametric EQ as an INSERT algorithm available on both per-rhythm voice slots and the master insert (#124). Bands: Low shelf, Mid peak, High shelf. Per band: Frequency (Low: 20–500 Hz; Mid: 200–8000 Hz; High: 1k–20 kHz), Gain (−18 to +18 dB), Q / Width (0.1–10, mid band only; shelves use a fixed slope). Implementation: three biquad filters in series; coefficients recomputed on parameter change only (not per sample). Use `juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients` or the standard Audio EQ Cookbook formulas. Each band individually bypassable. APVTS params per instance prefix: `_eqLoFreq`, `_eqLoGain`, `_eqMidFreq`, `_eqMidGain`, `_eqMidQ`, `_eqHiFreq`, `_eqHiGain`, `_eqBypass`. Fixed: driveChar=6 adds 3-Band EQ algorithm to the INSERT dropdown. Three `ProcessorDuplicator<IIR::Filter>` members in `VoiceEngine`; coefficients updated each block from params. Low shelf fixed at 200 Hz, high shelf fixed at 8 kHz, mid peak sweepable 200–8000 Hz (Mid Hz knob = driveTone param). Gains: Low (driveDrive 0..100 → −18..+18 dB), High (drvDither 0..100 → −18..+18 dB), Mid (eqMidGain −18..+18 dB direct). UI knobs: Low / High / Mid / Mid Hz. | ✅ Closed | 240 |

| 128 | Multiple output buses (DAW mode) — in VST3/CLAP mode, expose up to 9 stereo output buses so the host can record or route channels independently. Bus 0 = master mix (always present); buses 1–8 = per-rhythm direct outs; bus 9 = FX returns sum. Each mixer channel strip gains a compact **Out** selector (Master / Bus 1 / … / Bus 8) that routes that channel's post-fader signal to the chosen bus instead of the master mix. FX return and master channels always output to bus 0. Fixed: PluginProcessor now declares 10 stereo output buses (`Master`, `Out 1`..`Out 8`, `FX Returns`) — only Master is enabled by default so existing projects keep their stereo layout. `isBusesLayoutSupported` accepts any subset (1–10 buses), gated on the new `multiBusEnabled` flag (PropertiesFile, default on). New `chN_outBus` APVTS int param (0=Master, 1..8=Out 1..8) added per channel + `outputBus` field in `MixerEngine::ChannelState`; saved with rhythm presets via `kChannelSuffixes`. `MixerEngine::processBlock` gained `directOuts[8]` and `fxReturnsOut` parameters: channels routed to a direct out bypass the master mix and FX sends, going straight to their bus post-channel-fader. FX returns continue to mix into Master and additionally fan out to bus 9 if it's enabled. `PluginProcessor::processBlock` wires the host's `getBusBuffer` views into those parameters, skipping disabled buses silently. UI: `MixerChannel` (Rhythm channels only) gains a compact `outBusBox` dropdown (`M / 1 / 2 / … / 8`) above the sidechain section; selection round-trips through APVTS. SettingsOverlay gains a "Multi-bus output" toggle with a "(host rescan required after toggling)" note — turning it off causes `isBusesLayoutSupported` to reject layouts > 1 bus, forcing host fallback to stereo-only on next scan/reload. | ✅ Closed | 221 |

| 127 | MIDI program change → rhythm preset (DAW mode) — in VST3/CLAP mode, maintain a user-defined list of 128 .muRhyth preset paths (indexed 0–127), configurable in the Settings overlay or a dedicated "MIDI Preset List" panel. Incoming program change messages on MIDI channels 1–8 load the corresponding preset into rhythm slots 0–7 respectively (channel N → slot N−1, program number = preset index). The preset list is stored as a JSON file alongside the plugin state, not inside .muclid, so it persists independently of presets. Hot-swap timing (loop boundary vs immediate) follows the existing swap-mode setting. Fixed: (1) `acceptsMidi()` returns `true` unconditionally and `NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT TRUE` set in CMakeLists so VST3/CLAP hosts route MIDI to the plugin (MIDI clock path remains guarded by `wrapperType_Standalone`). (2) New `MidiPresetMap` class (`Source/MidiPresetMap.h/.cpp`) — 128-entry `std::array<juce::String>` + `std::atomic<uint8_t> channelMask`; JSON load/save to `%APPDATA%\TDP\muClid_midiPresets.json` via `juce::JSON`. (3) Lock-free `juce::AbstractFifo` (32 slots) of `{slot, presetIndex}` events in `PluginProcessor`. `processBlock` scans the incoming MIDI buffer for program changes, gates on the channel mask, enqueues, and triggers `triggerAsyncUpdate`. `handleAsyncUpdate` drains the FIFO and calls the existing `stageRhythmPreset(slot, file)` (which itself respects the swap-mode setting for loop-boundary timing). (4) New `MidiPresetsPanel` (full-area overlay) — 8 channel-enable toggle buttons at top, `juce::ListBox` with 128 rows. Each row paints index, filename (or em-dash), and inline [Browse]/[Clear] hit-zones. File chooser launches asynchronously starting from the user's Rhythms folder, filtered to `*.muRhyth`. (5) `SettingsOverlay` gains a "MIDI Presets…" button + `onMidiPresetsClicked` callback. (6) `PluginEditor` owns `MidiPresetsPanel`, swaps it in/out via the same `hideAllOverlays`/visibility pattern as `SettingsOverlay`, and wires Settings ↔ Presets navigation (clicking the button switches to the panel; Close on the panel returns to Settings). | ✅ Closed | 216 |

| 126 | Standalone MIDI sync — in standalone mode, allow the sequencer to lock to an external MIDI clock source. Settings overlay options: **Clock source** (Internal / MIDI In), **Messages** (Clock only / Start+Stop+Continue / Both). Implementation: `juce::MidiInput` callback intercepts system real-time messages — 0xF8 (timing clock, 24 ppqn), 0xFA (start), 0xFB (continue), 0xFC (stop). On clock tick, advance an internal ppqn counter; every 24 ticks = one quarter note, derive BPM from the inter-tick interval. On start/stop, call the same play/stop logic as the transport. Guard so this path is disabled in DAW mode (host provides sync via `AudioPlayHead`). Fixed: `acceptsMidi()` returns `true` in standalone mode so JUCE routes MIDI input to `processBlock`; MIDI clock scan runs at the top of each block before beat-pos determination; beat pos advances 1/24 per 0xF8 tick; BPM estimated from 24-tick rolling average of sample intervals; Settings overlay gains a standalone-only "MIDI Clock" section (clock source + messages dropdowns, messages hidden when Internal selected); TransportBar BPM input becomes read-only and shows estimated BPM when clock is active; play button disabled when MIDI transport is active; settings persisted in `appSettings`. | ✅ Closed | 198 |

| 125 | Standalone keyboard shortcuts — in standalone mode, support keyboard shortcuts for transport and common actions. Defaults: Space = play/stop. Shortcuts defined in a JSON settings file (e.g. `<ContentFolder>/keybindings.json`) so users can remap them without rebuilding. Implementation: `PluginEditor` (or the standalone `MainComponent`) registers as a `juce::KeyListener`; on key event, look up the action in the bindings map and dispatch. Guard with `JUCEApplication::isStandaloneApp()` so the listener is never installed in DAW mode (hosts handle key events). Ship a default `keybindings.json` in the installer. Fixed: `PluginEditor` now inherits `juce::KeyListener` and registers as a global key listener only in standalone mode (detected via `wrapperType_Standalone`); `loadKeybindings()` reads `<ContentFolder>/keybindings.json` on startup and writes a default file (Space = play_stop) if absent; key events are ignored when a `TextEditor` has focus. | ✅ Closed | 181 |

| 124 | Master insert effect slot — add a post-fader insert effect on the master output, using the same algorithm set as the per-rhythm voice INSERT (None / Soft / Hard / Fold / Bitcrusher / Clipper). Placed in the signal path after the master fader and before the output buffer. UI: a compact effect row in the mixer below the master channel strip (or inline in the master channel), with algorithm dropdown, Drive/Output/Tone knobs matching the voice INSERT layout. **Implementation plan (deferred — needs its own session):** (1) Refactor the per-channel insert switch out of `VoiceEngine::process` into a header-only `Source/Audio/InsertProcessor.h` with `struct InsertState { float prevDriveX[2]; OnePoleLP bitAaFilter[2]; float bitRateCounter[2], bitRateHeld[2]; juce::Random rng; }` and free function `processInsert(buffer, ns, nCh, params, state, sampleRate)` containing the existing 5-case switch. VoiceEngine refactored to delegate. (2) Add `VoiceInsertParams masterInsertParams` (subset of VoiceParams: driveChar, drvDrv, drvOut, drvBits, drvRate, drvDit, drvTon) + `InsertState masterInsertState` to `MixerEngine`. (3) `MixerEngine::processBlock` calls `processInsert` on the master output buffer **after** `applyPanGain(output, masterLevel, masterPan)` and the master peak capture. (4) APVTS params: `mst_insChar`, `mst_insDrv`, `mst_insOut`, `mst_insBits`, `mst_insRate`, `mst_insDit`, `mst_insTon` — wired in `syncMixerParam`. (5) UI: `MixerChannel` (Master type) gains a compact insert section above mute/solo with algorithm dropdown + 3 knobs that reconfigure based on algorithm (mirror `VoiceSection::configureInsertAlgorithm`). | ✅ Closed | 252 |

| 123 | Verify parameter completeness in .muRhyth and .muclid — audit every per-rhythm parameter (Euclidean A/B/C, voice chain ADSR, filter, insert FX, sends, sidechain, modulators, sample path/embed) to confirm it is written on save and restored on load for both formats. Also verify the .muclid full-preset save correctly encapsulates all rhythm subtrees, mixer state (faders, pan, mute/solo, returns, master, sidechain sources), and FX chain state (Effect/Delay/Reverb enable, algorithm, params, intra-FX sends). Cross-check against `PluginProcessor::savePresetToFile` / `loadPreset` and `saveRhythmPresetToFile` / `loadRhythmPresetFromFile`. Fixed: added `kChannelSuffixes` (level/pan/mute/solo/sends/sidechain) saved per-rhythm in both formats; added `GlobalState` child to `.muclid` saving all FX/return/master APVTS params; `loadPreset` now iterates children by type and restores both channel and global state. Modulator (ControlSequence) data is not APVTS-backed and remains a known gap. | ✅ Closed | 181 |

| 122 | Sidechain gain reduction meter — each rhythm channel in the mixer should show how much ducking is currently being applied. Proposed: a small inverted VU bar (fills downward from the top of the sidechain section, or overlaid on the main VU) that tracks `amount × env` in real time. Only visible when a sidechain source is active. Requires an atomic float per channel written by `MixerEngine::processBlock` (block-peak of the gain reduction amount) and read by the UI timer at 30 Hz. Fixed: `MixerEngine` writes `sidechainGR[r]` atomics each block; new `GRMeter` component (downward-filling, semi-transparent blue-grey) placed between fader and VU in rhythm channel strips; `bindRhythm` accepts optional `grAtomic` pointer to wire the meter. | ✅ Closed | 189 |

| 121 | Volume / gain staging deep dive — overall rhythm output levels may be unsuitable for practical use. Need to measure: peak and RMS levels from a single rhythm at full fader with a 0 dBFS sample, after the `kHeadroomTrim` (−6 dB), voice ADSR, and master fader. Check whether summing 8 simultaneous rhythms clips the master bus. Verify the K-14 calibration target (+4 dBVU ≈ −14 dBFS) is reachable without fader riding. Identify where gain should be adjusted (per-voice trim, channel fader default, master fader default) and document the intended gain structure. **Audit:** previous defaults yielded `0.5 (ampLevel) × 0.5 (kHeadroomTrim) × 0.75 (channel) × 0.75 (master)` = **−17 dB peak** for a 0 dBFS sample. K-14 calibrated but far quieter than typical drum plugins (Bitwig channel meter only hit −14 dB). Fix (build 224): raised `VoiceParams::ampLevel` + APVTS `r{N}_ampLvl` default 0.5 → 1.0; raised `ChannelState::level` + APVTS `ch{N}_lvl` default 0.75 → 1.0; raised `MixerEngine::masterLevel` + APVTS `mstr_lvl` default 0.75 → 1.0. Net **+11 dB** for fresh instances. New gain chain: `1.0 × 0.5 × 1.0 × 1.0` = **−6 dB peak** for a 0 dBFS sample, single rhythm — confirmed via Bitwig at −5 dB peak with a normalised kick. The fixed −6 dB `kHeadroomTrim` remains as the only summing safety net (8 fully correlated voices peak at +12 dB worst-case; in practice drums don't peak coherently and headroom is sufficient). | ✅ Closed | 224 |

| 120 | Sidechain ducking — analysis and verification needed. Current DSP: audio-signal envelope follower (not hit-triggered) driven by the source channel's post-fader stereo peak, with per-sample IIR: `env = atk·env + (1−atk)·srcLvl` on attack, `env = rel·env` on release. Gain = `1 − amount × env`. Attack range 1–500 ms, Release 10–2000 ms. Outstanding questions: (1) Is audio-signal drive correct, or should it optionally trigger from the sequencer hit event for tighter ducking? (2) Are the attack/release ranges musically useful — 1 ms attack may be inaudible at low BPM, 2000 ms release very long; consider 1–200 ms / 10–500 ms. (3) Verify the effect is audible end-to-end with a test case (loud source channel → ducked target). | ✅ Closed | 187 |

| 119 | Default preset not loaded on startup — `PluginProcessor` constructor creates a hardcoded default rhythm (16 steps, 4 hits) instead of loading `_default.muclid` from the user content folder. Fix: after constructing the processor, check for `<ContentFolder>/Presets/_default.muclid` and load it silently if present, falling back to the hardcoded default if the file is missing or invalid. | ✅ Closed | 142 |

| 118 | Sample preview when browsing — the file browser has no way to audition a sample before loading it. Need a preview button or auto-preview on selection that plays the file through a temporary `AudioFormatReader` without assigning it to the rhythm slot. Stop playback when a different file is selected or the browser closes. Fixed: replaced native `FileChooser` with a custom `SampleBrowserContent` dialog (`FileBrowserComponent` + `FileBrowserListener`); selecting a file triggers `PluginProcessor::startSamplePreview` which plays via `AudioTransportSource` mixed into the master output at 70% gain; preview stops automatically on dialog close, cancel, or new selection. | ✅ Closed | 181 |

| 117 | Sidechain Amount + Attack "/" + Release "\" controls — Amount knob (full channel width), two half-width knobs side-by-side for attack and release, labeled "/" and "\" to represent the ramp shapes. Placed at the top of each rhythm channel strip above the send knobs. | ✅ Closed | 176 |

| 116 | Sidechain DSP — `MixerEngine` needs a per-channel envelope follower driven by the source channel's post-fader audio, applying multiplicative gain reduction (`amount × env`) to the ducked channel. New `ChannelState` fields: `sidechainSource` (int, −1 = off), `sidechainAmount` (0–1), `sidechainAttackMs`, `sidechainReleaseMs`. | ✅ Closed | 176 |

| 115 | Sidechain input selector per mixer channel — each rhythm channel strip needs a compact dropdown listing "None" and the other active channels by name (or number if unnamed), allowing the user to route any channel as a sidechain trigger source. | ✅ Closed | 176 |

| 114 | Meter mode selector — all VU meters in the mixer showed the same Peak-style ballistics with no way to switch. Fix: added `MeterMode` enum (Peak / VU / K-12 / K-14) to `VUMeter`; Peak = current instant-attack + peak-hold behaviour; VU/K modes use a 300 ms symmetric IIR ballistic (α ≈ 0.895 at 30 Hz); K-12 and K-14 shift the reference mark and colour-zone boundaries to −12 dBFS and −14 dBFS respectively (green→yellow at the K reference, yellow→red +4 dB above it). A `SegmentControl` "Peak \| VU \| K-12 \| K-14" is placed in a 22 px header strip above the mixer channel strips and propagates the mode to every channel + return + master VU meter. | ✅ Closed | 172 |

| 113 | Rhythm preset button cryptically labelled "R.Pst" with no save option — users had no way to save a rhythm preset from the UI, and the load button label was unclear. Fix: replaced `loadPresetBtn { "R.Pst" }` with `loadRhythmBtn { "Load" }` and `saveRhythmBtn { "Save" }` in the rhythm panel header; implemented `RhythmPanel::saveRhythmPreset()` using a `juce::FileChooser` in save mode, calling the new `PluginProcessor::saveRhythmPresetToFile(index, file)` method. Labels now match the global preset Save/Load style. | ✅ Closed | 171 |

| 112 | Sample name blank or wrong in rhythm panel — the panel stored sample names in a local `std::map<int,String> loadedSampleNames` that was only populated when the user loaded a file in the current UI session; after preset load, session restore, or DAW project reload, the map was empty and the bar showed "drop sample here" despite audio playing. Fix: removed the local map; `paint()` now calls `proc.getSampleName(rhythmIndex)` which reads from `PluginProcessor::loadedSamplePaths` (the canonical per-slot array kept in sync by all load paths). | ✅ Closed | 171 |

| 111 | Delay→reverb and Effect→reverb intra-FX sends not audible — `doReverb` was computed from `reverbSendBuf` signal *before* `processSends()`, so when only intra-FX routing (not direct channel sends) fed the reverb, `doReverb` was false and `reverb.processReturn` was never called. `MixerEngine` also gated the reverb return mix on the stale `doReverb` flag. Fix: `FXChain::processSends` now computes `reverbNeeded = doReverb \|\| (doDelay && delToReverb > 0.001f) \|\| (doEffect && effToReverb > 0.001f)`; `MixerEngine` re-checks `hasSignal(reverbSendBuf)` after `processSends` for the mix decision. | ✅ Closed | 171 |

| 110 | Modulators have no uni/bipolar toggle — `ControlSequence::Polarity` enum (`Unipolar`/`Bipolar`) existed in the data layer and was applied in `ControlSequence::evaluate()`, but was never exposed in the UI. Fix: added `SegmentControl polarityCtrl { {"Uni","Bi"} }` to `ModulatorEditor` header row (alongside Smooth/Stepped and Internal/CC), wired to `cs->polarity` in `wireHeader()` and loaded in `loadFromCS()`. | ✅ Closed | 171 |

| 109 | Modulation depth for bitcrusher rate felt inconsistent with the knob — linear mod-depth normalization meant equal depth amounts had different perceptual effects at different rate values. Fix: updated the mod-matrix normalization for `insert.rate` to use log mapping (`log(driveRate/100) / log(48000/100) × 100`) in both the pre-mod write and post-mod read paths, matching the knob's log curve. | ✅ Closed | 171 |

| 108 | Bitcrusher rate knob is linear — the sweet spot is 700–7000 Hz but this occupies only a small portion of the 100–48000 Hz linear range, making fine control impossible. Fix: `setSkewFactorFromMidPoint(2190.0)` (geometric mean of the range) on the Rate slider gives logarithmic feel with the sweet spot spanning ~33%–68% of knob travel. | ✅ Closed | 171 |

| 107 | About panel license list incorrect — SoundTouch listed but never compiled in (no source references outside AboutPanel.cpp); Monocypher (BSD-2-Clause, compiled in `LicenseChecker.cpp`) and clap-juce-extensions (MIT, compiled for CLAP format) were missing. Fix: removed SoundTouch, added Monocypher and clap-juce-extensions; also corrected Björklund to use proper UTF-8 `ö` character. | ✅ Closed | 171 |

| 106 | Plugin has no custom icon — standalone exe, VST3 bundle, and installer all used the default JUCE icon. Fix: added `resources/Icon.png` (and multi-size `.ico` files) to `juce_add_plugin` via `ICON_BIG`/`ICON_SMALL`; added `SetupIconFile` to the Inno Setup script. JUCE's `juceaide` generates `icon.ico` at configure time from the PNG. | ✅ Closed | 168 |

| 105 | No Release build deployed for beta testers — only Debug builds were being copied to the OneDrive distribution folder. Fix: added `cmake/DeployRelease.cmake` (skips non-Release configs) and a `cmake -P` POST_BUILD command on `mu-clid_Standalone` that deploys VST3 + CLAP + Standalone to `TDP/Windows/` on Release builds only. | ✅ Closed | 167 |

| 104 | Beta tester gets `msvcrtdxxx.dll` / `vcruntime140d.dll` error on launch — Debug CRT DLLs are not redistributable; Release CRT requires the VC++ Redistributable. Fix: `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY "MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>"` in CMakeLists.txt embeds the VC++ runtime statically in all build configurations, eliminating the dependency entirely. | ✅ Closed | 167 |

| 103 | `loadPreset` (new `.muclid` format) missing `apvtsLoading` guard — the new-format path in `loadPreset` calls `param->setValueNotifyingHost(...)` for 60+ parameters without setting `apvtsLoading = true`. Each call fired `parameterChanged → syncRhythmParam → voiceEngines[ri]->setParams + sequencer.updatePattern`, causing ~60×n redundant engine updates. The old-format fallback (`restoreStateFromTree`) correctly uses `apvtsLoading`. Fix: set `apvtsLoading = true` before the parameter loop and `false` after, relying on the existing explicit `sequencer.updatePattern(i)` + `voiceEngines[i]->setParams()` calls at the end of each rhythm block. | ✅ Closed | 164 |

| 102 | Audio-thread race in `removeRhythm` — `PluginProcessor::removeRhythm` decrements `numActiveRhythms` before calling `sequencer.removeRhythm(index)`, but does not call `suspendProcessing`. A currently-executing `processBlock` that snapshotted the old count at block start can call `sequencer.getRhythm(r)` on the `rhythms` vector while the message thread is erasing and shifting elements (C++ UB, potential crash). Fix: wrapped structural changes in `suspendProcessing(true/false)`, matching the pattern used in `swapRhythms`. Also added `rhythms.reserve(MaxRhythms)` in `SequencerEngine` constructor as belt-and-suspenders to prevent reallocation during `addRhythm`. | ✅ Closed | 164 |

| 101 | Mixer/Sequencer toggle label fails to update — `hideAllOverlays()` set `mixerVisible = false` but never called `transportBar.setMixerActive(false)`. Fix: added `setMixerActive(false)` to `hideAllOverlays()`. | ✅ Closed | 162 |

| 100 | Sidebar click/drag while mixer is open jumps back to sequencer — `onRhythmSelected` and `onRhythmsReordered` both called `hideAllOverlays()` unconditionally. Fix: `onRhythmSelected` only calls `hideAllOverlays()` when `!mixerVisible`; `onRhythmsReordered` never calls `hideAllOverlays()`, refreshes mixer or rhythm panel based on current view. | ✅ Closed | 162 |

| 98 | `kEditorH` reduced 140 → 100 in `ModulatorEditor.h` (sibling of #309). Root cause of the original layout break: `topH = contentH × 0.55` consumed too much space, leaving ModulatorEditor only ~141 px when it needs ≥228 px (header+editor+timing+addBtn). Reducing the editor height contribution is half of the fix. | ✅ Closed | 160 |

| 97 | Hot-swap a rhythm while it is playing — when a rhythm preset is loaded into a slot that is currently playing, the old rhythm should continue uninterrupted; the new rhythm waits in a "pending" state. A swap button (play/swap icon) appears in the rhythm panel top bar to signal a pending swap is ready. When the user clicks it, the swap is scheduled to take effect at the next loop boundary according to a new Settings overlay option: **"Swap on main loop"** (waits for the master loop to wrap) or **"Swap on rhythm loop"** (waits for the individual rhythm's own step counter to wrap). Infrastructure: per-slot `hasPendingSwap[MaxRhythms]` atomic bool; `swapRequested[MaxRhythms]` flag set by UI; `pendingRhythmData[MaxRhythms]` holding the staged Rhythm struct; swap-mode setting persisted in `PropertiesFile`; loop-point detection in `SequencerEngine::processBlock` (rhythm wrap flag and master-loop reset event); thread-safe swap execution (copy pending data and update pattern under `patternLock` at loop boundary); UI: swap button in `RhythmPanel` top bar, visible only when a pending swap exists; per-channel fade-out/fade-in on swap (optional polish). CLAUDE.md notes: "Atomic pointer for rhythm hot-swap from day one — required for v2 live swap feature." | ✅ Closed | 165 |

| 96 | Drag-to-reorder rhythms in the sidebar — direct mouse-tracking drag on `SidebarItem` forwarded to `RhythmSidebar`; adjacent-swap chain via `PluginProcessor::swapRhythms(i,j)` (suspendProcessing + sequencer patternLock); swaps voiceEngines, midiEngines, mixerEngine.channels, loadedSamplePaths, and APVTS rN_*/chN_* params. Selection tracks the dragged rhythm through the chain. Ghost snapshot and insertion line drawn via `paintOverChildren`. | ✅ Closed | 161 |

| 95 | `loadSampleForRhythm` bounds-checked against `voiceEngines.size()` which is always `MaxRhythms` (8) (sibling of #310). Invalid indices 2–7 would pass the guard when only 1 rhythm is active, then dereference a null `unique_ptr`. Fixed by checking against `numActiveRhythms.load()` instead. Found in the post-#94 audit. | ✅ Closed | 149 |

| 94 | Delete rhythm causes abort() crash — the audio thread captures `numRhythms` at the start of `processBlock` and then accesses `voiceEngines[r]` by index; if the message thread calls `removeRhythm()` between those two operations, `voiceEngines` is erased to a smaller size and the audio-thread index is out of bounds (MSVC debug iterator check calls `abort()`). Exposed by the #76 vector refactor (was `std::array` before). Fix: convert `voiceEngines` and `midiEngines` to `std::array<…, MaxRhythms>` (same pattern as #93), add `std::atomic<int> numActiveRhythms` updated atomically before any slot shift, and have `processBlock` read the atomic rather than `sequencer.getNumRhythms()`. | ✅ Closed | 148 |

| 93 | SequencerEngine race on rhythm removal during playback — `removeRhythm()` erases from `safePatterns`, `safeCPatterns`, and `lastStepIndex` vectors under `patternLock`, but the audio thread reads those vectors after releasing `patternLock` using a `numRhythms` count snapshotted before the lock. If removal races with the audio iteration loop, the iterator accesses past the shrunken vector end (UB / crash). Was safe with `std::array` (fixed size); exposed by the #76 vector refactor. Fix: revert `safePatterns`, `safeCPatterns`, and `lastStepIndex` to `std::array<…, MaxRhythms>` (audio-thread-only, never resizes) while keeping the message-thread vectors (`rhythms`, `cachedPatterns`, `cachedCPatterns`, `patternUpdated`) as `std::vector`. | ✅ Closed | 146 |

| 92 | Buffer overrun in ReverbSlot — `wetL`/`wetR` scratch buffers are sized to `blockSize` in `prepare()`, but `process()` and `processReturn()` indexed them with `buffer.getNumSamples()` (no guard). A host that calls with a larger-than-promised block size would write past the end. Fixed by clamping `numSamples` to `wetL.size()` at the top of each function. | ✅ Closed | 145 |

| 91 | Redundant `std::exp` per channel per block in Insert and Tone filter sections — `OnePoleLP::prepare()` (which computes `exp(−2π·fc/sr)`) was called inside `for (int ch = 0; ch < nCh; ++ch)` in both the bitcrusher anti-alias filter and the post-drive tone filter, computing identical results twice per block. Fixed by hoisting the prepare calls above the channel loop. | ✅ Closed | 145 |

| 90 | Audio-thread data race in bitcrusher TPDF dither — `VoiceEngine::process()` called `juce::Random::getSystemRandom()` on the audio thread; this is a shared singleton and concurrent calls from multiple VoiceEngine instances race. Fixed by replacing with a per-instance `juce::Random rng` member. | ✅ Closed | 145 |

| 76 | Rhythms fixed-size array → dynamic list — `SequencerEngine` stores rhythms as `std::array<Rhythm, 8>` with a `numRhythms` counter, essentially a manual vector. `PluginProcessor` mirrors this with `std::array<VoiceEngine, 8>` (non-copyable, needs `unique_ptr` to move to a vector). APVTS pre-registers all 8 slots regardless so that's not the bottleneck. Main benefit: allows >8 rhythms in the future. Complexity: medium — mechanical but VoiceEngine's non-copyability means `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<VoiceEngine>>` and accessor changes throughout. Not Opus-level; straightforward refactor once the preset system (#68) is in place so we know how state will serialise. | ✅ Closed | 143 |

| 50 | Audio-thread safety: `SequencerEngine::cachedPatterns`/`cachedCPatterns` read in audio thread without lock — `processBlock` reads `cachedPatterns[r]` (a `std::vector<bool>`) while `updatePattern()` on the message thread can reassign it. The reallocation could leave the audio thread reading freed memory. Pre-existing design. Fix options: (a) double/triple-buffer the cached patterns with atomic index swap; (b) protect with the `modLock` spinlock; (c) use a lock-free SPSC queue to publish updated patterns to the audio thread | ✅ Closed | 138 |

| 49 | Audio-thread safety: `Rhythm::operator=` is not lock-aware — `RhythmPanel::confirmReset` does `r = Rhythm{}` which replaces `controlSequences` (`std::vector<ControlSequence>`) and `modulationMatrix` non-atomically while the audio thread may be reading them. The `modLock` spinlock guards modulation matrix reads in `processBlock` but the assignment bypasses it. Same exposure on `addRhythm`. Practical risk: brief audible artefact (not crash) during reset. Fix options: (a) acquire `modLock` around the assignment in `confirmReset`/`addRhythm`; (b) make `Rhythm::operator=` itself lock-aware so any caller is safe | ✅ Closed | 138 |
